title: Industrial Outdoor Storage Zoning and Truck Parking Permits
description: Check whether a parcel can be used as a truck or trailer yard. See how Fontana approved a 250-space layout and which records establish operating rights.
coverAlt: Aerial view of the industrial area around 9910 Almond Avenue, Fontana, with the 9.5-acre project parcel outlined in gold.
coverCaption: Parcel 0234-061-04 at 9910 Almond Avenue in Fontana. The outline shows the city’s parcel boundary. Aerial imagery from USGS and USDA NAIP.
intro: Before buying or leasing an industrial outdoor storage yard, verify which activities the local code allows on the parcel and which ones the permit covers. Fontana’s Planning Commission approved a 250-space registered vehicle storage project on land its staff already described as truck parking. The approval set a cap, restricted other activities and required the city to accept the completed work before the new use could begin.
takeaways: Describe the operation before checking zoning. A fleet yard, a warehouse’s accessory trailer parking and a paid public truck lot can fall under different use categories.
Match the parcel ID, zoning district, specific plan and dated decision. A land-use label and a permit record answer different questions.
Keep the approved stall count, completed stalls and spaces reserved for your tenant as separate numbers.

guideActions.label: Look up a parcel with Invariant Earth

sections.heading: How to check zoning for a truck or trailer yard

blocks.text: Start with the lot and the activity you would put in the lease. Specify whether you will park tractors, store detached trailers, transfer loads, run repairs, store equipment, or let drivers stay on site. Include the hours, estimated trips, equipment dimensions and whether the yard serves a business on the same property. Use those facts to find the local use category.

rows: Parcel map and zoning layer
The lot boundary and mapped zoning. Check every lot in the lease or option.
Check any overlay or specific plan and the edition of the applicable use table.
Local use table and adopted amendments
Whether the exact operation is allowed by right, as an accessory use, or with a separate decision.
Confirm whether any accessory parking depends on a principal use that your tenant will actually operate.
Decision, conditions and approved site plan
The authorized activities, layout and restrictions for the project.
Confirm expiration, extensions, appeals, amendments and whether the proposed operator can use the approval.
Building and inspection records
Whether improvements received permits and required final city acceptance.
Confirm open and reserved stalls with the operator and walk the truck route from the street to the farthest usable row.

sections.heading: What Fontana approved at 9910 Almond Avenue

blocks.text: Fontana’s parcel layer returns assessor parcel number 0234-061-04 at 9910 Almond Avenue. A point inside the parcel returns SP, the city map’s specific-plan designation. The staff report identifies the Speedway Industrial District within the Southwest Industrial Park Specific Plan. It also identifies the proposed use as registered vehicle storage, which required a conditional use permit. Use the case number and parcel ID when searching for the drawings. The first site-plan sheet carries 9882 Almond Avenue in its title block, while the case, conditions and parcel layer use 9910.

rows: September 15, 2026
The Planning Commission voted 5–0 to adopt PC 2026-032, approve Conditional Use Permit 25-0015 and approve Administrative Site Plan 25-0020.
Approved layout and cap

The staff report describes approximately 9.5 acres, 250 truck spaces, 39 passenger-vehicle spaces and a 1,558-square-foot office. Exhibit A limits registered vehicle storage to 250 vehicles in marked stalls.
September 18, 2026
The state posted the project’s CEQA Notice of Determination following the city approval.
Before use can begin
The permit conditions require the city to accept completed improvements through a certificate of occupancy or equivalent final documentation, along with fulfillment of the other conditions.

blocks.text: Exhibit A bars storage in drive aisles and fire lanes and requires trucks to queue off the public right-of-way. Stored vehicles must remain registered and operable. The conditions also bar using vehicles to store materials and prohibit fuel sales and repair facilities. Ask for the stamped plan and the latest acceptance record before treating the approved 250 spaces as rentable capacity. Our review verified the approval and conditions. The completion and availability of the spaces remain unverified.

blocks.label: Download the permit records, parcel shape and replay queries

sections.heading: Why another truck yard can have different rights

blocks.text: On November 17, 2026, Fontana’s Planning Commission adopted the item for a different registered vehicle storage project at 13929 Santa Ana Avenue. That case expressly included incidental truck maintenance and a proposed consolidation of three existing parcels. The staff report identifies the Slover West Manufacturing District in the same Southwest Industrial Park Specific Plan. California posted the project’s Notice of Exemption on November 20.

When screening a list of parcels, save the actual uses and restrictions from each dated case. A search for ‘truck storage’ would surface both sites. The right to maintain vehicles, the need for a parcel consolidation, and the conditions for opening belong to the individual approvals.

sections.heading: How to screen a portfolio of outdoor storage sites

blocks.text: Use addresses and parcel boundaries to map each candidate to the planning authority. Add mapped zoning and overlays, building and driveway geometry, and the latest case references. Keep the date each decision was adopted, the date it was filed and the date you checked the record. On the shortlist, verify the exact use and count usable stalls from the stamped plan. Measure trailer swing and queuing with the largest vehicle you expect on site.

Invariant Earth’s parcel lookup is a starting point for matching a site to its boundary. Use the same parcel IDs to compare site context and to retrieve local conditions and issued permits for the proposed operation.

items.label: Compare mapped zoning and allowed-use fields
Measure usable trailer parking
Verify the acreage and parcel rights before making an offer

faqs.question: Does industrial zoning allow outdoor truck or trailer storage?
faqs.answer: Check the exact use in the applicable local use table and any specific plan or overlay. A warehouse’s accessory parking and a stand-alone storage yard can need different approvals. Fontana’s 9910 Almond Avenue case required a conditional use permit for registered vehicle storage.

faqs.question: How many truck spaces did Fontana approve at 9910 Almond Avenue?
faqs.answer: The approved case shows 250 truck spaces and 39 passenger-vehicle spaces. The permit caps storage at 250 registered vehicles in marked stalls and requires city acceptance of improvements before the authorized use can begin.

faqs.question: Can an industrial outdoor storage tenant repair trucks on site?
faqs.answer: Check the site’s approved operations and conditions. Fontana’s Almond Avenue conditions prohibit repair facilities. A separate Santa Ana Avenue case explicitly included incidental truck maintenance.

title: How to Estimate a Manufacturing Labor Shed for Site Selection
description: Use Census commuting data, occupation wages, and drive times to screen a factory or warehouse location. Reproduce the Dayton metro example.
coverAlt: Census 2024 primary jobs with workplaces in the Dayton metro by home location. There were 230,406 inside the metro and 116,658 outside it, or 33.6 percent outside.
coverCaption: 2024 Census LODES 8.5 primary jobs, workplace counties Greene, Miami and Montgomery. Home locations are from the published aggregate records.
intro: A manufacturing labor shed is the area a plant can reasonably recruit from. Start with where workers in the area live, use the plant’s employee entrance and shift times to test the commute, then compare wages by occupation. In Dayton, 33.6% of primary jobs in the three-county metro were linked to homes outside it in the Census Bureau’s 2024 data. A county or metro boundary can leave out places worth recruiting from.
takeaways: Use work-to-home Census records to identify where existing workers live. Measure travel to the proposed entrance at each shift start.
Use home-based manufacturing employment to identify areas with industry experience, and occupation wage estimates to benchmark each role.
Verify shift-level hiring with competing employers, job postings, training providers and local recruiters before relying on a recruitment target.

guideActions.label: Compare labor force by drive time

sections.heading: How do you estimate a plant’s labor shed?

blocks.text: Build the hiring plan first. Record the number of people needed by job, shift and start date. Keep construction trades separate from the people who will operate the facility. Match each permanent role to a Standard Occupational Classification code so you can compare wages and existing jobs across markets.

rows: Where do people who work near this site live?
Census OnTheMap or LODES origin-destination files for an existing industrial corridor or a comparable group of workplaces.
Workplace boundary, reference year and primary jobs by home area.
Who can reach the proposed site?
Drive times toward the employee entrance at each shift start. Use ACS civilian labor force and employed resident counts for context.
Entrance coordinate, inbound trip times, traffic assumptions, assumed travel mode and geographic coverage.
What would it cost to recruit the required roles?
BLS occupation wages, recent postings for comparable jobs, local recruiting quotes and competing shift premiums.
Role and skill requirements, wage definition, shift differential and data vintage.
How many can we hire by opening?
Interviews with staffing and training partners and a hiring test for the proposed duties, pay and schedule.
Expected qualified applicants, acceptances and training completions by date.

blocks.text: For a first pass, run Invariant Earth’s labor shed API from each candidate entrance at 15, 30 and 45 minutes. The result sums ACS labor-force estimates for included tracts and reports population separately. It uses tract representative points and typical travel conditions. Before committing to a site, test inbound routes at the actual shift change, especially across bridges, grade crossings and restricted entrances.

sections.heading: What does the Dayton manufacturing labor market look like?

blocks.text: Using the May 2025 BLS metro definition, we selected workplaces in Greene, Miami and Montgomery counties. In the 2024 Census primary-job files, those counties account for 347,064 primary jobs. Of those, 230,406 are linked to homes in the same three counties, and 116,658 to homes outside them. Warren County accounts for 18,200 and Clark County for 13,233 of the outside-metro job links.

The outside-metro count is 33.6% of the workplace total, including 6,789 job links to homes outside Ohio. Census describes LODES home patterns as partially synthetic. These are job links between recorded home and work areas. The records contain no trip frequency, travel mode or shift time. The Census release also identifies missing data for Alaska and Michigan workers.

The separate home-based file counts 42,760 primary jobs in manufacturing held by residents of the three counties. That figure includes people whose jobs may be outside the metro. It measures the employer’s industry, including roles such as accounting, maintenance and production. The BLS occupation estimates below cover the entire metro and all industries.

rows: Industrial engineers · 17-2112
Industrial machinery mechanics · 49-9041
Machinists · 51-4041
Welders, cutters, solderers, and brazers · 51-4121

blocks.text: The May 2025 estimate for machinists was 1,360 jobs with a median wage of $28.39 an hour. Its location quotient of 1.97 means machinists accounted for nearly twice the share of local jobs that they did nationally. It helps identify an established occupation to investigate. Recruiting feasibility still depends on the required skills, the work schedule and the offer.

To reproduce the count, filter both Ohio origin-destination files to the three workplace county FIPS codes, then group S000 by the first five digits of the home block code. The main file covers homes in Ohio and the auxiliary file covers homes outside Ohio. Use the residence file separately for the industry counts. The download includes the Census checksums and twelve BLS series IDs.

Download counts, occupation estimates and exact source queries

sections.heading: What does a 40-minute commute measure in an Ohio site screen?

blocks.text: Ohio DOT and JobsOhio screened 78 priority development sites. Ohio DOT classified 24 as high readiness, 38 as medium and 16 as low. The overall score uses labor access alongside utility infrastructure, transportation proximity, environmental conditions and site readiness. Ohio DOT notes that a site can have high overall readiness with low workforce access.

rows: Figure 2.87 shows workers within a 40-minute drive under congested conditions, alongside site readiness classes.
Compare geographic reach using the same time threshold and traffic assumptions.
Projected workers within a 40-minute congested drive enter the readiness score.
Screen a planned opening year with a dated estimate for population and network conditions.
Figure 2.75 maps the risk that congestion will reduce access to workers. The report flags segments around Columbus’s I-270 and Cincinnati’s I-275.
Identify routes that merit a traffic sensitivity check. Ask for a current inbound route test to the gate.

blocks.text: For two candidate sites, hold the workforce vintage and 40-minute cutoff fixed while you change the traffic assumptions. Run the inbound trip to the employee gate at each planned shift start. Then compare occupation counts and wages on the same geography. The statewide score and maps do not supply a count of workers who meet a plant’s skill or shift requirements.

sections.heading: Which labor market data tools should site selectors compare?

blocks.text: Give providers the same site entrance, shift window and list of occupations. Ask for the source year, geography, work or home basis and the occupations that enter each count. Ask each provider to reproduce the Dayton baseline, then show what their tool adds when the analysis moves down to a parcel.

rows: Invariant Earth
Screen drive-time labor force at the employee entrance alongside parcel, access and infrastructure checks.
Can the same candidate entrance and travel limits be reused across the site screen, and which tracts were missed or approximated?
Census OnTheMap / LODES
Find where workers live and work from published job links.
Does the workplace total include home blocks outside the state? Which release and job type were used?
BLS OEWS
Benchmark jobs, wages and occupation concentration for a metro.
Can we reproduce the role, median, year and geography without applying industry labels to occupation counts?
Lightcast
Compare labor markets, employer demand and skills in postings.
How did the provider map CNC experience to the role, and how are duplicate postings handled?
Chmura JobsEQ
Compare regional workforce, job posts, wages and recruitment areas.
Which figures are local observations and which are modeled? Can we change the catchment without changing the unit?
ArcGIS Business Analyst
Create road-based catchments and add demographic and socioeconomic data.
Does the estimate use trips toward the entrance, and how does the provider allocate a partially covered Census area?

faqs.question: What is the difference between a labor shed and a drive-time area?
faqs.answer: A labor shed describes where a site can recruit workers. A drive-time area estimates geographic reach under stated road and traffic assumptions. Use existing commuting patterns, occupation and wage data, and local hiring evidence to turn that boundary into a recruiting assessment.

faqs.question: Can you count machinists within a 30-minute drive using Census LODES?
faqs.answer: LODES measures employment and residence geography. The combined goods-producing field in the origin-destination file includes multiple industries, and the file has no detailed occupation field. Use a separate occupational source and ask how it estimates worker residence at the scale you need.

faqs.question: Is a manufacturing job count the same thing as available workers?
faqs.answer: Manufacturing employment measures covered jobs at manufacturers. It includes many occupations and cannot show who is willing to change jobs. Test the actual offer, shift and start date with local recruiters and training providers.

title: How to Estimate EV Charging Electricity Costs and Demand Charges
description: Estimate a fleet depot or fast charging station’s electricity bill from 15-minute loads. Replay four scenarios using PG&E’s business EV tariff.
coverAlt: Under PG&E’s March 2026 BEV-2-S rate, a modeled 36,000 kWh costs $14,458.44 with concurrent evening charging, $13,885.08 with a lower evening peak, and $5,371.08 with a lower midday peak.
coverCaption: Modeled April 2026 charges under PG&E Schedule BEV-2-S. Every scenario uses 36,000 metered kWh.
intro: To estimate the electricity bill for a fleet depot or fast charging station, use the rate available at the proposed meter and a 15-minute estimate of what the site will draw. Price the energy by time of day and calculate the charge tied to peak demand separately. In a PG&E example, halving the peak draw saved $573.36 for the month. Moving the same charging to midday saved another $8,514.00. The savings depend on when vehicles are actually available to charge.
takeaways: Use power at the utility meter in kilowatts (kW) and energy in kilowatt-hours (kWh). A charger’s advertised output to the vehicle measures a different part of the system.
Ask the serving utility which rates, meter configurations and service voltages it will offer at the parcel before underwriting the site.
Replay the same loads under each eligible tariff and check both an ordinary month and the busiest month you expect.

guideActions.label: Check the serving utility for a charging site

sections.heading: How do you estimate a commercial EV charging bill?

blocks.text: Start with the number of vehicles, when they arrive, when they must leave and how much energy each needs. Turn that schedule into intervals of power drawn at the utility meter, including charger losses and loads served by that meter. For a fast charging station, use expected session arrivals and duration and test a busy period with several sessions overlapping.

rows: Energy
Multiply each interval’s metered kWh by the applicable rate for that time of day. Sum the interval charges.
Demand or subscription
Apply the tariff to the metered peak or subscribed kW. Check the measurement interval, demand windows, minimums and whether prior peaks carry into later months.
Other bill items
Use the actual rate terms for fixed charges, riders, taxes and credits. Confirm whether your energy supplier and your delivery utility bill separately.
Connection and site costs
Carry the utility upgrade, meter and customer-side work, charger costs, rent and maintenance in the broader site model.

blocks.text: At a candidate address, identify the serving utility and request the applicable rate code, delivery voltage, metering arrangement and expected service date. Ask whether the charging load can be metered on its own and which fees apply to that account. A published rate helps price the load after the utility confirms eligibility and the service it can deliver.

sections.heading: What would a 600 kW charging depot pay under PG&E’s business EV rate?

blocks.text: This example uses a dedicated EV meter on PG&E’s bundled secondary-voltage BEV-2-S rate for April 2026, outside the subscription grace period. Each scenario uses 1,200 metered kWh a day for 30 days. The model assumes vehicles are available for the entire charging window. The meter draws a constant 600 kW for two hours or 300 kW for four hours.

The March 2026 sheet lists $95.56 per 50 kW subscription block and $3.82 per excess kW. Energy costs $0.36977 per kWh from 4 p.m. to 9 p.m. and $0.13327 per kWh from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. PG&E lists $0.15654 per kWh for the remaining hours. These windows apply every day under this schedule.

columns: April scenario and local charging time
rows: Concurrent evening charging · 4–6 p.m.
Managed evening charging · 4–8 p.m.
Managed midday charging · 9 a.m.–1 p.m.
Concurrent charging with a 300 kW subscription · 4–6 p.m.

blocks.text: Spreading the evening load keeps all usage in the same energy band and saves six subscription blocks, or $573.36. Moving that 300 kW schedule to midday cuts the energy charge by $8,514.00. The final row shows the exposure when the subscribed demand stays at 300 kW but the meter still reaches 600 kW. That adds $1,146.00 in overage for the billing period.

Under this tariff, the overage uses the highest 15-minute average in the billing period. It is assessed once per period, even when multiple intervals exceed the subscription. For the example, multiply the 300 kW excess by the filed $3.82 per kW. The subtotal excludes taxes, account-specific credits and the cost of building or operating the site.

Download the tariff inputs and modeled monthly totals

sections.heading: Which tools can compare EV electricity rates for a proposed site?

blocks.text: Give each provider the same address, rate version, service voltage, meter arrangement and interval file. Ask for the billed peak, energy by time band, the subscribed kW, the overage and the source sheet for each charge. Use a recent bill from the same account to check the result when one is available.

columns: What to verify in a trial
rows: Invariant Earth
Screen the property and bring the serving utility, access and site context into the same diligence file.
Confirm the parcel match, service availability and evidence date. Then use the eligible tariff and metered profile to price the load.
Utility tariff and account team
Confirm rate eligibility and the terms and timing for serving the proposed load.
Request the written service and meter assumptions and the filed schedule for the expected service date.
OpenEI Utility Rate Database
Find structured energy and demand rates as inputs for a tariff screen.
Check the effective date and representation of subscription and overage against the sheet.
Arcadia Signal
Look up tariff versions and model itemized electricity costs.
Ask whether the specific tariff version can price the subscription and monthly overage in the replay.
NLR EVI-FAST
Compare charging project economics, with electricity and demand costs as inputs.
Trace the electricity input to the verified site tariff. Add utilization, charging revenue, installation and financing assumptions.

blocks.text: Run the comparison again with your busiest operating day, a cold-weather charging assumption and a service or charging interruption. A lower subscription works only when the fleet can reliably stay within the planned peak or the expected overages fit the budget. A public fast charging operator also has to account for lost sales or queues when the load cap slows service.

faqs.question: Do all commercial EV rates have a demand charge?
faqs.answer: No. The rate varies by utility and schedule. PG&E’s BEV-2-S model uses a kW subscription plus an overage. Check the applicable tariff for fixed charges, demand charges, subscription terms and any temporary exclusions.

faqs.question: Can you estimate the bill from a charger’s kW rating?
faqs.answer: The rating helps bound what one charger can deliver to a vehicle. To estimate utility charges, model simultaneous sessions and total AC draw at the meter, then price the 15-minute intervals under the applicable tariff.

faqs.question: How much is a 300 kW subscription on PG&E’s BEV-2-S example rate?
faqs.answer: At the rate effective March 1, 2026, six 50 kW blocks cost $573.36 per billing period. Time-of-use energy charges and any overage are separate.

title: How to Find Commercial Foreclosure Records by Address
description: Find a commercial foreclosure by address, parcel and case number. Follow the 20 Times Square leasehold auction through court, ACRIS and SEC records.
coverAlt: For the 20 Times Square leasehold, the court records a $50 million credit bid at the January 2022 auction and a $857.4 million court valuation as of the auction date.
coverCaption: Natixis v. 20 TSQ Lessee LLC, New York County index 850272/2019. The 2024 order valued the leasehold as of January 26, 2022.
intro: To check a commercial foreclosure by address, start with the parcel and owner of record, then find the court case or recorded notice for the mortgage in question. Check the notice, the auction result and the conveyance separately. At 20 Times Square, the court records a $50 million credit bid for the leasehold. A separate SEC filing ties the same address to debt secured by the owner’s interest in the land. The two records describe different collateral.
takeaways: In New York, check the county clerk or court record for the notice and the case. Use land records for the recorded instrument and its legal description.
Keep the court index number and the interest at stake, such as fee ownership or a leasehold, with each event.
Label bids, recorder index amounts, court valuations and loan balances by what they measure. An address match alone cannot reconcile those amounts.

sections.heading: Where do you look up a commercial foreclosure by address?

blocks.text: Start with the original parcel record and the property owner or holder of the interest being foreclosed. In New York City, use the borough, block and lot (BBL) for land records. Use the case index number to open the court docket and relevant filings. New York’s public NYSCEF guest search covers cases filed electronically, and the clerk can help locate other records.

rows: A case affects the property
Read the notice of pendency and complaint in the county or court records. Match the property, mortgage recording references and reason the case was filed.
A sale was authorized or scheduled
Check the judgment of foreclosure and sale, the latest notice of sale and any adjournment or stay in the docket.
The auction took place
Check the referee’s report of sale and any order addressing it. Record the actual auction date, buyer or assignee and whether the bid was a credit bid.
A specific interest transferred
Read the executed conveyance and any recorded assignment. Match the legal description, interest conveyed, instrument number, document date and recording date.

blocks.text: A notice of pendency, often called a lis pendens, can arise from other litigation affecting real property. Read the notice and complaint before classifying the event. At 701 Seventh Avenue, a separate order addressed notices tied to mechanics’ liens, even though the same property also appeared in a mortgage foreclosure case.

sections.heading: What did the 20 Times Square foreclosure actually transfer?

blocks.text: The address is 701 Seventh Avenue, Manhattan block 1000, lot 1 (BBL 1010000001). The Supreme Court’s order in index 850272/2019 identifies the foreclosed collateral as the leasehold interest in the building and improvements. The case began on December 9, 2019. The court records a January 26, 2022 auction, a $50 million credit bid and a conveyance of that leasehold to 20 TSQ Property Owner LLC after an assignment of the winning bid.

rows: Court decision, describing the auction and referee report
Credit bid for the leasehold at auction. The court says no other bidder participated.
$56,715,573 · recorded March 16, 2022
NYC ACRIS CRFN 2022000113051, document type ACON
Amount in the record index for an assignment or termination of contract or bid. The selected index fields give no breakdown of the amount.
NYSCEF document 1156, pp. 13–14
Court’s fair and reasonable market value for the leasehold as of the auction date. The court denied the requested deficiency judgment.
$21,582,303.42 · period ended October 13, 2026
UBS 2018-C12, Loan 6, SEC ABS-EE filed November 2
Reported period-end actual loan balance for this securitized asset. The prospectus identifies the underlying collateral as the borrower’s fee interest in the land.

blocks.text: A second ACRIS entry, CRFN 2022000092118, was recorded on March 2, 2022 as a transfer tax return and has an indexed amount of $0. Both city index records have a February 24 document date and name 20 TSQ Property Owner LLC as party two. Keep the city records attached to the parcel and keep the amounts in separate fields. The court’s auction amount comes from the court record.

The Appellate Division marked the appeal from the 2024 order withdrawn on April 23, 2026. The case download records that disposition along with the auction, the two selected ACRIS entries and the dated loan row. Each has its own source and identifier.

blocks.label: Download the court, recorder and SEC record crosswalk

sections.heading: Which foreclosure data sources should a commercial buyer compare?

blocks.text: Use a vendor to find candidate addresses or alerts, then read the public record behind the event. For a multi-market trial, include a court-filed notice, an adjourned auction and a completed conveyance. Ask for the source date, docket or instrument ID and which legal interest each record describes.

rows: Invariant Earth
Resolve the address and parcel and include relevant land, building and hazard context in the collateral file.
Attach the court and recorder evidence to the matched parcel. Preserve the asset interest and source dates.
ATTOM
Review the preforeclosure endpoints and expanded history for address-linked default and auction entries.
Check commercial coverage in each county and ask whether the output preserves the original instrument and case identifiers.
PropertyRadar
Try the commercial property and foreclosure stage criteria for screening.
Check the local definition of each stage and when a cancellation, sale or later filing changes the flag.
PropertyShark
Use the New York auction and preforeclosure listings to find local cases.
Confirm that the most recent public notice and any adjournment cover the exact asset in the listing.
BlockLot
Review the recorded sale history and foreclosure-sale labels for a New York City lot.
Ask whether the relevant event is a recorded conveyance or a court-only notice. Test a leasehold sale with an assignment code.
TreppWatch and SEC EDGAR
Trace securitized loans and their reported collateral and balances.
Keep the trust, loan ID and reporting period. Check whether the source covers a loan in the fee interest, a leasehold loan or another part of the capital structure.

title: How to Find Truck Traffic Counts by Address
description: Find daily truck traffic on a road segment and compare AADT with annual average daily truck traffic. Reproduce a six-segment Minnesota test and compare traffic data APIs.
coverAlt: Minnesota DOT reports 1,652 heavy commercial vehicles per day on 85th Avenue North west of Zane Avenue, and 426 east of Zane Avenue, for 2025.
coverCaption: MnDOT 2025 Heavy Commercial Annual Average Daily Traffic, locations 42697 and 42698. Both values have source data type E.
intro: To find how many trucks pass an address each day, locate the entrance that trucks will use, then match the road in front of it to a state or local traffic segment. Read the truck volume, vehicle class, year and direction. In Brooklyn Park, Minnesota, MnDOT’s 2025 maps report 1,652 heavy commercial vehicles per day west of Zane Avenue on 85th Avenue North and 426 east of it. Choosing the correct side of the intersection changes the estimate by almost fourfold.
takeaways: Use an annual average truck figure, such as AADTT or Minnesota’s HCAADT, for corridor screening. Check the source’s definition of a truck.
Match the same segment and year before dividing truck traffic by total traffic. One Minnesota pair of current layers showed 2025 truck traffic beside 2019 total traffic.
Request a turning count or gate data when the decision depends on movements into a driveway, a particular shift or actual warehouse arrivals.

guideActions.label: Download the counts and source queries
Check a site’s road and rail access

sections.heading: Where can you look up daily truck traffic near a property?

blocks.text: Start with the driveway or gate, then identify the road segment on the approach to it. A parcel may front several roads, and a nearby freeway can be closer to the parcel than the street trucks actually use. For an industrial lease, use the address and frontage fields in Invariant Earth to narrow the search, then join the approach road to a traffic record from the road authority.

rows: Annual average daily traffic (AADT)
All motor vehicles on a specified road segment. Record the year and whether the value covers one direction or both.
Annual average daily truck traffic (AADTT)
Trucks on the same segment. Check which classes the publisher includes. MnDOT defines heavy commercial traffic as trucks with at least two axles and six tires.
Hourly or turning movement counts
Time of day, direction and maneuvers at a specific intersection or driveway. Ask for the observed dates, vehicle classes and a collection period suited to the decision.

sections.heading: What changes when you pick the correct road segment?

blocks.text: We queried MnDOT’s current all-vehicle and heavy commercial segment layers on November 25, 2026. We joined six records by Location ID and checked that the geometry matched between layers. MnDOT annual averages cover both directions for these road segments. The table keeps each layer’s year and source type code.

rows: 85th Avenue N, west of CSAH 14 (Zane Avenue) · 42697
85th Avenue N, east of CSAH 14 (Zane Avenue) · 42698
I-94, southeast of MN 101 · 10393
Main Street (CSAH 81), south of I-94 · 43026
Rogers Drive, south of Diamond Lake Road · 66417
Industrial Boulevard, southwest of Church Avenue · 42991
Different years

blocks.text: The two Brooklyn Park records share an endpoint at Zane Avenue. Total traffic is 20,014 west of the intersection and 18,396 east of it. The much larger difference in heavy commercial traffic gives estimated truck shares of 8.3% and 2.3%. Keep the actual approach segment in the site record so a reviewer can reproduce the result.

In Rogers, MnDOT reports 13,424 heavy commercial vehicles per day on the selected I-94 segment and 604 on Rogers Drive south of Diamond Lake Road. Both support a regional screening decision. To plan arrival windows or model a proposed loading entrance, collect traffic for the relevant approach, turning movement and hours.

items.label: See a worked turning count and driveway access check

sections.heading: How do you calculate truck share when the years differ?

blocks.text: For Industrial Boulevard, Location ID 42991, the current layers display 14,800 total vehicles per day for 2019 and 863 heavy commercial vehicles per day for 2025. Hold the ratio until you have values for the same year. MnDOT’s historical AADT table has a 2025 entry of 13,204 at that same location. Pairing the two 2025 rows gives 863 divided by 13,204, or 6.54%.

Keep the original method code alongside both numbers. MnDOT’s data products page describes A as count-based, M as modeled and C as factored. The heavy commercial export also returned E for several rows in this example. The download preserves that code as published. Use the agency’s classification records when the decision requires a direct count.

blocks.label: Download the six segment matches, historical rows and source queries

items.label: Annual average daily traffic definition and example

sections.heading: Which truck traffic data API or source fits the job?

blocks.text: Use a traffic authority’s data where it covers your approach road. For a national shortlist, commercial estimates can fill in research on additional roads and dates. Trial each source on the same segment, direction, year and truck class. Ask how it handles a local road without observations.

faqs.question: Can I find truck traffic counts by address?
faqs.answer: Start from the driveway address and identify the road segment trucks use. Check the state or local transportation agency’s truck traffic or vehicle classification layer. Save the segment ID, count year, directions and vehicle classes along with the estimate.

faqs.question: What is the difference between AADT and AADTT?
faqs.answer: AADT describes average daily traffic for the reporting year on a segment. AADTT describes the truck component. Look up the local definition of truck and the time period before calculating truck share.

faqs.question: Can I use a truck traffic count to estimate deliveries to one warehouse?
faqs.answer: Use the road count to understand the corridor. For arrivals to a specific warehouse, request gate records or count truck movements into and out of the entrance in the relevant hours.

faqs.question: Why does a current traffic layer show an older year?
faqs.answer: The current layer can contain the latest value published for that segment in that layer, even when another layer has a different reporting year. For a comparable pair, look up each figure for the same Location ID and year in the historical tables.

title: How to check flood insurance claim history by address
description: Buying a property? Find out which flood records you can request by address, what sellers disclose in NJ, NY and FL, and why public FEMA claims cannot prove a loss at a specific home.
coverAlt: Among 380 public NFIP claim records for Hurricane Ida in two Hudson County ZIP codes, 326 share the same published map point. The shared point covers 259 of 273 rows in ZIP 07030 and 67 of 107 in ZIP 07302.
coverCaption: Invariant analysis of FEMA’s redacted NFIP claims, Hudson County, New Jersey. Loss dates September 1–4, 2021, data as of November 16, 2026.
intro: To check flood insurance claim history before buying a property, start with the seller’s flood disclosure. Ask the seller to request and share any available National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) records and to obtain relevant records from private insurers. FEMA requires appropriate consent for a prospective buyer to obtain prior NFIP claims. You can look up the flood zone and nearby reported losses yourself. Use those public sources to decide what to ask about at the address and which repairs to inspect.
takeaways: Use the applicable disclosure form and ask when the seller took ownership. New Jersey, New York and Florida ask about the seller’s flood insurance claims, and each form has its own scope.
Match any disclosed loss to the insured building, date and cause. Request repair records separately from evidence of a claim payment.
In two Hudson County ZIP codes, 326 of 380 Hurricane Ida claim rows share one public map point. Use these public records to study losses by area.

guideActions.label: Download the FEMA comparison and queries

sections.heading: What flood records can you look up by address?

rows: Effective flood zone
Search FEMA’s Flood Map Service Center by address. Confirm the building’s position on the map and note the panel and effective date.
The flood hazard designation on the effective map. Keep the map date for comparisons with past losses.
The property’s NFIP claim history

Ask the seller to request any available history from FEMA and share it with the necessary consent. Once you own the property, ask FloodSmart about access to records and how to verify ownership and identity.
Which NFIP losses FEMA can disclose for the property. Check the date, insured building and whether the record covers the structure or its contents.
Private flood claims

Ask the seller or authorized broker for records from the carrier and the time each policy was in force. For personal property insurance, the seller can request their own CLUE file and check which losses appear.
Reported losses within the carrier and policy history reviewed. Ask which insurers, policies and dates the report covers.

blocks.text: Ask for the dates the seller owned the property and held each policy. A seller may be able to tell you about water they saw in the building, even when they have no claim record for that event. Ask about the first time water entered, which floors or systems were affected, and what work followed.

sections.heading: What does a seller have to disclose about flood claims?

blocks.text: Read the version of the form that applies to the property and transaction. These three states ask about flood claims alongside separate questions about damage or assistance.

rows: New Jersey
The seller of real property must disclose the required information before the purchaser becomes obligated under a contract.

Section 2(b)(7) asks whether the seller filed a flood insurance claim with any provider, including the NFIP, and the amount received for an approved claim. Section 2(b)(8) asks separately about known flood damage, seepage or pooled water and its frequency.
New York
For covered residential sales, request the signed disclosure before signing the binding sale contract. The law defines the covered property types and exempts certain transfers.

Item 17 of form DOS-1614-f asks about the seller’s flood damage claims and requests an explanation. The nearby questions ask about known federal disaster assistance, current flood insurance and an available elevation certificate.
Florida
For residential real property, the seller must provide the disclosure at or before execution of the sale contract.

Item 1 asks about known damage from flooding during the seller’s ownership. Item 2 asks whether the seller filed a flood insurance claim, including with the NFIP. Item 3 asks about flood damage assistance the seller received.

blocks.text: A seller who reports no flood claims may still disclose past damage. Follow up on both answers. A repair invoice, a dated inspection photo or an earlier disclosure can help establish what happened and whether the cost was paid out of pocket.

sections.heading: Can public FEMA claims identify which properties flooded?

blocks.text: We queried OpenFEMA for Hudson County, New Jersey, and reported ZIP codes 07030 and 07302, using September 1 through September 4, 2021 as loss dates. All 380 returned rows carry the Hurricane Ida event designation NJ0421. We grouped the rows by the latitude and longitude pairs published by FEMA.

columns: Rows at the most common point across both ZIPs
rows: Both ZIPs

blocks.text: FEMA rounds public claim coordinates to one decimal place for privacy and documents that the resulting point may even fall outside the county or state for the claim. Here, the same point represents about 86% of the selected rows and appears under both reported ZIP codes. Use the published geographic fields to summarize area losses. For a specific building, obtain the authorized loss documentation.

The sample counts the rows returned by the redacted NFIP dataset. It describes one event and two reported ZIP codes as of November 16, 2026. The download includes the exact queries and ZIP-level counts so you can reproduce the grouping or check a future revision.

blocks.label: Download the aggregate counts, source queries and form references

sections.heading: Which documents should you request before closing?

blocks.text: For each disclosed loss, ask for the reported cause, date of loss, affected building or unit and the claim determination the seller can share. Request dated photos, repair invoices and any permits or inspection sign-offs. Use the current inspection to check the parts of the building those records describe, including electrical equipment or mechanical rooms that were affected.

For commercial property, request carrier loss runs through the seller or the authorized broker. On a campus or at a shared mailing address, reconcile each loss against the insured building or scheduled location. Check which policy years the reports cover and record any unknown building matches.

Use Invariant Earth to find the flood zone at the address as part of the screening record. Keep a dated reference to the map, then attach the disclosure, authorized claim history and repair evidence as you receive them.

faqs.question: Can a buyer look up prior NFIP claims for an address?
faqs.answer: A prospective buyer needs appropriate consent for FEMA to release prior NFIP claim information. Ask the seller to request their available property history and share it, or ask FloodSmart about the required consent. The public redacted dataset is for geographic analysis.

faqs.question: Can the public FEMA claims API show whether a particular house filed a claim?
faqs.answer: FEMA removes the identifying information used to connect a claim to a house. The public coordinates are rounded. Use the available geographic fields for area research and obtain authorized records for the house.

faqs.question: Does a seller reporting no insurance claims establish that the property never flooded?
faqs.answer: The claim question covers a particular kind of history. Read the separate questions about water damage and assistance and review records from the seller’s ownership and any earlier periods you can verify.

faqs.question: Can I get a previous owner’s private flood claim history through CLUE?
faqs.answer: The CFPB describes how a consumer can request their own CLUE file. Ask the seller to request and share their file where relevant. Ask the seller or broker for carrier records to verify the specific insurers, policies and periods you need.

title: ERCOT LMP vs. Settlement Point Price
description: Find ERCOT dispatch and 15-minute settlement prices. Replay one quarter-hour and verify a $25.70/MWh gap between the West Load Zone and West Hub.
coverAlt: ERCOT’s published real-time prices from 6:30 to 6:45 p.m. CST on November 25, 2026, were $46.78 per MWh at West Hub, $62.14 at ALP_BESS_RN, and $72.48 at West Load Zone.
coverCaption: ERCOT NP6-905-CD, November 25, 2026, delivery hour 19, interval 3. Prices shown in US dollars per MWh as posted.
intro: ERCOT’s real-time locational marginal price (LMP) is a dispatch price for a location at a Security-Constrained Economic Dispatch run. The real-time Settlement Point Price (SPP) is the published price for a 15-minute settlement interval. Match the price series, settlement point and delivery interval before calculating an energy cost or comparing power contracts. In one November 25 quarter-hour, ERCOT posted $46.78/MWh at West Hub and $72.48/MWh at West Load Zone. That $25.70/MWh difference comes from comparing two different settlement points at the same time.
takeaways: Use NP6-788-CD for dispatch LMPs at settlement points, NP6-787-CD for electrical bus LMPs and NP6-905-CD for 15-minute settlement point prices.
Match the exact point name, point type and delivery interval. The ERCOT export can list a load zone under more than one type.

At resource node ALP_BESS_RN, weighting four dispatch intervals by their seconds in the quarter-hour reproduces the posted $62.14/MWh to the cent. Averaging the three runs that started inside the quarter gives $62.25/MWh.

guideActions.label: Download the source rows and calculation

sections.heading: Which ERCOT price series should you use?

columns: What to keep from the record
rows: What price did a dispatch run produce at a resource node, hub or load zone?
NP6-788-CD, LMPs by settlement point. Dispatch usually runs about every five minutes.
SCED timestamp, repeated-hour flag and settlement point name.
What was the price at a specific electrical bus?
NP6-787-CD, LMPs by electrical bus.
Electrical bus identifier and dispatch timestamp. Check any mapping to a settlement point separately.
What real-time price was posted for the contract’s settlement interval?
NP6-905-CD, settlement point prices at 15-minute intervals.
Delivery date, hour, interval, repeated-hour flag, point name and point type.
Was a reliability deployment price adder present?
NP6-323-CD, price adders by dispatch interval.
Timestamp, repeated-hour flag and the separate energy adder field, RTRDPA.

blocks.text: A resource node, trading hub and load zone are different settlement locations. ERCOT’s rules specify how prices are formed for each. Start with the point and product named in your contract or market workflow. When you need a historical result, save the report edition and check for corrections after the initial posting.

sections.heading: How does a dispatch LMP become a 15-minute settlement price?

blocks.text: The sample covers 18:30 to 18:45 Central Standard Time on November 25, 2026. ERCOT identifies it as delivery hour 19, interval 3, with DST flag N. In UTC it runs from 00:30 to 00:45 on November 26. The dispatch run at 18:25:25 was still in effect for the first 20 seconds. The run at 18:45:25 falls beyond the interval.

For a resource node, ERCOT applies the published time weights to the dispatch prices plus the energy adder, subject to the applicable price floor. In this quarter-hour the four energy adders were zero. The weighted sum divided by 900 seconds was $62.1431/MWh, which rounds to the posted $62.14/MWh. An equal-weight average of the three runs that started in the quarter-hour gives $62.25/MWh. The downloadable record includes the prior and next dispatch timestamps so you can check the interval boundaries.

Download the Python replay

blocks.text: Save the Python script beside the JSON and run python3 ercot-settlement-replay.py. It derives the four time weights and checks the posted price. The versioned ZIP also includes instructions for verifying all ten original ERCOT archives.

sections.heading: Why can the West Hub and West Load Zone prices differ?

rows: HB_WEST
Trading hub (HU)
LZ_WEST
Load zone (LZ)
ALP_BESS_RN
Resource node (RN)
HB_HOUSTON
Trading hub (HU)
LZ_HOUSTON
Load zone (LZ)

blocks.text: For the same 15 minutes, West Load Zone minus West Hub was $25.70/MWh. Houston’s load zone minus hub was $0.15/MWh. A flat 50 MW load would consume 12.5 MWh during the interval. Multiplying that volume by the West price difference gives an illustrative $321.25 difference in the indexed energy component. Apply the contract’s settlement point, meter profile, delivery charges and other terms for a site budget.

The original export lists both LZ and energy-weighted LZEW records for West and Houston. The two type rows share a name and happen to have the same price for these zones in this quarter-hour. Preserve the type in the raw key, then select the relevant series before calculating a spread. Use the quoted contract point when comparing procurement options.

blocks.text: Give each candidate the same local time window and point type. Request the source timestamp, UTC timestamp, price units, correction treatment and source report. Start with the posted ERCOT prices as the control.

Ask for the as-posted record and any later revision for the same interval. Match the exact West Load Zone and West Hub types.

An open-source Python client with distinct ERCOT dispatch and settlement data products.
Save the query parameters and API timestamps. Verify that the returned report matches your intended interval and price series.
Dryos
Public query endpoints for dispatch LMP and 15-minute settlement prices.
Compare the returned type code and source publication time against ERCOT’s raw rows. Check the duplicate name case at West Load Zone.
Invariant Earth
Join the electricity evidence to the site’s mapped utility territory and physical assets where fields are available.
Start with an exact site match and check the field sources. Attach the relevant contract or ERCOT record to establish the settlement point and pricing basis.

The West Load Zone query returned one LZEW row. ERCOT’s raw file includes both LZ and LZEW. The prices coincide in this sample, so checking the price alone would miss the difference in returned types.

faqs.answer: An LMP comes from a dispatch run at a location. The 15-minute SPP is the published real-time price for a settlement point and delivery interval, calculated under ERCOT’s rules for resources, hubs and load zones.

faqs.question: Which ERCOT report has 15-minute prices?

faqs.question: Can I average three five-minute LMP readings to get an ERCOT settlement price?
faqs.answer: For a resource node, weight each dispatch run by the seconds it covers inside the quarter-hour, include the applicable energy adder, and apply ERCOT’s price calculation rules. Use the published SPP to verify the result.

coverCaption: NYC DOB NOW approved permits for contractor license GC 002305, January 1 through November 25, 2026. Counts from an Invariant review of the city extract.
intro: To find a contractor’s building permit history, start with the issuing agency’s contractor name or license lookup. Match the license type and number, then pull the original permit IDs and issue dates for the work you care about. In New York City, a 2026 search for permits listing Turner Construction returned 254 source rows and 230 distinct work permit numbers. Only 182 of those permit numbers had an initial issuance in the selected period. The difference matters when using permit data to evaluate prior work, count new authorizations, or identify sales leads.
takeaways: Check the authority, license type and license number alongside the company name. Keep the exact business name from the permit record.
For a count of new work authorizations, group by work permit number and check the filing reason. Keep renewal sequences and work types for the history.
Use inspection and sign-off records to check completion. For a sales lead, verify the active scope and whether the contract or subcontract is still open.

sections.heading: How do you look up permits by contractor name or license?

rows: Find the contractor’s credential
Open NYC DOB NOW’s Licensee tool. Search by business name or license number and select the license type. Confirm the associated business and check the current status through the issuing authority.
Licensing authority, license class, number and associated business. Preserve leading zeros.
Find permits issued to that license
In the NYC Approved Permits dataset, filter Applicant License and Permittee’s License Type. Try a distinctive business-name prefix if you start with a company name.
As recorded business name, work permit ID, sequence, filing reason, work type, address and Building Identification Number (BIN).
Check the original job record
Look up the job filing and permit in the public DOB portal. Check BIS for records filed there. NYC publishes separate datasets for electrical, elevator and limited alteration applications.
Source system, job filing, permit issue and expiration, and applicable inspection and sign-off records.

blocks.text: NYC allows a different business associated with the same applicant’s license to be selected through a renewal with changes. The city also provides a process for a new applicant to take over a permit. Preserve the applicant and business at each sequence. Read the source paperwork when a renewal affects who was responsible for the work.

For market analysis, publish the unit of measurement. Work permit numbers, first issuances, jobs, buildings and construction starts each describe a different quantity. For a construction lead, confirm that the relevant package is still open before entering it into a pipeline.

title: How to check a Chicago liquor license by address
description: Look up active Chicago liquor licenses and applications by address. Check the license class, operator, site number, expiration and Illinois state record.
coverAlt: Three sourced records at Door 24. A packaged goods renewal was issued May 28, 2025, a Tavern application payment was recorded October 23, 2026, and a retail food license was issued November 20, 2026.
coverCaption: Three city records for 2124 North Damen Avenue, first floor. Chicago Business Licenses and the BACP liquor application list, checked November 25, 2026.
intro: To check a Chicago liquor license by address, start with the city’s current liquor and amusement licenses. Match the street direction, floor or unit, legal operator and license class. Then check the separate city application list and the Illinois state license lookup. At 2124 North Damen Avenue, the same operator and floor had an issued packaged-goods renewal, an issued food license and a Tavern application in the records we reviewed on November 25, 2026. Each record supports a different decision about the space.
takeaways: Use the city’s current view to check the license class and valid term. Use Business Licenses history to find earlier terms and issue dates.
Chicago’s recent application list displays a payment date. Look for an issued license for the requested class before relying on the application.
Before underwriting a lease or acquisition, verify the local and state records under the legal entity that plans to operate.

sections.heading: Where to look up a Chicago liquor license

rows: 1. Find the current city record
Open Current Active Business Licenses for Liquor and Amusement and filter Address. Try the city’s abbreviated form, such as 2124 N DAMEN AVE. Check the floor and legal name on each match.
License number and class, account and site, start and expiration, and the date you checked.
2. Recover the license history
In Business Licenses, filter by license number and check for multiple terms. Search the account and site to find other license classes held by that operator at the premises.
Record ID, application type, source status, date issued and term dates. Keep a separate row per term.
3. Check applications and location restrictions
Search the six-week city application list by street or operator. Use the city’s licensing resources to check restrictions for the property and the planned class.
The reported class, payment date, and the agency’s current decision or case record when available.
4. Check the state license
Use the ILCC public lookup by legal name, address or full state license number. Confirm the location, entity, class and dates in the result before relying on it.
State license number and exact match to the premises and operating entity.

title: How to find commercial construction leads before bids close
description: Compare construction lead sources and verify open bids, pre-bid meetings, awards, and rebids. Download 13 records from two Miami-Dade cases.
coverAlt: Two timelines show W-951R moving from bid opening to award filing and later ratification, while S-20057 moved from bid opening to rejection and later ratification.
coverCaption: Two procurement histories from Miami-Dade County records. The announced successor S-20057R needs its own solicitation and deadline check.
intro: To find construction projects you can bid on, start with the owner’s current solicitation or a bid service that links back to it. Check the mandatory pre-bid meeting, the latest addenda and the deadline for your package. Planning records help you spot projects early. Permit and award records help you identify the work and the prime contractor for follow-up. Each answers a different question about who can still bid.
takeaways: Track the next action for your trade and package. A general contractor’s bid can close while a separate subcontract package is still accepting bids.
Miami-Dade’s W-951R award was filed in December 2025. The Board ratified it in October 2026, 308 days later. Those dates describe the same award.
Miami-Dade rejected both bids for S-20057 and identified S-20057R as the revised solicitation. Require a current notice before treating the successor as open.

sections.heading: Where to find projects at the right stage

blocks.text: Decide who you sell to and the point when they can act. A design firm can monitor planning agendas and capital budgets. A prime contractor needs the owner’s solicitation. A subcontractor needs the package, its deadline and the general contractor’s invitation or status. A manufacturer may use plans, specifications and the named project team before bidding starts.

columns: What you can do with it
rows: Planning or design
Capital plan, planning case, site plan or design solicitation
Track the owner and scope, confirm the affected site and watch for the relevant package.
Open prime bid
Current notice, eligible bidders, pre-bid meeting, addenda and deadline
Verify the submission requirements before estimating or bidding.
Trade package
Invitation or package listing from a named prime, owner or construction manager
Confirm the work your company can bid on and the package deadline.
Bid results or award
Bid tabulation, recommendation, award notice and executed agreement
Separate bids received from the winning contract. Identify which packages could still be procured.
Permit or construction
Issuing agency permit, issued notice to proceed or dated construction progress record
Verify what the record authorizes or observes at the building or facility.

blocks.text: For public work, use the owner’s procurement portal and check the latest notice and addenda for the exact solicitation. A listing can remain searchable after bids close. For private work, ask the party issuing the trade package to confirm who can submit, what is in scope and when pricing is due.

sections.heading: Two Miami-Dade solicitations, two different outcomes

blocks.text: The county advertised W-951R for electrical upgrades at the Alexander Orr, Jr. Water Treatment Plant on August 28, 2025. Its mandatory pre-bid meeting was scheduled 20 days later. The county opened three bids on October 29, 62 days after the advertisement. A contractor who waited for the bid-opening record would already have missed the mandatory meeting.

rows: W-951R award filing
December 2, 2025. The county recorded the $28.904 million award to Poole & Kent Company of Florida.
Close out the prime bid stage for that solicitation. Keep the original award date.
W-951R execution
March 12, 2026. The October memorandum records execution and clerk attestation.
Store execution as a later event on the same contract.
W-951R notice to proceed estimate
July 20, 2026 appears as an estimate in Exhibit A.
Keep the field marked estimated until an issued notice or reliable progress record establishes the next milestone.
W-951R Board ratification
October 6, 2026. The October transparency report identifies resolution R-827-26.
Link ratification to the December award. It came 308 days later under the county’s delegated award process.
S-20057 bids and rejection
Two bids opened on August 27, 2025. The county says it rejected all bids on December 3.
Close the original bid opportunity as rejected. Preserve the filing date and decision date separately.
S-20057R revised solicitation
The county identified the successor number when it explained the rejection.
Monitor the new solicitation ID for an issued notice, requirements and deadlines.

blocks.text: The W-951R tabulation gives Poole & Kent a $23.3 million base bid and a $28.904 million total including allowances. That $5.604 million difference belongs to the bid’s amount fields. A dashboard should keep the base bid, total bid and contract award in their own columns.

For S-20057, the clerk stamped the rejection recommendation on December 2. The February Board memorandum describes December 3 as the rejection date, and the Board ratified it on February 18, 2026. The October status table shows December 2. Preserve the two source values with the records they came from. The same North District plant also had a separate electrical distribution building award under S-968. Match the contract ID and work scope before attributing that award to a lead.

blocks.text: Give each provider the same contractor role, trade, territory and project type. Ask it to find the official notice for W-951R, report the prime bid deadline and identify the eventual award. Then test whether it keeps the rejected S-20057 bid and the planned S-20057R successor separate. The provider descriptions below come from public product materials. The procurement results come from the county’s records.

Planned projects, timelines and firms from published reports and searches.

sections.heading: Keep the next step and the evidence in your CRM

blocks.text: Use a persistent project record for the site or capital program. Give each solicitation and trade package its own ID. Store the observed event, the date it applied, the date fetched, the issuing source and whether the record reports an actual event, estimate or proposal. Keep prior events when a bid is delayed, canceled, rejected or reopened.

Before sending estimating work to your team, record the trade package, issuer, deadline with time zone, mandatory meeting and source. An award can support a follow-up with the named prime. For an issued permit or the start of work, check the specific agency record and what scope it covers.

faqs.question: How do I find open commercial construction bids?
faqs.answer: Start with the owner’s procurement portal or a project service that links to it. Confirm the solicitation and package ID, current deadline, mandatory meetings, eligibility, and latest addenda before estimating the work.

faqs.question: Can a building permit show whether subcontract bidding is still open?
faqs.answer: A permit documents the agency’s action for specific work. Ask the prime or package owner for a current invitation, trade scope, and deadline to check whether there is still a bidding opportunity.

faqs.question: What is the difference between bid results and a contract award?
faqs.answer: Bid results list the submissions received. An award identifies the contractor selected for the contract. W-951R shows both records, with a later signed contract and a separate Board ratification.

faqs.question: Does a rebid number mean I can bid now?
faqs.answer: It identifies a possible successor solicitation. Check the actual advertisement and addenda for an open window. In Miami-Dade’s rejection record, S-20057R is the announced successor to S-20057.

title: How to compare elevation data APIs for a U.S. address
description: Compare Invariant Earth, USGS, Mireye, Google, OpenTopography and emem. See three live elevation results at one address and download the source trial.
coverAlt: Illustrated oblique aerial view of streets and buildings climbing a hillside above a California bay.
coverCaption: Generated editorial illustration of a coastal hillside. The source trial uses a separate address in San Francisco.
intro: For ground elevation at a U.S. address, confirm the address point and start with a bare-earth terrain source such as USGS 3DEP. For slope or grading, use a terrain raster and the full site boundary. In a live test at San Francisco Main Library, USGS and Mireye returned 19.25 m and 19.28 m from different terrain grids. emem returned 20.59 m from a Copernicus surface model at a nearby representative point. Each value answers a different measurement question.
takeaways: Check the coordinate, physical surface, vertical datum, source resolution and date before comparing two elevation results.
For parcel screening with Invariant Earth, use point elevation alongside separate records for the parcel, building footprint and flood intersections.
For flood underwriting, establish which building is being insured and obtain the required surveyed elevations where applicable.

guideActions.label: Download the trial inputs and results

sections.heading: Which elevation API fits the job?

blocks.text: A point service is a good fit for a lookup on a confirmed coordinate. Use a raster for a parcel or route where the question concerns a range of elevations, terrain slope, or the area meeting a grading threshold. Use a combined property platform when the evidence needs to travel with parcel identity and other site records.

rows: Invariant Earth
Start here when terrain is part of a site or property workflow. Earth documents separate tools for point elevation, parcel lookup and site screening, with source metadata on field responses.
Request the elevation and its source URL. Then confirm that the parcel and flood results use the intended geometry.
USGS EPQS
Direct point lookup using the best available 3DEP terrain data at the coordinate.
Keep the reported raster ID, resolution and acquisition date. Repeat at the same coordinate rather than at a nearby geocode.
Mireye Fetch
Address or coordinate lookup for point elevation and other location fields. Its catalog describes a seamless 3DEP terrain grid and an EPQS fallback.
Read the source, data vintage and status. Request the original raster ID or acquisition date if your review needs it.
Google Maps Elevation API
Point and sampled path elevations through the Maps Platform. Returns coordinates and elevation, with resolution where available.
Compare a single-point call with your production sampling pattern. Ask how to align the result with the vertical datum used by your other inputs.
OpenTopography
Source-selectable elevation rasters, including global terrain and surface products.
Clip a named terrain raster to your site and retain the source product, datum, resolution and any missing cells.
emem
Location-cell observations and verifiable receipts. The tested band reads a Copernicus surface-model pixel.
Confirm the physical surface, representative coordinate and date that the fact describes. Verify the receipt separately.

blocks.text: Invariant publishes this comparison. We ran live reads against USGS, Mireye and emem on November 25, 2026 Pacific time. The entries for Invariant Earth, Google Maps Platform and OpenTopography use their public documentation. The test covers one point and compares what each response measures and reports.

sections.heading: Three elevation readings at San Francisco Main Library

blocks.text: We used the published city address point for 100 Larkin Street, at 37.77905419° N and 122.41632622° W, within San Francisco tax lot 0354001. The download retains the coordinate at full precision. USGS and Mireye accepted it directly. For emem, we resolved the coordinate to its cell and requested that cell’s Copernicus elevation band.

rows: USGS EPQS
Interpolated bare-earth elevation at the input point. The response returned raster 72150 at 1 m resolution, with a March 4, 2023 acquisition date.
Mireye Fetch
Ground elevation at the input point. The response identified the 3DEP seamless grid at about 10 m. Its vintage field named the product without a specific acquisition date.
emem
Copernicus GLO-30 surface height at one pixel containing the cell’s representative point. The response identified April 30, 2021 as the source edition date.

blocks.text: The displays are rounded to two decimal places to distinguish the returned values. That precision is a display choice. The products sample the ground or surface differently, at different resolutions and sometimes at different points. The elevation difference cannot establish building height or an error in either source.

blocks.label: Download the request coordinates, source details and returned values

sections.heading: What to save with an elevation value

items: Keep the address-match type, input coordinate and sampled geometry. A geocoder can place you at a rooftop, a driveway or an estimated location on the street. Preserve a moved or representative point if the service uses one.

Record what was measured. Bare-earth terrain models remove above-ground features where possible. Digital surface models can retain buildings and vegetation. A statistic computed inside a site boundary needs its own record of the boundary and sampling method.

Keep the vertical datum and units. A datum sets the height reference. The WGS84 latitude and longitude in a request describe horizontal position. USGS generally uses NAVD88 in the conterminous U.S. Copernicus GLO-30 uses EGM2008. Check the specific product before combining values.

Separate the source date from the time the API fetched or served the record. Some services report an acquisition date, while others give only a product name or edition. Preserve the meaning of the date in your data model.

blocks.text: In the emem trial, the provider’s verifier reported a valid signature and Merkle proof for the returned receipt. We submitted the receipt alone. The provider described the pixel and the edition date separately, outside the signed bytes. Keep both the receipt and the source description so a reviewer can check what was served and what the elevation actually measures.

items.label: What a vertical datum measures

sections.heading: Apply the result to the property decision

blocks.text: For a development site, use the parcel boundary and a terrain raster to estimate slope and identify the largest contiguous usable area. Keep access, drainage, wetlands and setbacks as separate layers. For underwriting, match the building footprint to the applicable flood map and confirm the required building elevation and datum from the elevation certificate or a qualified professional.

With Invariant Earth, request the documented elevation field at a confirmed point, then look up the parcel and carry the geography, source links and dates into the review. The field catalog describes a seamless 3DEP terrain grid with USGS EPQS as a fallback. The published response example shows how to carry a source link with a result. An Earth trial should capture the actual response for the same address and explicitly record differences in source file, acquisition date and sampled geometry.

faqs.question: How do I get ground elevation by street address?
faqs.answer: Resolve the address to a latitude and longitude and confirm it matches the intended property. Query a bare-earth source such as USGS 3DEP for that point. Save the coordinate, datum, source and date along with the value.

faqs.question: Why do elevation APIs return different results for the same address?
faqs.answer: They may sample different coordinates, terrain or surface models, grid resolutions, acquisition dates and vertical datums. Compare those details before interpreting the difference between two returned elevations.

faqs.question: Can an API elevation replace a flood elevation certificate?
faqs.answer: A terrain API gives modeled ground elevation for a point or raster cell. A flood elevation certificate documents building-specific elevations used for the applicable flood determination. Follow the requirement for the particular building and review.

faqs.question: What does a signed elevation receipt prove?
faqs.answer: A verified receipt can establish the integrity of the provider’s returned payload. Review the source dataset and its measurement method separately to decide what the reading represents.

title: How to find Chicago city-owned lots for sale
description: Find Chicago city-owned land through ChiBlockBuilder. Check application dates, group parcel IDs into sites, and download the November 25 inventory review.
coverAlt: Illustration of a grassy vacant lot between two brick homes on a residential Chicago street.
coverCaption: Generated editorial illustration of an infill lot, separate from the sites in the city’s offering.
intro: To find city-owned land for sale in Chicago, start with the ChiBlockBuilder listing for your planned use. Check its application window and the exact parcel numbers before you put the site on a shortlist. On November 25, 2026, the city inventory showed 12,001 records marked Owned by City. Only 19 also said Apply, and four failed a check of the opening and closing dates.
takeaways: Check ownership, sales status and the application dates separately. Compare the listing with the application or notice for the specific site.
The November 25 inventory review found six parcel rows for the city’s three courtyard-building RFP sites. Four of those rows form one offering on South Indiana Avenue.
Check the basis of a listed dollar value. The city’s Land Value field carries its own valuation date. The solicitation or agreement sets the actual purchase terms.

guideActions.label: See the dated Chicago inventory check

sections.heading: Where to look for city-owned land in Chicago

blocks.text: Use ChiBlockBuilder for purchase opportunities from Chicago’s Department of Planning and Development. It organizes offerings around uses including housing, commercial and mixed-use development, side yards, open space and agriculture. Open the offering for your planned use and check which parcel or group of parcels it lists. The same city site separately posts public notices for proposed transfers and other limited processes.

Use City-Owned Land Inventory to verify the property index number (PIN), the city’s ownership label and the status fields. The inventory includes historical records such as sales. For a county land bank property, use the Cook County Land Bank Authority’s own listing and announcement. On November 25 the Authority said it was temporarily pausing applications during a system transition.

sections.heading: How many records pass the city’s application date check?

blocks.text: We queried Chicago’s published inventory on November 25, 2026, using the local calendar date. We counted unique PINs, filtered to Owned by City and Apply, and required the published opening date to be at or before November 25 and the deadline to be at or after it. The dates are as the city recorded them. Check the offering for the time of day and amendments.

blocks.text: Three of the four excluded records carried November 16 deadlines. At 118 East 104th Street, the recorded January 15, 2026 deadline precedes the October 1, 2026 opening date. Keep the original values and flag the row for review. An application URL or an Apply label alone leaves that conflict unresolved.

Even among the 15 date-matched records, four were classified as Public Notice. A notice can describe a transfer or a limited process. Read the notice before treating it as an invitation to apply. These are counts from an inventory query on one date. The city can change offerings.

Invariant Earth can screen parcel and location attributes such as terrain, mapped hazards, and nearby infrastructure. Start with the actual lot or parcel group from the city application.
