title: How to compare data center site selection platforms and advisors
description: Compare Invariant, MeanderX, Site Selection Group and other options for data center siting. Test what each can verify using the 176 MW Plaza 500 case.
coverAlt: Illustration of a data center building beside a wooded power corridor in low winter sunlight.
coverCaption: Generated editorial illustration of a generic data center and utility corridor.
intro: Start with Invariant when you need to compare parcels and model power delivery on the same set of sites. A development platform can help a team build a pipeline. A site selection advisor can also negotiate the deal. Compare each on the actual land, electrical service points and dates your project needs. In Fairfax County, Virginia, the proposed Plaza 500 data center’s 176 MW request, state order, county substation review and utility construction schedule each came from a different record.
takeaways: Give every provider the same boundary, facility demand by phase and earliest acceptable service dates. Ask what it can document for each stage.
MeanderX helps analyze interconnection opportunities and queue activity. Site Selection Group advises data center occupiers and developers and can handle real estate and incentive negotiations.

At Plaza 500, the August 2025 state order specifies an October 2027 in-service date. Dominion’s project page lists Q2 2028 as its energization target. Keep both dates and ask which terms apply to customer service.

sections.heading: Which providers fit the decision?

blocks.text: Start with the work your team needs this month. A market shortlist needs consistent data across many parcels. A land option needs a site-specific path to utility service. An acquisition or colocation agreement also needs commercial terms and negotiation. The table reflects public descriptions of the offerings. Invariant publishes this guide. The Plaza 500 record review below is independent of the providers’ marketing.

rows: Invariant

Parcel and site screening through Invariant Earth, plus pre-application power studies for specific connection options. The published method covers AC power flow, contingencies, and indicative upgrade costs and schedules.
A cited parcel record and a study showing phase MW, binding constraints and the proposed work at each connection. Ask which assumptions need utility review.
MeanderX
Interconnection intelligence built from utility records. Public examples emphasize renewable development, queue analysis and planned network changes.
A sample for importing load at the site. Ask whether the headroom number represents customer withdrawal or generation export, what year it covers and which upgrades it assumes.
Site Selection Group
Location advisory for greenfield, powered shell and colocation projects. Its services include infrastructure and power assessment, incentive negotiation and real estate transactions.
The dated diligence file supporting the shortlist, with serving utility, each site’s service assumptions and ownership of the remaining negotiations.
Paces
Development pipeline tools and site diligence covering power, permitting and site constraints.
A report and the evidence behind each stage in the pipeline. Ask how a modeled connection becomes a utility application and how the team tracks subsequent changes.
Geoforge
Site reports with modeled injection and offtake capacity by year and scenario, plus other site diligence information.
A site-level offtake scenario with named connection, study year, modeled MW and assumptions on competing demand and upgrades.
GridCARE
Grid modeling and utility collaboration for accelerating large customer connections. Its Portland General Electric announcement describes using load flexibility to study capacity.
Whether the serving utility can study that path and how the proposed firm and flexible load portions would be treated under the service terms.
LandGate
Parcel and site screening with power, fiber, topography and exclusion layers, plus data center feasibility studies.
A buildable polygon and a named service point for the same candidate. Ask for the year and case behind the offtake estimate, then compare both with your phased service dates.
GE Vernova Consulting Services
Engineering and power economics consulting. Published data center siting work covers generation surplus, curtailment, congestion and site conditions.
A scoped study that connects the regional cost and reliability results to the specific facility’s point of delivery and operating profile.
GridUnity
Software for managing large-load connection requests, including application intake, study milestones and financial security deadlines.
Start with a phased load request. Ask which utility reviews it, who owns the next milestone, and which study or agreement records the proposed service date.
Transect
Environmental feasibility reports with buildable area, local permitting context and site-level exclusion mapping.
Use the same candidate tract to reproduce excluded acres and check the permit triggers. Ask which utility records support a separate connection review.

sections.heading: MeanderX vs. Site Selection Group for data center siting

blocks.text: MeanderX is relevant when your decision depends on tracking queues and changes to the grid across a market. Its published case study describes turning unstructured utility documents into structured records, including plans for new transmission lines and substations. For data center power access, ask to see its load-side coverage for your serving utility and the evidence behind the import capacity estimate. A queue forecast can help prioritize a conversation with the utility.

Site Selection Group is relevant when you need a real estate advisor to identify locations, compare commercial terms and negotiate a transaction. Its March 2026 Central Virginia land acquisition announcement describes that work for a confidential hyperscale client. The announcement omits the site, requested MW and delivery date. Ask for a representative diligence package with those fields before relying on a shortlist.

When you need repeatable data for a pipeline or an application, start with Invariant Earth’s documented site screening workflow. For a parcel you want to advance, scope a separate power study around the planned demand and target in-service dates. Use the same site and evidence requirements when asking an advisor or software vendor for a trial.

sections.heading: What the Plaza 500 public records establish

blocks.text: Use 6295 Edsall Road, Alexandria, Virginia, and Fairfax County tax parcel 0812 01 0007 as the inputs. The Virginia State Corporation Commission hearing examiner links the customer’s planned campus to Plaza 500. Dominion told the commission that the existing Van Dorn Substation could not supply the initial bridging load as designed and that serving the full amount there would overload transformers by 2029. That assessment pertains to the design and load in the case record.

rows: February 2025 hearing examiner’s report
Dominion reported 176 MW in projected load requested for the planned campus.
The demand by phase and the amount the utility would deliver by each required date.
August 2025 state order, PUR-2024-00135
The SCC granted state authorization as provided in its order. Ordering paragraph 8 specifies October 1, 2027 as the in-service date and October 1, 2028 as the certificate sunset.
Any later order affecting the schedule, and the permits and site work still needed to construct the facilities.
October 2027 virtual open house timeline and Q2 2028 utility project page
The virtual open house displays October 2027 for project energization. Dominion’s main Edsall project page displays Q2 2028.
Which revision governs the build schedule, whether the order has been amended, and which milestone supports each customer phase.
Fairfax County application 2232-2025-MA-00007
As checked November 25, 2026, the county agenda scheduled the substation’s public hearing for December 2, 2026.
The county’s actual action and any conditions. The state order and the local substation review are separate records.

blocks.text: A report that shows one power date for Plaza 500 hides a scheduling discrepancy a buyer would need to resolve. Q2 2028 begins six months after the October 1, 2027 in-service date in the order. The October 1, 2028 sunset concerns the certificate. Ask for current utility documentation tying construction, commissioning and service at the meter to the intended load ramp.

The docket also records a $23.1 million conceptual project estimate in 2024 dollars. Carry the basis and scope with that number. For an investment decision, confirm current estimates, the customer’s cost obligations, security, and which upgrades the charging terms cover.

sections.heading: How to run a trial on an actual site

blocks.text: Give every vendor the same parcel polygon and project brief. Include facility demand at the meter by phase, earliest and latest acceptable service dates, reliability requirements and the amount of load you can curtail. Note whether the request is for utility import, backup, export or a combination. Give the vendor a different parcel from your real pipeline after it shows a worked example.

items: Ask for the exact parcel and evidence date. Have the provider account for usable area, land use, access, water and fiber where they drive your decision. Keep a mapped feature and a provider’s service offer in separate fields.

Ask for the connection option and year. A credible load study names the limiting equipment, outages tested, competing loads and any upgrades that change the answer. Ask which model came from the utility and which was reconstructed.
Ask for the contract or dated utility correspondence behind each phase. Track who owns the next decision, who pays for connection work, and whether key dates carry conditions.

Ask the vendor to replay the Plaza 500 case. A usable answer retains the 176 MW request, the two ordered dates, the different published schedule and the pending local hearing in separate fields. A vendor should leave a field unresolved when its source cannot establish it.

title: Electric Utility Lookup by Address: Who Serves a Site?
description: Find the electric utility for an address. Compare state and national territory maps, see a verified Minnesota overlap, and learn whom to ask about new service.
coverAlt: Summer aerial imagery of western Chaska, Minnesota, marked at the county address point for 2007 Schoolmaster Drive.
coverCaption: CloudHQ’s proposed Chaska site address at 2007 Schoolmaster Drive. County address point over USDA NAIP imagery from 2023.
intro: To find the electric utility for an existing address, start with a recent bill or meter record from the property. For vacant land, match the address or parcel to the planned location of electric service and check the state’s utility territory map. A national map can narrow the search. At three Minnesota addresses we tested, it also returned a municipal utility from Nebraska.
takeaways: Check who delivers electricity to the meter. A competitive supplier that sells the power can be a separate company.
Use the commission’s electric service area map where available. Keep all candidates from an overlapping national layer and check the utility IDs and states.
For a new high-load site, confirm who would build and own the connection, which organization studies it, and how much load can be delivered by each required date.

sections.heading: How to find the electric utility for an address

items: For a building with service, get a recent bill tied to the premises or meter number. Record the delivery utility and the organization that bills for the electricity supply.
For vacant land, confirm the parcel and mark the proposed service entrance or utility handoff. In a multi-building development, check each planned point separately.

Search the public utility commission’s map for that point. Where the state publishes only a county list or an approximate boundary, ask the likely provider and the commission to confirm the assignment.
Give the utility the parcel, planned point of delivery, requested service date and expected facility load. Ask which application and study apply to the site.

blocks.text: A ZIP code can contain customers of multiple utilities. EIA’s county-level service territory survey tracks counties where a utility reports distribution equipment. Use that list to find candidates when a detailed map is missing. Use a state or utility record to resolve the individual site.

sections.heading: What three Minnesota addresses show about national utility maps

blocks.text: On November 25, 2026, we took address points from Carver County and queried two layers: the official Minnesota service area map and the national HIFLD layer republished by NTIA. At Chanhassen City Hall, the county also lists a separate Park unit at 7700 Market Boulevard. We used the county point identified as City Hall.

rows: 2007 Schoolmaster Drive, Chaska
City of Chaska, EIA ID 3400
City of Chaska, plus City of St. Paul, Nebraska, ID 17899
1 City Hall Plaza, Chaska
City of Chaska, EIA ID 3400
City of Chaska, plus City of St. Paul, Nebraska, ID 17899
7700 Market Boulevard, Chanhassen
Xcel Energy, EIA ID 13781

blocks.text: The Xcel and Northern States names carry the same EIA ID in the two layers. St. Paul, Nebraska, is a separate utility. The national layer’s record for ID 17899 says NE and intersected all three Minnesota points. The Nebraska municipality describes its retail system as serving its own community. This trial shows why a team should keep the full set of matches and confirm the relevant one with a better local source.

sections.heading: Who studies the power connection for a large new load?

blocks.text: The Minnesota service-area map places the address point for CloudHQ’s proposed campus in the City of Chaska’s distribution territory. Chaska’s project description says that under the proposed design the Minnesota Municipal Power Agency would own and operate the new on-site substation, which would connect directly to Xcel Energy transmission. The city describes a preliminary system impact study involving CloudHQ, MMPA and Xcel.

Keep separate records for the mapped retail territory, the proposed point of delivery, the substation owner and the organization responsible for the study. Before underwriting a factory or data center phase, request the utility’s written service evidence for the facility MW, service voltage, delivery point, upgrade scope and earliest service date. Record the status of each agreement and the date of the evidence.

sections.heading: How to integrate a utility territory lookup in your workflow

blocks.text: Invariant Earth’s electric utility service territory field queries the NTIA copy of HIFLD. Its current public definition calls for a single containing utility before it names one. When a point has overlapping matches or no match, route the address to a state map or the local utility for review. Keep the utility ID, source and date you checked so the next analyst can reproduce the decision.

faqs.question: How do I find the electricity provider for a new address?
faqs.answer: Find the parcel or planned service point, then check the state’s electric utility service area map. Give the likely utility the street address, parcel identifier and intended load. Ask it to verify which organization should handle a new service request.

faqs.question: Can I use a ZIP code to find my electricity supplier?
faqs.answer: Use a ZIP code to form a list of candidates. For an existing building, use the bill or meter record to verify the delivery utility and any separate supplier. For new construction, verify the exact service point with the utility.

faqs.question: Does a service territory map tell me how many MW a utility can deliver?
faqs.answer: A territory match helps you identify whom to contact. Request written service evidence for the requested load, date, voltage, location and upgrades. A large project may have a proposed transmission connection or a separate power agency involved.

title: How to Find Recorded Property Easements by Address
description: Find an easement by address or parcel number, locate the recorded agreement, and see why a New York City parcel search can miss a real easement.
coverAlt: Aerial view of 4095 9th Avenue in Inwood with Manhattan tax lots 50 and 75 outlined beside the Harlem River.
coverCaption: Manhattan block 2197, lots 50 and 75. The outlines show NYC MapPLUTO 26v3 tax lots. Aerial imagery by NYC OTI, 2024, CC BY 4.0, cropped and annotated by Invariant.
intro: To find a recorded easement by address, match the address to a parcel number, search the recorder for that lot and its earlier identifiers, and open the agreement and its survey exhibit. At 4095 9th Avenue in Manhattan, New York City cites a recorded telecom easement over part of a development site. The city’s document index classifies it as an easement. Every attached tax-lot row has an easement flag of N.
takeaways: Use the parcel number to find document candidates. Read the recorded agreement and exhibits to establish the area, permitted use and parties who benefit.
Search beyond the parcel’s easement flag. A search limited to rows marked Y would miss the Inwood agreement. Look up the document type and read the original instrument.
Keep execution and recording dates separate. At a Queens commercial property, the board decision and city instrument index assign different meanings to the same date.

guideActions.label: Find the assessor parcel number field

sections.heading: Where to look for easements on a property

items: Use the assessor or GIS map to resolve the address to the correct parcel. Take note of lots that share the same address and older lot numbers from splits or mergers.

Search the county recorder or register for the parcel number, the owner names in the deed chain and any document numbers in the deed or title commitment. Agreements, deeds and recorded plats can all carry easement language.
Pull the recorded agreement, legal description and exhibit. Read what was granted, over which land, to which party and for what purpose. Follow later amendments, notices and releases.
For a purchase, loan or development decision, ask the title team and surveyor to reconcile the instrument with the current legal description and proposed site plan.

blocks.text: A GIS easement layer can indicate where to investigate. Fairfax County publishes a general easement layer and a separate stormwater layer, and acknowledges gaps in its mapped data. Clark County, Washington, points buyers to deeds, title reports and recorded surveys for evidence that may be absent from the map.

items.label: What to verify in a recorded easement

sections.heading: Two easement searches in New York City

blocks.text: NYC’s ACRIS Legals table links documents to borough, block and lot. ACRIS Master supplies the document type, City Register File Number (CRFN), and the document and recording dates. Join them by document ID. The city’s control-code table defines EASE as an easement instrument.

rows: 4095 9th Avenue, Inwood
CRFN 2022000070247. Recorded February 15, 2022 in ACRIS.
Manhattan block 2197. Lots 47, 50, 75 and 77 all carry N. The RFP identifies lots 50 and 75 as its site.
HPD cites the agreement for Spectrum’s exclusive use of the easement area.
43-20 Little Neck Parkway, Queens
CRFN 2021000504930. ACRIS lists December 15, 2021 as the document date and December 23 as the recording date.
Queens block 8129. Lots 44, 64 and 65 carry Y.
The board decision describes pedestrian and vehicle access to the parking parcel.

blocks.text: Inwood developers asked whether the area could serve as a pedestrian path, building access or access to parking. HPD referred them to the recorded agreement and described Spectrum’s exclusive use. The city’s answer is a reason to retrieve the agreement before counting the area as usable access. The tax-lot outlines in the cover image locate the site. The agreement’s exhibit is the record to review for the easement limits.

In Queens, the board describes access from Little Neck Parkway over portions of lots 64 and 65 to the lot 44 parking area. The decision calls December 15 the recording date. The ACRIS index puts that day in the document-date field and lists December 23 separately as the recording date. Keep both sources in the file and use the recorded cover page to reconcile the discrepancy. The board’s decision also describes conditions tied to the variance, so pull any later approvals and changes before relying on the access.

faqs.question: Is an easement the same as a right of way?

title: How to Use Daytime Population for Retail Site Selection
description: Compare jobs near a storefront with workers who live nearby. Download a two-site Chicago example using 2024 Census employment and home-to-work data.
coverAlt: 2024 Census primary jobs within straight-line 800 metre circles. Washington/Wabash has 379,349 jobs at workplaces and 9,661 employed residents in the data. Logan Square has 2,988 jobs at workplaces and 10,048 employed residents in the data.
coverCaption: Invariant analysis of 2024 Census LODES 8.5 records using Chicago Transit Authority station coordinates.
intro: To compare daytime demand around a store, count the jobs located in its trade area and the employed residents who live there. Keep both alongside measured foot traffic for your opening hours. In two 800-metre Chicago samples, the number of employed residents was similar, but Washington/Wabash had about 127 times as many primary jobs at workplaces as Logan Square.
takeaways: Use workplace jobs to screen where daytime demand could come from. Use household data for the residential market.
Use home-to-work records to find workers who already live nearby and avoid counting them twice.
Use street-level counts by day and hour before estimating store visits or sales.

sections.heading: What does daytime population mean for a retail site?

blocks.text: The Census Bureau defines commuter-adjusted population as resident population plus workers at workplaces in the area, minus workers who live in the area. For the geographies where the American Community Survey publishes all three components, use its matching tables and period. Its published workplace table covers selected geographic levels. A custom store radius calls for a separate estimate.

For a trade area you draw yourself, Census LODES gives you jobs by workplace block, represented in the Workplace Area Characteristics file, and jobs by home block, represented in the Residence Area Characteristics file. In the Chicago comparison we use primary jobs, the highest-earning job for each worker as defined by Census. That makes it possible to compare covered employed residents with covered jobs at workplaces without adding all secondary jobs.

Workplace locations in LODES are assigned to establishments. To plan service hours, confirm actual presence with counts at the storefront or along the approach people would use. The employment records describe the jobs tied to an area, while counts describe observed activity in a specific window.

sections.heading: What do two Chicago trade areas show?

blocks.text: We centered straight-line circles on the CTA Washington/Wabash and Logan Square station coordinates. A 2020 Census block is counted in full when its Census internal point falls within the radius. Each run uses 2024 Illinois LODES 8.5 primary-job records. The two stations are comparison points. A real lease decision should use the storefront entrance and its walking routes.

Workplace jobs held by people living outside the circle

Logan Square

blocks.text: Within 800 metres, Washington/Wabash had 379,349 primary jobs at workplaces and 9,661 employed residents in the data. Logan Square had 2,988 primary jobs at workplaces and 10,048 employed residents. The difference in workplace jobs appears at 400 and 1,200 metres as well. The two home-to-work files independently reconcile to the workplace job counts at every radius.

The home-to-work file matches 2,844 jobs held by workers who also lived within 800 metres of Washington/Wabash and 216 within the Logan Square circle. Those jobs are part of the workplace total. To understand who might visit a store, keep the overlap visible alongside workers whose homes are outside the circle.

Shortlisting two sites

Use one boundary method across sites and record the radius or travel time, network date, Census release, and days and hours in the foot-traffic sample. Let the counts and operating costs drive the lease decision.

faqs.question: Where can I find daytime population data?
faqs.answer: For places with ACS workplace tables, estimate commuter-adjusted population from resident population, workers at area workplaces and employed residents. For a custom retail trade area, use Census LODES block records to compare workplace and resident jobs and add a separate estimate of reachable households.

faqs.question: How do I avoid counting workers twice in a retail trade area?
faqs.answer: Use the LODES primary jobs files and compare home and work blocks in the origin-destination file. Workers whose home and workplace both fall in the trade area are part of both summaries. Keep that overlap visible when combining market segments.

faqs.question: Can daytime employment stand in for foot traffic?
faqs.answer: Use daytime employment to find areas with a large workplace base. Use measured visits or pedestrian counts near the store during planned hours to estimate the traffic it might capture.

title: How to Check a FEMA Floodway Before Buying Land
description: See what a regulatory floodway means for development. Reproduce a FEMA parcel overlay, check Zone AE outside the floodway, and find the records a permit review needs.
coverAlt: FEMA floodway overlay for Maricopa parcel 104-71-007C. About 2.70 acres are in the regulatory floodway and the remaining 0.09 acres are also in Zone AE.
coverCaption: Mapped areas on Maricopa County parcel 104-71-007C, calculated from county assessor geometry and the FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer retrieved November 25, 2026.
intro: To check a FEMA floodway before buying land, look up the effective flood map and overlap the regulatory floodway with the parcel and the proposed work. Check the pad, grading limits, utility lines and access roads separately. A Zone AE label tells you the property is in a mapped flood hazard area. The floodway boundary tells you where a different review of the proposed work may apply.
takeaways: Check the adopted floodway and the full area of proposed work, including off-site access and temporary construction.
Keep effective map records, the engineer’s review and any issued permit tied to the same plan revision.
For existing buildings, retain the applicable flood determination and elevation records alongside any approvals for later work.

guideActions.label: Check a parcel against FEMA maps

sections.heading: What is the difference between a floodway and a floodplain?

blocks.text: A regulatory floodway is the channel and adjoining land the community reserves to carry the base flood. The base flood has a 1% chance of occurring in a given year. The wider mapped Special Flood Hazard Area can include land outside the floodway. In FEMA’s National Flood Hazard Layer, two adjacent polygons can both be Zone AE while only one has the FLOODWAY subtype. Keep the zone and subtype in separate fields.

Check the community’s adopted map and any effective revisions for the decision date. Also ask which local floodplain layers or development rules apply. The mapped floodway acreage tells you where to investigate the proposed work. The permit file tells you which work the local authority reviewed.

sections.heading: A Maricopa parcel shows why the Zone AE label is too broad for site design

blocks.text: In the zoning packet for case Z260017, Maricopa County describes a 2.79-acre parcel near 67th Avenue and Southern Avenue and says the Salt River floodway covers more than 95% of the site. The proposed use was a single billboard. The engineering conditions called for a floodway analysis and a no-rise certification before building permit issuance.

We matched APN 104-71-007C to the assessor polygon, then intersected it with effective FEMA polygons. Panel 04013C2190M has an effective date of November 4, 2015. The map was retrieved November 25, 2026. The download preserves the query URLs and calculated areas, with the area calculation in NAD83 / UTM zone 12N. The county packet supplies the separate planning record.

rows: Whole parcel
2.787 acres
100% within mapped Zone AE
Regulatory floodway
2.696 acres
96.7% of parcel area; FEMA polygon 04013C_4523
Special Flood Hazard Area outside the floodway
0.091 acres
3.3% of parcel area; still Zone AE, FEMA polygon 04013C_4519

blocks.text: Before treating the 0.09 acres as a place to build, check where the proposed foundation and its grading, access and utilities would go. A small piece of land outside the floodway can still be in the mapped hazard area and may have its own development constraints. The zoning packet gives a proposed use and engineering conditions. Confirm the issued permit and the construction drawings with the county.

blocks.label: Download the parcel and mapped floodway intersection

sections.heading: What does a no-rise certification establish?

blocks.text: Under 44 CFR 60.3(d)(3), participating communities with an adopted regulatory floodway generally must prohibit encroachments unless hydraulic and hydrologic analysis shows the proposal would cause no increase in flood levels during the base flood. The one-foot provision in paragraph (d)(2) describes how a floodway is selected. The review of individual encroachments follows paragraph (d)(3). For proposals that would raise the base flood elevation, paragraph (d)(4) and 44 CFR 65.12 describe a separate conditional revision process before local permitting.

Ask the floodplain administrator which analysis and records the local ordinance requires. For a project reviewed on a no-rise basis, obtain the engineering certification and supporting model results for the applicable plan, then check the local permit decision and conditions separately. For a conditional map revision, check the conditions and the status of any later effective revision.

The Lower Minnesota River Watershed District’s Kennaley’s Creek review shows why to include temporary work. A temporary construction bridge was outside the earlier permit scope. The district’s October 2024 memo records a new analysis comparing proposed permanent conditions with the temporary bridge in place. The modeled base-flood water surface did not change between those conditions. That finding was part of the amendment review for the specific crossing.

Parcel, existing buildings, proposed grading and fill, road crossings, utility routes and temporary work. Include off-site pieces.
Engineering review
Proposal revision, baseline and proposed model results, certification and any conditions. Confirm the work under review matches the plan being financed or purchased.
Permit and insurance records
Local permit and approvals, any effective FEMA revision, and the separate flood determination or building elevation records used for lending or coverage.

faqs.question: Is all land in Zone AE in a regulatory floodway?
faqs.answer: Zone AE can include land both inside and outside the regulatory floodway. Check the floodway subtype or adopted floodway layer on the effective map and compare it with your site plan.

faqs.question: Can a property be partly in a floodway?
faqs.answer: Yes. A mapped floodway can cross part of a parcel. Calculate overlap for the parcel and compare the actual construction limits, access and utilities with the same boundary.

faqs.question: What if only a driveway or a utility crossing is in the floodway?
faqs.answer: Include the work in the proposal you give the local floodplain administrator. Roads, utilities, grading and temporary crossings can require their own review even when the building footprint is clear of the mapped floodway.

title: How to Verify Rail Spur Service at an Industrial Site
description: Check whether an industrial rail spur can serve your facility. Compare recorded crossing rights, track inspection, carrier terms and the first delivered railcars.
coverAlt: A crossing reopened in Greensburg in December 2022. Union Pacific reported a completed track inspection in Pleasant Prairie on June 17, 2026. Seven railcars reached Sofidel in Inola on April 10, 2024.
coverCaption: Dates from the Indiana Department of Transportation, Union Pacific’s inspection record filed by Pleasant Prairie, and Tulsa Ports.
intro: To verify rail spur service, give the serving railroad the facility address, the track ID and the legal name of the shipper or consignee. Ask the railroad to confirm in writing which track it can serve, which agreement covers your company and what must happen before the first delivery. Then match the route to the survey and recorded access rights. A recent switching record or shipment to the same track establishes past use. Current terms establish what your operation can schedule.
takeaways: Trace the route from the carrier’s line to the exact spot where the car will be unloaded.
Match ownership, operating rights and track maintenance to the correct agreement and segment.
Record crossing reopening, inspection, contract completion and accepted shipments as separate events.

guideActions.label: Screen rail access at a site

sections.heading: What records prove a spur can serve your facility?

blocks.text: A spur is a track that branches from a railroad line to reach a facility. Tell the carrier what you want to ship, the type and loaded weight of each car, and the number of cars per switch. A switch is the carrier’s move that places or picks up cars at the facility. The carrier can then confirm the track, who performs that move and what capacity it will accept.

rows: Route and access
Survey, track diagram, deeds and easements from the carrier’s line to the unloading spot.
Identify each parcel and crossing the cars must pass through. Resolve any segment the seller cannot show the right to use.
Shipper and serving carrier
Current track agreement or other written authorization covering your operating entity, plus carrier confirmation of the track and spot.
Establish who may receive cars and who is responsible for upkeep, access and repairs.
Readiness at the unloading spot
Latest track inspection, outstanding work, carrier acceptance of the car type and weight, and the switching schedule.
Confirm what the carrier can handle once the operation begins.
Recent operations
A dated switching record or a shipment record for the exact spot, with sensitive terms redacted as needed.
Confirm prior use. Obtain your own service terms before promising a first shipment.

blocks.text: Union Pacific’s policy covers new shipments to and from industrial tracks, including existing facilities used by other customers. It asks for an active agreement covering the shipper, consignee or other named party, or coverage under another customer’s agreement. Ask the serving carrier which rules apply to your facility and shipment.

sections.heading: Greensburg shows why the deed must cover the crossing

blocks.text: During a 2019 review of State Road 3 near Greensburg, Indiana DOT found that both sides of a roughly 1¾-mile spur had been deeded to Central Railroad of Indiana. The deed omitted the road crossing. Indiana DOT reported that Conrail retained the crossing right-of-way and that the reinstalled crossing reopened in December 2022.

The federal crossing inventory lists SR-3/SR-46 as record 916452T. Its July 21, 2025 revision lists the crossing as open. The state note links the reopening to reconstruction of the crossing surface. Ask for the recorded rights that cover the crossing and the carrier’s authority to serve the shipper at its unloading spot. The inventory documents the crossing and its reported status.

sections.heading: Pleasant Prairie separates inspection from project completion

blocks.text: The Village of Pleasant Prairie’s June 2025 update described about 1,994 feet of proposed track for Balcan USA. It named That’s a Wrap (WI) LLC as landowner and Balcan as tenant, with the village managing procurement and holding the rail infrastructure under the grant terms until the conditions could be met. These are the roles and terms the village described when the project was advancing.

On June 17, 2026, Union Pacific reported that the industry tracks were complete and inspected. The grant completion certificate lists June 30 as the date the contract work finished. It carries the project engineer’s July 3 signature and the WisDOT project coordinator’s July 21 signature. The October 26 village minutes record approval of a letter-of-credit reduction. Each date relates to a different decision. To date the first shipment, ask for a carrier or shipper record that identifies the cars delivered to Balcan’s spot.

sections.heading: Inola records the first delivery to a named shipper

blocks.text: Tulsa Ports reports that construction of the Verdigris Southern project finished on March 29, 2024, and that the first delivery brought seven railcars of raw materials to Sofidel on April 10. The Railroad Retirement Board dates the start of Verdigris Southern operations to April 9. Watco identifies Union Pacific as the interchange carrier at Inola.

The port describes a 4.4-mile construction project. The federal decision identifies a leased operating segment of approximately 13,883 feet, from the Union Pacific connection to an endpoint west of the S 4200 crossing. Use the endpoints in the applicable agreement when checking the track that serves your property. To qualify a different building at the port, confirm its track and shipper with the operator.

Screen the rest of the site

items.label: Check truck access and trailer capacity
Check whether the plant and yard fit

faqs.question: How can I tell if an industrial property is rail-served?
faqs.answer: Ask the serving carrier to identify the exact track and unloading spot, confirm your company is covered, and state what it can deliver and on which days. Verify that the route and rights cover the whole connection to the facility.

faqs.question: What does an open grade crossing establish?
faqs.answer: An open crossing record identifies where a road and railroad intersect and gives the status reported to the inventory. Check the track rights and carrier’s authorization for your shipper separately.

faqs.question: Can a new tenant use the previous occupant’s rail agreement?
faqs.answer: Ask the carrier who is covered. Union Pacific applies its track agreement policy when a new customer begins shipping at an existing facility. It can recognize a customer covered as a user under another valid track agreement.

title: How to Find CMBS Loan Collateral by Address
description: Use SEC filings to match 90 industrial properties across two CMBS schedules. Learn which figures describe the whole loan, each trust’s interest, and each property.
coverAlt: The $1.62 billion Mountain Industrial Portfolio whole loan consists of $1.1694 billion senior and $450.6 million junior notes. Three labeled figures show separate trust interests.
coverCaption: The trusts report portions of the senior loan in SEC-filed Benchmark, BANK5, and BMO offering documents.
intro: Start with the property address in a mortgage loan schedule. Use its parent loan row to find the whole-loan description and the notes held by the trust. The Mountain Industrial Portfolio appears in two SEC schedules with the same 90 industrial properties under different row numbers. The prospectuses disclose one $1.62 billion whole loan and several smaller trust interests. We matched the two public schedules so you can see which number belongs in each part of a credit file.
takeaways: Store the whole loan once and link each trust interest and property to it.
Match street address, city, state and ZIP across schedules. Retain both filing row IDs.
Keep property allocations, trust balances and current payoff figures in separate fields.

sections.heading: One whole loan appears in several trusts

blocks.text: A commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) trust may hold only some of the notes that make up a borrower’s loan. The Mountain Industrial Portfolio whole loan is secured by first mortgage liens on fee or leasehold interests in 90 industrial properties across 27 states. The filings report $1.1694 billion in senior notes and $450.6 million in junior notes.

rows: Mountain Industrial Portfolio whole loan
$1.620 billion
The combined obligation described in the offering documents.
Benchmark 2026-V22
$67.50 million
Loan row 1 in Annex A. This is the portion attached to this trust’s loan row.
BANK5 2026-5YR22
$81.50 million
Loan No. 2. The term sheet lists eight senior notes at the reporting date.
$45.75 million
Loan 4.00 in Exhibit A. Annex A identifies six notes from three sellers.

blocks.text: The three trust figures are components of the same senior financing. Store them with their own note and trust identifiers, and keep the whole-loan balance as a separate record. Both term sheets say servicing of the whole loan follows the MTN 2026-LPFX trust and servicing agreement. Check the latest servicer report when you need current exposure.

sections.heading: Match collateral across filings by address

blocks.text: Open the Benchmark Annex A and BMO Exhibit A. Filter each schedule to Mountain Industrial Portfolio, then match the property rows on the filed address, city, state and ZIP. We matched all 90 on those fields. The matching order put Benchmark 1.01 through 1.90 alongside BMO 4.01 through 4.90. The prefixes identify loans within their own schedules.

columns: Benchmark row and allocated cut-off balance
rows: 3150 Highway 42, Locust Grove, GA 30248
246 Glasson Drive, Corpus Christi, TX 78406
7569 Golf Course Boulevard, Punta Gorda, FL 33982

blocks.text: The 90 Benchmark property allocations sum to $67,499,997, or $3 below the published $67.5 million loan row. The schedule displays the property allocations in whole dollars. Preserve the individual values and the difference when you reconcile the file. BMO reports $45.75 million on the loan row and leaves its property balance cells blank. Keep those cells blank in your crosswalk.

A shared schedule can still contain separate mortgage groups. The term sheet says the Florida notes are directly secured by mortgages on Florida properties, and the other notes by mortgages on properties outside Florida. It also describes a guaranty of the Florida obligations from the non-Florida borrowers. In the crosswalk, Punta Gorda and Corpus Christi belong to different mortgage groups even though they are part of the same portfolio.

blocks.label: Download the 90-property CMBS collateral crosswalk

sections.heading: Follow note splits across dated filings

blocks.text: Read the whole-loan note tables as dated versions. The BANK5 filing on May 13, 2026 identifies a Wells Fargo note pair at $67 million and a UBS pair at $33.75 million. The BMO term sheet filed June 8 shows two new pairs under each of those prior note designations. The groups reconcile to the same principal in the two tables.

rows: Wells Fargo
$67 million in A-3-1-1-1 and A-4-1-1-1
$61 million in the pairs ending -2 and $6 million in the pairs ending -1. BMO lists the $6 million pair in its trust.
UBS
$33.75 million in A-3-6 and A-4-6
$27.75 million in the pairs ending -1 and $6 million in the pairs ending -2. BMO lists the $6 million pair in its trust.

blocks.text: Retain the prior note IDs and the filing dates alongside the successor IDs. A change in the number of note rows can leave the whole-loan principal unchanged. Confirm later amendments and transactions against the current documents before using these terms.

sections.heading: Which amount matters for a property release?

blocks.text: The Benchmark property figure allocates that trust’s reported balance. A release calculation uses the allocation defined in the loan documents and the loan balance at the applicable date. For Mountain Industrial, the BANK5 term sheet describes a release option from the May 11, 2028 payment date. Its formula uses 105% of the applicable allocation before the outstanding whole loan reaches the stated $1.134 billion threshold and 110% thereafter, subject to the outstanding balance cap. The term sheet also describes possible prepayment fees and conditions on debt yield and tax treatment.

The Corpus Christi and Punta Gorda properties illustrate another distinction. The term sheets identify both as ground leased by the borrower. Record whether the lien covers a fee or leasehold interest, then confirm the legal description and any later release with the recorded documents. For a closing, request a current release quote and the applicable loan provisions from the servicer.

items.label: Check whether a recorded release covers a parcel
Read commercial mortgage prepayment and defeasance terms

sections.heading: Build a collateral file you can reconcile

items: Start with the property address, then tie it to the parcel number and legal description. Keep the filing’s original address values.
Give the whole loan, note, trust interest, and property allocation separate IDs. Carry the filing date and the balance’s as-of date with each record.
Use the most recent documents to check modifications, releases and later note transfers. Save prior schedules so you can replay an earlier decision.
Join physical records such as building footprints and flood maps to the verified property. Keep the underlying geometry, edition and source separate from the financing records.

faqs.question: Where can I look up the properties securing a CMBS loan?
faqs.answer: Search SEC EDGAR for the trust and open its prospectus property annex or the schedule attached to a mortgage loan purchase agreement. Match the address to a property row and follow its parent loan ID to the whole-loan terms.

faqs.question: Why does the same property appear in more than one CMBS trust?
faqs.answer: Different trusts can hold separate notes from one whole loan. Their schedules can repeat the same collateral while reporting different trust-specific balances. The Benchmark and BMO schedules both list the 90 Mountain Industrial properties.

faqs.question: What is an allocated loan amount in a CMBS filing?
faqs.answer: It is the share of a reported loan balance assigned to a property for the purpose stated in the document. Check whether the figure allocates a trust interest or the whole loan. For a property release, look up the allocation and conditions defined by the loan agreement.

title: Commercial Property Statement of Values: How to Check an SOV
description: Download a commercial property statement of values workbook. Check duplicate rows, valuation bases and changes across three real renewal schedules.
coverAlt: Illustrative aerial view of a maintenance yard with several distinct buildings sharing one driveway.
coverCaption: Illustrative image of a public works yard, generated for this guide.
intro: A commercial property statement of values, or SOV, lists the buildings, contents and other property interests submitted for insurance, with the value and valuation basis for each. To validate it before quoting or renewing, match each line to the intended asset, reconcile amounts by coverage and keep each schedule edition. At one Appanoose County address, the same 12 printed lines recur across three terms while a handwritten fuel-tank entry changes form and value.
takeaways: Keep the carrier’s location ID, building ID and coverage code. One building can have multiple coverage rows, and one address can represent several buildings.
Separate replacement cost, actual cash value and policy limits. Preserve the value source and effective date for each line.
At Appanoose County’s 1200 IA-2 location, the 12 comparable printed lines rose by $88,800 from the 2022 to the 2023 schedule. A separately listed fuel-tank amount needs its own review.

sections.heading: What belongs in a commercial property statement of values?

blocks.text: Ask the insured or broker for the original schedule and its effective date. Keep the insured name, source document, location and building references, occupancy, construction, and the basis and date of each amount. When the program includes business income, record the worksheet and period behind that figure. Texas’s public risk program separates the building, contents and time-element values for its participants.

rows: Location and building identity
Record the address, site or campus name, location and building IDs, and any suite or structure designation. Verify the named building before assigning a parcel or footprint.
Building and contents values
Keep distinct rows or fields for the insured subjects. Record the currency, valuation basis, valuation date, and whether the figure comes from the insured, an appraisal, or another estimate.
Business income and extra expense
Record which location or operation the calculation covers, the time period, and any amount reported separately for extra expense.
Policy term and supporting records
Keep the schedule version and the issued declarations and endorsements. Check which document establishes the limit, deductible, sublimit, and valuation terms.

At 1200 IA-2 in Centerville, Iowa, the location-building IDs run from 3-1 to 3-8. For 3-6, the contents row begins at the bottom of the first schedule page. The address and building description continue on the next page before the truck wash bay and salt storage entries. The 12 rows below come from the printed table. The handwritten fuel-tank entry on the last page is tracked separately in the renewal comparison.

The Truck Garage and Truck Wash Bay each have a $41,000 building line, with different building IDs and valuation bases. A first-row-per-address import would keep $225,100 and omit $842,800 in submitted values. The $1,067,900 reconciliation is the sum of the selected schedule rows. Read the issued policy for the applicable limits and terms.

sections.heading: How to compare a statement of values across renewals

blocks.text: Start with the prior and proposed schedules. Match the location-building ID, coverage and valuation basis, then verify the address and description. Keep changes in the valuation basis in their own review queue. At 1200 IA-2, three Appanoose County board packets let you compare the same eight building IDs and 12 printed lines from the 2021 through 2023 terms.

rows: Building, actual cash value
Building, replacement cost
Contents, replacement cost
Sum of the same 12 lines

blocks.text: The fuel tanks share the address and carry ID 3-9 under business personal property. In the 2021 packet they appear as a $124,155 handwritten entry below the printed table. The 2022 packet has a similar handwritten entry with a blank amount. In 2023 the tanks appear in the printed table at $134,100, bringing that year’s printed subtotal for the address to $1,333,600.

Record the 2022 tank amount as unknown and keep the handwritten source for review. The $88,800 change measures the same 12 lines, and the $134,100 tank entry needs separate treatment. To establish when it was included and on what terms, request the final submitted schedules and applicable policy documents. Confirm the physical asset before adding hazard results.

sections.heading: Download a statement of values review workbook

blocks.text: Use the Review tab for up to 200 lines from one dated schedule in U.S. dollars. Enter the building ID, complete address, building or contents coverage code, valuation basis and submitted value. Use the same address spelling on related rows. Add the inspection, building plan or other match reference when you have it.

Review the flagged rows before using the totals. The workbook flags duplicate building, coverage and valuation combinations, conflicting addresses for one ID, and missing or invalid amounts. It keeps a recorded zero as a value and shows an empty total when a coverage and valuation combination has no included rows. A shared address and an open building match have their own columns.

Use the County example tab to see the review on a complete set of public rows for one location. The eight building IDs share one address. The workbook shows $398,300 in building actual cash value, $315,200 in building replacement cost and $354,400 in contents replacement cost. Each physical building match remains open until it has its own reference.

sections.heading: How to validate a statement of values before renewal

items: Retain the original submission and assign an immutable row ID to each imported line. Store the term and schedule version with carrier, location, building and coverage references.

Check for duplicate rows within the same version and coverage. Review repeat building IDs across coverage codes and shared addresses. Reconcile the row count and value totals to the original document before editing.
Match the physical building independently. Confirm the footprint or plan with the insured or the jurisdiction. Keep the public building ID and tax parcel ID as separate references.

Compare current COPE evidence with the submission. Verify construction, occupancy, protection and exposure for the building under review. Record the vintage and scope of each source, including whether the value describes a parcel, building or tenant space.

Compare renewals by subject and valuation basis. Record additions, removals, changed amounts and corrected attributes alongside the source and date. Obtain agreement from the insured or broker before adopting changes.

blocks.text: Use Invariant Earth to identify candidate parcels and retrieve building footprint attributes at a verified location. Compare the footprint with the source plan before adding hazard evidence to a schedule line. Keep the original value, source document and confirmed coverage with the submission. For a large portfolio, isolate uncertain building matches for review before running exposure totals.

sections.heading: Which number does the carrier or lender need?

blocks.text: A statement of values records submitted amounts by location and subject. The policy and endorsements establish how limits, deductibles and sublimits apply. Ask the broker to confirm the valuation basis for the line in question, especially where a blanket program includes differently valued property. The New York Department of Financial Services’ approved evidence form points readers back to the policy terms.

For a financed property, reconcile the collateral buildings to the insurance schedule and confirm which policy and terms apply to them. In its multifamily guide, Fannie Mae asks lenders to review the schedule and geographic concentrations for blanket coverage. Treat the loan program and its current requirements as part of the review.

faqs.question: What is a statement of values in commercial insurance?
faqs.answer: A statement of values is the submitted list of property and values under review, organized by location, building and subject of insurance. It can include building and contents values and, where applicable, business income or extra expense. Use the issued policy documents to verify limits and terms.

faqs.question: How should I handle multiple buildings at one address in an SOV?
faqs.answer: Keep each building’s own identifier and preserve every applicable coverage row. Validate the building name and footprint against an independent reference before using building-level hazard and valuation data. Reconcile the resulting totals to the original schedule.

faqs.question: What is the difference between actual cash value and replacement cost on a statement of values?
faqs.answer: Replacement cost generally uses current repair or replacement costs. Actual cash value generally accounts for depreciation. Record which basis applies to each subject and check the issued policy terms. A single building can have entries on different bases for the structure and its contents.

faqs.question: How should I treat a blank amount on a renewal statement of values?
faqs.answer: Keep the row and mark the amount unknown. Compare the rest of the schedule on the same asset, coverage and valuation basis. Request the final schedule or policy documents to resolve the blank and keep the draft with your review evidence.

title: Commercial Property Loss Runs
description: Request commercial property loss runs, match claims to the insured building, and reconcile paid amounts and reserves across two dated carrier reports.
coverAlt: Two commercial warehouse buildings with distinct roofs on either side of a shared driveway.
coverCaption: Illustration of a two-building industrial property. The worked example uses fictional claims and locations.
intro: Get commercial property loss runs from the current and prior insurers through the insured or authorized broker. A loss run lists claims reported under the policies and periods it covers. To build a history for one property, match each claim to the insured building, then compare the paid amounts, reserves and status as of each report’s valuation date. A street address can get you to the property while leaving the building match unresolved.
takeaways: Ask for the policy terms under review, a dated valuation, the covered loss location and a report for each term, including terms the carrier confirms had no claims.
Use the location and building numbers on the schedule in effect when the loss occurred. Hold claims at a shared street address for review until a record identifies the building.
Read cumulative payments and outstanding reserves as of a date. Two reports on the same claim show how it developed over time.

sections.heading: How do you request commercial property loss runs?

blocks.text: Start with the property policies and terms your underwriter or lender wants reviewed. Give the carrier the named insured, policy numbers, periods and line of business. Ask for a spreadsheet for reconciliation and retain the original report. Travelers, for example, asks for the policy number, policy period, line of business and preferred format. The Hartford describes how its reports show reported claims and information such as the loss date, status and amounts paid.

For a purchase, ask the seller to obtain reports for its period of ownership and supply the location schedule that goes with each policy. Track the carriers and terms you have received, any confirmed claim-free terms, and any missing terms. Ask separately about known uninsured losses or repairs. A loss run covers reported claims within the report’s scope.

columns: Ask the carrier or broker for
rows: Policy number, term, line and named insured
Reconcile which parts of the insurance program the report covers. Keep primary and excess reports identified.
Loss date, reported date and valuation date
Choose the location schedule covering the loss and interpret the balance as of the report valuation.
Claim ID, status, cause and coverage component
Track the same claim through later reports and distinguish building damage from contents or business interruption.
Risk location, building or schedule number
Check where the claim occurred and whether the carrier identifies a particular structure.
Paid, outstanding reserve and incurred amounts
Use the report’s definitions for loss, expenses and recoveries before comparing insurers or periods.

blocks.text: Capture the date you received each report, too. A September 30 valuation received October 3 describes the carrier’s position as of September 30. The October 3 receipt date establishes when that evidence became available to your team.

sections.heading: How do you match a loss run to the right building?

blocks.text: Open the statement of values or policy location schedule in effect on the loss date. Match on carrier location and building IDs when the report supplies them. Check the named insured, location address, building descriptor and any endorsements that changed the schedule. A current parcel or footprint can help resolve the physical location. Save the evidence that connects it to the insurance record.

For a campus, keep one row per insured building even when the buildings share a tax parcel or street address. When a report identifies only the campus, keep the claim at that level until the carrier, adjuster or a linked record identifies the building. Keep business interruption and other amounts at the level the report supports. A facility-wide item may require its own allocation review.

Invariant Earth helps you match an address or point to a parcel and check building footprints, site context and dated hazard sources. Carry the matching evidence into your underwriting file alongside the authorized carrier report. Retain the original carrier location and building references so someone can audit the match.

Check the Earth API’s property and hazard fields

sections.heading: How do you reconcile the same claim across two reports?

blocks.text: Consider a fictional industrial property with two buildings at one shared address. The policy lists Building A and Building B separately. The June and September reports both identify the April water damage claim as Building A. The September report also shows an August claim at the shared address without a building number.

rows: June 30, EX-17, Building A
September 30, EX-17, Building A
September 30, EX-23, building unresolved

blocks.text: EX-17 had $50,000 more in cumulative payments by September. Its outstanding reserve fell by $70,000, so reported incurred loss fell by $20,000. For this example, incurred loss equals cumulative paid loss plus outstanding loss reserve. Carrier reports can treat expenses or recoveries differently. Compare the same coverage component on the same accounting basis, and keep the carrier’s reported incurred figure with its definition.

The September report supports $80,000 for Building A and $12,000 pending building assignment. Building B’s claim history remains unresolved in this example. The two EX-17 rows are separate observations of one claim. Use the latest applicable observation for a current total and retain the earlier one to explain the change.

blocks.label: Download the illustrative loss run reconciliation

blocks.text: The CSV keeps the source site and building labels, matched building ID, loss date, valuation date and receipt date. In a real portfolio, retain the carrier, policy, claim ID and coverage component so you can distinguish repeated observations from separate amounts. Group revised or reopened claims under the carrier’s documented identifiers.

faqs.question: Can you look up commercial property insurance claims by address?
faqs.answer: Underwriters with authorized access can use certain commercial loss history products to search by risk location. For a specific building or acquisition, obtain the relevant carrier loss runs through the insured or broker and match claims to the policy location schedule. Public flood claim releases withhold exact insured addresses.

faqs.question: What is the valuation date on a loss run?
faqs.answer: The valuation date is the date as of which the report shows claim status and financial amounts. Record it alongside the loss and receipt dates. Use the applicable valuation when comparing an older underwriting decision with a later report.

faqs.question: How many years of commercial property loss runs should you request?
faqs.answer: Ask the receiving insurer or lender which policy terms it wants to review. For an acquisition, also ask the seller which periods it can document. Track each requested term and mark the terms that are missing or that the carrier confirms had no reported claims.

faqs.question: What is the difference between incurred and paid loss on a loss run?
faqs.answer: Paid loss is the amount already paid on the reporting basis. An incurred figure often includes paid loss and the remaining loss reserve. Check how the report handles expenses and recoveries, and compare totals based on the same definitions.

region: Seattle, Washington, and Scottsdale, Arizona, United States
title: How to Find Fire Hydrant Flow Test Results by Address
description: Find hydrant flow and pressure records for a commercial property. Verify a Seattle water-main estimate and reproduce a Scottsdale test’s 4,392 gpm figure at 20 psi.
coverAlt: Scottsdale hydrant test curve. During the test, flow was 1,244 gallons per minute at 76 psi residual pressure. The extrapolated flow at 20 psi was 4,392 gallons per minute.
coverCaption: Invariant plotted the August 18, 2021 hydrant test in Scottsdale case 21-DR-2021. The dashed curve uses the pressure-drop calculation. The test itself reached 76 psi residual pressure.
intro: To find a fire hydrant flow test for a commercial property, identify the serving water utility and ask for a dated report tied to the building and proposed connection. Check which hydrant flowed, where pressure was recorded, how much water flowed, and which values were calculated. A utility map can help screen a site before you request the report.
takeaways: A hydrant map answers where to look. A flow report records conditions and readings for a named test. The applicable fire code separately sets how much flow and duration a building needs.
The closest mapped hydrant to Seattle’s Fishermen’s Terminal reference point showed 4,300 gpm of modeled water-main capacity. The site point was 122 metres away in a straight line.
The Scottsdale report recorded 1,244 gpm flowing at 76 psi residual and calculated 4,392 gpm at 20 psi. Keep both values with their evidence type.

sections.heading: Where can you get a fire hydrant flow test by address?

blocks.text: Start with the water utility’s development services or engineering office. Give the exact building address, parcel, proposed fire service connection and permit number where available. Ask whether it has an existing report for the relevant pressure zone and test location. A public permitting file may contain an older report alongside a site plan or sprinkler design.

rows: Utility hydrant map
Asset location and published status
Asset or source record ID and observation date
Hydraulic model result
Estimated main capacity under the model’s demand and pressure assumptions
Model date, pressure criteria, location and units
Hydrant flow test report
Flow and pressure readings under the test conditions, plus any calculated flow at a target pressure
Test date and time, hydrant IDs, static and residual pressures, observed flow and any extrapolation
Fire-code review or sprinkler permit
The demand and evidence required for a specific design submission
Building scope, approved design revision, required flow and duration, and any conditions

sections.heading: What does the Seattle hydrant map tell you?

blocks.text: At Fishermen’s Terminal, we queried Seattle Public Utilities’ modeled capacity layer within 300 metres of the Port’s reference coordinate. The query returned 14 records. These are the three closest by straight-line distance to that point. The reference describes the terminal. Confirm the actual building and accessible route before selecting a hydrant for review.

The records show a March 6, 2025 model date and use 2021 maximum-day demands. The layer takes the lower of two modeled flows. One preserves 20 psi at the upstream end of the hydrant lateral. The other preserves at least 5 psi across the pressure zone. These values refer to the main at the lateral connection. To assess simultaneous flow, ask the utility to model the hydrants together under the relevant demand conditions.

sections.heading: How did a 1,244 gpm test become 4,392 gpm at 20 psi?

blocks.text: Scottsdale’s public case 21-DR-2021 includes a Metro Fire Equipment test from August 18, 2021 at 11107 North Scottsdale Road. The report lists 82 psi static pressure before the test flow, 76 psi residual pressure during flow, and 55 psi pitot pressure at the outlet. The readings describe different points in the test. Use the static and residual values together to compute the drop in main pressure.

Using the recorded 2.5-inch outlet, 0.90 discharge coefficient and 55 psi pitot pressure gives 1,244.39 gpm. Multiply that unrounded result by ((82 − 20) ÷ (82 − 76)) raised to 0.54. The result is 4,391.84 gpm, which rounds to the report’s 4,392 gpm. The observed pressure fell by 6 psi. The 20 psi projection uses a 62 psi drop, so the points in the report carry materially different evidence.

For an actual design or renewal, ask whether the utility and reviewing authority accept that test for the project’s date and demand. Keep the test location, water system, observed conditions and pressure basis with the estimate. Pumps, demand and elevations can change the pressure available at a building connection.

blocks.label: Download the Seattle lookup and Scottsdale calculation

sections.heading: What belongs in the design or underwriting file?

blocks.text: For most Seattle fire sprinkler permit applications, the Fire Prevention Division asks for an official Fire Flow Availability Report. Its guidance says an actual test within 500 feet of the parcel and within the last five years can qualify for the report at no charge. The city describes a separate path for certain NFPA 13D designs. For construction plan review the city can use its own databases. Confirm the applicable request before planning around turnaround times.

Keep approved fire-flow demand and duration beside the available supply for the same building, project phase and connection. For insurance, obtain the carrier’s accepted protection class for the exact premises. Fire station response, a creditable hydrant, and the building’s own sprinkler inspection or acceptance records answer separate questions.

faqs.question: Is the fire hydrant capacity on a map a flow test?
faqs.answer: A map may show a model estimate or a link to a dated test. In Seattle’s water-main capacity layer, the reported value comes from a hydraulic model at the hydrant lateral’s upstream connection. A flow test report records the test location, flow, pressures and conditions.

faqs.question: What is the difference between static and residual pressure?
faqs.answer: Static pressure is the main pressure before water is discharged for the test. Residual pressure is the main pressure while the selected outlets flow. Pitot pressure at the flowing outlet is used to calculate how much water flows during the test.

faqs.question: Can I use an older hydrant test for a sprinkler permit?
faqs.answer: Ask the reviewing authority which test dates and locations it accepts. For Seattle, request the official report from the utility. The city describes a no-cost route where it has an actual test within five years and within 500 feet of the parcel.

title: Florida Hurricane Insurance Claims Data by County
description: Find Florida hurricane claims by county and statewide insured losses by line. Compare Helene and Milton with dated records and a downloadable reconciliation.
coverAlt: Hurricane Milton commercial property claims in Florida as of December 9, 2025. Of 23,901 claims, 12,541 were open, 4,154 were closed with payment, and 7,206 were closed without payment.
coverCaption: Hurricane Milton, statewide commercial property line. Invariant grouped the four statuses in the December 9, 2025 Florida OIR snapshot into three categories.
intro: Florida’s Office of Insurance Regulation publishes hurricane claim counts and statuses by county. Its separate statewide tables show estimated incurred losses by insurance line. Use the county views to decide where to investigate first, and keep the storm, reporting date, and insurance line with every figure. The summaries describe a market. For a particular building, obtain the property’s own loss history.
takeaways: County rows show counts and reported statuses across lines. The published commercial property incurred total is statewide.
Hurricane Milton’s December 9, 2025 snapshot lists 23,901 commercial property claims and about $1.03 billion incurred, including payments and case reserves.
Calculate closure percentages from all reported claims. To compare nonpayment among closed claims, use only closed claims in the denominator.

sections.heading: Where to find hurricane claims by county

blocks.text: The Florida OIR publishes separate reporting dates for each storm. Pinellas leads the named counties in the Helene snapshot. Hillsborough leads the named counties in the Milton snapshot. The table uses four counties that the agency names in both releases.

blocks.text: Use these counts as event-specific context for a portfolio or a market. The snapshots have different reporting dates and cover the reported lines combined. Check the agency’s other-counties group before drawing conclusions about a county without a named row.

sections.heading: What the reported commercial property loss includes

blocks.text: OIR describes case-incurred loss as payments to date plus indemnity case reserves. For Milton, the agency reports $1,028,401,242 statewide for commercial property across 23,901 claims. Of those, 12,541 remained open at that date. Helene’s June report shows $708,838,483 across 7,137 commercial property claims. These figures are insurer-reported estimates at their respective dates.

rows: Open with payment
A payment appears in the reported status and the claim remains open.
Open without payment
The claim remains open at the report date.
Closed with payment
The insurer reports closure with payment.
Closed without payment
The insurer reports closure without payment. Review the separate reason data for context.

blocks.text: The two closed categories sum to 11,360, or 47.5% of the 23,901 reported commercial property claims. The 7,206 closed without payment represent 63.4% of the closed group. A report can accurately show both percentages because they answer different questions.

OIR separately lists reasons such as damage below the deductible and administrative closure. In the selected Milton table, the commercial property reason counts sum to 7,590, while the status table shows 7,206 closed without payment. Keep the reason rows as a separate aggregate. Use the status table to calculate the nonpayment share.

sections.heading: Which records belong in the underwriting file?

items: For county exposure, save the storm, county, scope of the claim count, reporting date and source. Match the property to that geography before comparing it with the portfolio.
For commercial losses, use the statewide line and record which amount is incurred or paid. Use the county table for all-line claim statuses.
For flood, keep Florida’s private flood category separate from the federal NFIP dataset. Each source measures a different insurance population.

For a building, request the relevant loss runs from the owner or carrier through an authorized channel. Check the covered location, claim date, cause of loss and valuation date alongside the inspection and repair evidence.

faqs.question: Can I look up hurricane insurance claims for a specific address in the Florida OIR tables?
faqs.answer: The public storm tables report aggregates by county and statewide line. Ask the owner or carrier for the location-specific loss runs and verify the covered building before using them in underwriting.

faqs.question: How much did Hurricane Milton cost Florida commercial property insurers?
faqs.answer: Florida OIR reported $1,028,401,242 in statewide commercial property case-incurred losses as of December 9, 2025. The estimate includes payments to date and indemnity case reserves.

faqs.question: What does closed without payment mean in a hurricane claims report?
faqs.answer: It is the insurer’s reported closure status. Examples include damage below the deductible, coverage exclusions, withdrawals or administrative closure. Use the report’s dated reason table for context.
