title: EV Charger Uptime, Availability, and Charge Success Data
description: Compare EV charger uptime, live port availability and successful charges. Recalculate the California field-test results and see what data to request from a network.
coverAlt: California DC fast charging field tests. There were 1,610 successful charges across 1,754 plug-in tests, or 91.8 percent. Among the 1,712 operational ports tested, that was 94.0 percent.
coverCaption: The same 1,610 successful charges produce two results depending on which tests are included. CEC staff report CEC-600-2026-034 and Appendix B.
intro: Use live port status to see whether a compatible charger is free now. Use a dated port history to measure uptime, and session results to see whether attempts succeed. Those feeds answer different questions. In a recent California field study, 1,610 fast-charge tests succeeded. That is 94.0% of plug-in tests at operational ports and 91.8% of all fast-charge plug-in tests in the sample.
takeaways: Request timestamps and stable port IDs alongside live status so a routing app can tell when a status is stale.
Calculate uptime over time using the applicable rules. Keep observed test success separate and show its denominator.
The California sample records ports testers could not access. Keep congestion, obstruction and access restrictions visible in route planning.

sections.heading: Which EV charging metric answers your question?

rows: Live availability
Can a compatible vehicle use a port right now?
Port ID, connector, current status, last update and access hours.
Annual uptime
How much of the reporting period did this port meet the applicable definition of operational?
Dated intervals, outage minutes, exclusions, reporting window and missing data policy.
Charge attempt success
How often did a vehicle successfully charge in the attempts counted?
Outcome events by port and session, with the denominator and recorded failure types.
Field operational rate
What share of ports in the sample were judged operational at the visit?
Visit method, accessed sample, and any weighting applied to uncertain observations.

sections.heading: What California’s charger field tests found

blocks.text: UC Davis tested and observed public charging ports between January 2024 and February 2026. California Energy Commission staff used 3,571 plug-in tests and 12,586 visual-only observations to calculate a field operational rate. Its charge attempt success rate, or SCAR, uses plug-in tests at ports the study classified as operational.

rows: Ports researchers tried to access
Accessed ports used for the field operational rate
Published field operational rate
Published SCAR, among operational plug-in tests
Success across all plug-in tests, calculated from the appendix

blocks.text: For fast charging, the study records 42 confirmed nonoperational ports in the plug-in test group and 102 failed charge tests at operational ports. Removing the 42 from the denominator gives the published SCAR. Including them gives the all-test success share. The visual-only visits and the 615 fast ports testers could not access have their own counts. Neither group belongs in the plug-in success denominator.

blocks.label: Download the reported counts and reliability calculations

blocks.text: Missing access can still spoil a trip. In the fast-charge sample, congestion prevented access to 244 ports and obstructions accounted for another 305. For a route or fleet, record those events separately from the network’s technical outage status.

The first assigned payment method failed in 17.7% of the study’s attempts. The reported rates were 34.4% for credit or debit cards, 2.3% for plug-in payment and 14.0% for other methods. Testers could try another method after a failure, and one closed-network provider dominated the plug-in payment sample. For a fleet, test the actual payment method and account before using those results to judge a stop.

sections.heading: What does the 97% EV charger uptime rule measure?

blocks.text: Federal rules require greater than 97% average annual uptime per port for covered projects, including NEVI Formula Program projects. The calculation looks back 12 months, is performed monthly and has specified outage exclusions. Review the project’s funding and applicable rules before using the threshold.

California also has a 97% per-port standard for certain publicly funded DC fast chargers. Coverage depends on funding, installation date and whether the ports exclusively serve a fleet. The California field-test report gives observations and charge outcomes. Demonstrating compliance for an individual port requires the reporting-period records and applicable exclusions.

sections.heading: What to ask for when choosing a network or data feed

items: For navigation, join station coordinates and access hours to current connector and port status. Give the driver a backup stop when the status is stale or the stall may be blocked.
For a fleet, verify vehicle compatibility and physical access along the route. Track payment failures, congestion and successful sessions separately so the team can diagnose disruptions.
For a site host, ask for per-port outage logs and the time, reason and evidence behind every exclusion. Keep the contract’s uptime definition with the reported number.
For expansion planning, compare actual port performance with access, traffic, land and power availability. Keep parcel and utility evidence attached to the site.

faqs.question: Is an available EV charger counted as a successful charge?
faqs.answer: A current status reports how the port is classified at that moment. A successful charge requires a session outcome showing the vehicle charged. Payment or vehicle-to-charger communication failures can interrupt an attempt at an operational port.

faqs.question: Can I estimate charger uptime from public field visits?
faqs.answer: Field visits measure the conditions observed at the visit. To calculate uptime, use a port history over the required period and apply the relevant outage and exclusion rules.

faqs.question: Are the California statistics reports for individual stations?
faqs.answer: The figures here come from statewide sampled field tests. For a specific station, match its operator and port IDs to dated availability, session and outage records.

title: How to Find UCC Fixture Filings and Terminations by Address
description: Look up UCC fixture filings by address and trace UCC-3 terminations to the original file number. Download a worked example from New York City’s ACRIS index.
coverAlt: Two historical Empire State Building fixture filing records. UCC-3 97TN06679 points to 93PN46191, and 97TN06680 points to 93PN46192.
coverCaption: Historical City Register cross-references for Manhattan block 835, lot 41. Both terminations were recorded June 25, 1997.
intro: Start a fixture filing search by matching the address to the legal parcel. Pull the filings indexed to that parcel and follow each amendment, continuation or termination back to its original file number. In New York City, the ACRIS personal property tables link filings, tax lots and recorded references. General UCC searches can also require the debtor’s exact legal name in a separate state index.
takeaways: Match the borough, block and lot before reviewing fixture filings. The same building can appear under several street numbers.
A UCC-3 can reflect several actions. Identify the document type and the file number it affects.
Two Empire State Building terminations share a recording date. Each references a different initial fixture filing.

sections.heading: Where to search for a UCC fixture filing

blocks.text: A fixture filing is a financing statement filed in the real property records for goods that are or will become fixtures. Under New York’s current filing rules, the filing office generally follows the real estate recording office for a fixture filing. A financing statement filed centrally against an entity may require a separate debtor-name search. The law provides a separate filing rule for transmitting utilities.

For Manhattan, Brooklyn, the Bronx and Queens, use ACRIS to confirm the tax lot and find City Register documents. Also check the mortgage documents. A duly recorded mortgage can serve as a fixture filing when it satisfies the statutory requirements.

sections.heading: How the Empire State Building filings match

blocks.text: The landmarks designation identifies 350 Fifth Avenue as Manhattan block 835, lot 41. The selected historical ACRIS entries show 336 Fifth Avenue. MapPLUTO lists 338 Fifth Avenue for the same lot. The three records agree on the parcel identifier, BBL 1008350041, so the street numbers can remain visible as source values.

The selected master records use collateral code F for fixture filings. Joining the references to the master by document ID gives the initial filing number, the action on the later record and its recording date.

rows: 93PN46191 · September 13, 1993
97TN06679 · UCC-3 termination recorded June 25, 1997
The termination references 93PN46191 and its exact document ID.
93PN46192 · September 13, 1993

The termination references 93PN46192 and its exact document ID.
88PN67956 · December 19, 1988

The continuation references the original filing. The termination references both.

blocks.text: Another initial filing, 93PN46193, shares the 1993 recording date and the same lot. The two 1997 termination rows point to the other filings, so this sample leaves the status of 93PN46193 undetermined. Match the number on the actual document before using a termination in a review.

blocks.label: Download the eight fixture records and exact ACRIS cross-references

blocks.text: The download preserves the original recording, modification and good-through dates. For example, each of the 1997 termination rows has a June 25 recording date and a July 3 modification date. The good-through date describes the extract, so retain it with the source version.

sections.heading: What a lender or buyer should verify before closing

items: Confirm the legal parcel and the equipment included in the sale or financing. Read the collateral description and the real property description on the original document.
Follow the first filing number through assignments, continuations, amendments and terminations. Record each action’s scope and the party shown on the instrument.
Search the relevant additional indexes, including recorded mortgages and the state debtor-name index where applicable. Check the exact legal names of the entities involved.
Use current, certified filing records for a closing decision. Ask counsel or the title team to confirm filing effectiveness, priority and the documents needed to release the specific collateral.

blocks.text: Under New York’s current rules, the ordinary term for a filed financing statement is five years, with specific exceptions and a statutory continuation window. A qualifying mortgage recorded as a fixture filing follows a different duration rule. A filed termination acts on the financing statement it identifies, subject to the statute’s authorization rules. The public index gives a starting point for finding that document.

faqs.question: Can I search all UCC filings by property address?
faqs.answer: Use the address to find the legal parcel and search for real-property-related filings. Search the appropriate state index by debtor name for filings recorded there. The filing office and the collateral determine where to look.

faqs.question: What does a UCC-3 termination relate to?
faqs.answer: It identifies a particular financing statement. Confirm the referenced initial file number and the filed document before recording the result in a diligence file.

faqs.question: Can a mortgage also serve as a UCC fixture filing?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under New York UCC § 9-502(c), a duly recorded mortgage can serve as a fixture filing when it identifies the covered goods and real property and meets the specified requirements.

title: Building Permit Change Alerts by Address
description: Track building permits by address or nearby radius. Compare issue dates, recent portal loads and county totals, with queries from the San Francisco permit feed.
coverAlt: Three dates for the permit at 345 California Street. The permit was issued on December 1, 2020, showed an expired status dated October 28, 2026, and was loaded to DataSF on October 30, 2026.
coverCaption: Three dates for San Francisco DBI permit 202009234825. All four address rows carry the same permit dates and October 30 portal load date.
intro: To get alerts for building permits at or near an address, identify the lots you want to watch and check the issuing agency’s permit feed. Use the issue date for a new permit alert and keep the portal load date so you can see when the record appeared. In one San Francisco example, 34 distinct permits within 300 meters had November issue dates, while 103 had rows loaded in the same period. The right filter depends on whether you want new authorizations or recently loaded records.
takeaways: Use the permit number and issuing system to count permits. Keep the linked address, unit and parcel rows for property matching.
A San Francisco permit issued in 2020 shows an expired status dated October 28, 2026. DataSF loaded the row on October 30.
Use an issued permit to check what work the agency authorized. Use a final inspection or closeout record for decisions that require completed work.

sections.heading: What changed at the property?

blocks.text: We checked two San Francisco Department of Building Inspection permits and one PermitSF record on November 24, 2026. The Department of Building Inspection publishes a row per permit and associated address record. Separate rows can carry the same permit number. PermitSF publishes a separate extract for its online permit types.

sections.heading: How to get alerts for building permits near an address

blocks.text: Choose a distance and a milestone. For new authorizations, filter by the permit issue date. To catch records the portal recently published or refreshed, also check the load timestamp and compare each result with the last saved version. For a neighboring parcel, confirm the lot boundary. Nearby address points can be on either side of a street or several properties away.

We used the city’s published point for 345 California Street and queried its building permit extract on November 25, 2026. The table compares the displayed issue and load dates from November 1 through November 25, inclusive. The city’s permit locations are associated with its assessor block and lot. The queries include only records with a mapped point inside the radius.

rows: 2 permits across 2 rows
9 permits across 9 rows
34 permits across 35 rows
103 permits across 109 rows

blocks.text: Within 300 meters, the issue-date query returned 34 distinct permit numbers. Two rows for permit 202611130735 at 353 Sacramento Street account for the 35th row. They carry different lot identifiers under the same permit. Notify once for the November 20 issuance and retain both lot links.

The load-date query returned 103 distinct permit numbers within 300 meters. One row at 345 California Street was loaded on November 25 even though its issue and status dates were January 21. At 350 California Street, the same November 25 load included two different permit numbers still marked filed. Those records belong in a recently loaded activity view. A new-issuance alert should use the issue date.

To answer what was permitted next door, look up the adjoining parcels in the city’s parcel map and join by block and lot. For an area watchlist, keep the radius and center with the query. Give each notification a stable identity based on the issuing system, permit number and dated milestone, and make the original record available from the alert.

sections.heading: What do county building permit totals count?

blocks.text: Use county building permit totals to compare how much new housing was authorized. Use the city’s permit number and dated activity to monitor a specific property. The Census Building Permits Survey covers new privately owned housing. Its annual county file counts buildings and housing units in separate columns.

rows: Housing units authorized
Residential buildings authorized
Housing units in buildings with five or more units
Single-family housing units authorized

blocks.text: Authorized housing units rose 87.5% while the count of residential buildings fell 24.1%. The increase came from buildings with five or more units. For a market report, retain the county FIPS code, year, structure size and whether the measure is units or buildings. For an alert on a sprinkler permit, roof permit, or completion date, query the local record for that address.

sections.heading: How to monitor permit changes across a portfolio

items: Match the address, building and unit. Use municipal parcel and building identifiers where they exist. Preserve multiple property links for permits that cover several addresses.
Save the issuing system, permit ID, milestone dates, current status, and the time you retrieved the record. Keep the source response available for review.

Query the publisher’s update timestamp with an overlapping time window. Compare relevant fields against the last saved version. A newly downloaded row only establishes a new observation until the dated fields or earlier version support an event.

Send one notification per permit, milestone type and recorded event time. Attach the properties affected by that milestone. Surface later corrections on the original event and keep the prior value for review.
Backfill from known dated fields and label history gaps. Share the source, permit ID, event date and observation time with every alert.

blocks.text: DataSF provides separate times for the source record update and the portal load. Store both as returned and keep your own retrieval time with its UTC offset. A batch load can bring in several older milestones. The source values in this example are floating timestamps, so they carry no offset.

sections.heading: Which permit changes are worth a notification?

blocks.text: An owner managing a tenant build-out may want to know when a permit issues and when the final inspection closes. A construction lender can use those events to queue a draw review alongside the loan’s other requirements. An underwriter assessing roof age needs the permit’s work scope and evidence that the claimed replacement was completed. Set the notification around the decision each team has to make.

Start with the building and parcel identifiers. Invariant Earth can help match the property and its mapped features. Use the issuing agency’s dated permit and inspection records for the milestones, and confirm the update cadence for each jurisdiction before committing to an alert schedule.

faqs.question: How can I get notified when the city issues a building permit next to a property I own?
faqs.answer: Identify the property and adjoining lot IDs, then check for newly issued permits in the city’s permit feed. You can use a radius for a wider watchlist. Filter on issue date and deduplicate the permit number before sending a notification. Use portal load time to pick up records that arrived late or were refreshed.

faqs.question: Can an old building permit trigger a new alert?
faqs.answer: Yes. A recent status change can affect a permit issued years earlier. Confirm the date of the change from the issuing agency and keep the source update and publication times with the notification.

faqs.question: Does a permit marked issued show that the work is complete?
faqs.answer: Issuance records the authorization. For completed work, look for a final inspection or approved closeout for the work in question. San Francisco publishes issue and completion dates separately.

faqs.question: How do you avoid duplicate permit alerts?
faqs.answer: Keep separate row identifiers for addresses and lots. Group by issuing system and permit number, then notify once per dated milestone with links to the affected properties.

title: How to Find an Elevation Certificate by Address
description: Find a flood elevation certificate by address or permit. Use a Myrtle Beach case to check the building, floor and floodproofing elevations, and FEMA map data.
coverAlt: Elevation comparison for Building 3 at 2519 Vacation Drive, ranging from the loading dock at 10 feet to equipment at 16.2 feet on the NAVD88 datum.
coverCaption: Building 3 at 2519 Vacation Drive, Myrtle Beach. The chart uses elevations transcribed from Horry County permit 136756.
intro: Search the local floodplain or permit portal by street address. Some counties organize scanned elevation certificates under the parcel number or building permit. Ask the local floodplain manager for the finished-construction certificate for the specific building. An elevation certificate records surveyed heights. The current flood map, any map amendments and the applicable policy answer separate questions.
takeaways: Match the certificate to the building and permit before using a survey from a shared parcel.
Compare heights in the same units and vertical datum. Keep the floor, equipment, grade and floodproofing levels as separate fields.
A mapped Zone AE result can have an empty static base flood elevation field. Keep that field empty and check the panel or study for the applicable flood elevation.

sections.heading: Where can I look up an elevation certificate?

blocks.text: Start with the city or county that issued the building permit. Lee County, Florida, provides a property search and links to elevation certificates where it has one on file. Horry County, South Carolina, publishes a certificate list by permit number. When the address search fails, use the parcel ID to look up the building permit, then request the certificate from the local floodplain office.

Match the structure shown in Section A to the building being insured, including the building number and photographs. Review the construction stage in Section C before using the measured values. A file based on drawings or work in progress can differ from the final survey. When records are missing or the structure has changed, ask the local office or insurer what documentation they need and whether a qualified professional should update it.

sections.heading: What did Horry County file for Building 3?

blocks.text: Permit 136756 contains an elevation certificate for the non-residential Building 3 at 2519 Vacation Drive. The certificate was signed December 14, 2022 and marks finished construction. It lists FEMA panel 45051C0704K with a December 16, 2021 effective date and a base flood elevation (BFE) of 13 feet. The packet also includes a separate floodproofing certificate.

rows: Base flood elevation on the certificate
Elevation certificate, B9

Elevation certificate, C2(e)

blocks.text: On the common vertical datum, the floor was 1.0 foot above the BFE on the certificate. The certified floodproofing elevation was 2.0 feet above that same BFE. The floodproofing form also records 1.0 foot above lowest adjacent grade, while the elevation certificate locates its 10.0-foot lowest grade at a recessed loading dock. Keep these entries as filed and ask which grade the floodproofing form used before applying a height above grade.

sections.heading: What does a current map lookup confirm?

blocks.text: We queried the county’s flood zone and panel layers at the survey coordinates recorded in Section A. The county returned Zone AE and panel 45051C0704K. The polygon’s static BFE field returned −9999 with the datum and unit blank. That field supplies no numerical flood elevation at the point. The 13-foot figure in this example comes from the filed certificate, so confirm the applicable elevation in the effective map or flood insurance study before using it for a new decision.

faqs.question: Can you get a copy of an elevation certificate online?
faqs.answer: Some city and county portals link the recorded PDF to an address, parcel or permit. Ask the local floodplain manager or the building owner when it is missing from the portal.

faqs.question: Does a FEMA flood zone lookup show the building’s first floor height?
faqs.answer: A flood zone lookup shows mapped hazard information. Use an elevation certificate or other accepted measurement to establish the building’s floor and grade heights for the specific structure.

faqs.question: Does a finished elevation certificate expire?
faqs.answer: FEMA’s instructions say that a completed certificate remains applicable unless physical changes invalidate the documented information. Separately verify whether later maps or local rules changed what is required for the decision.

title: How to Find CMBS Debt Service Coverage and NOI by Property
description: Look up net operating income and debt service coverage in SEC CMBS filings. Check the operating statement date and whether the ratio covers one property or a portfolio.
coverAlt: Illustration of a mixed-use retail and office building on an urban corner in late-afternoon light.
coverCaption: Illustration of a commercial property. The worked examples use the addresses and asset numbers in the SEC filings.
intro: Start with the trust, the loan’s asset number and the property address. Then open the asset data exhibit to the trust’s Form ABS-EE. It can show one debt service coverage ratio (DSCR) based on net operating income and a second based on net cash flow. Keep both ratios, the dates of the operating statement and the code that tells you whose financials the figures cover.
takeaways: One Marietta property had 1.0104× coverage on net operating income and 0.9886× on net cash flow for the same 12 months.
The same trust placed a consolidated ratio beside one address for a five-property loan. Four other address records had no separate ratio.
The September and October filings carried the same March 31 financial cutoff. A new filing date can leave the property financials unchanged.

sections.heading: Where are commercial property financials filed?

blocks.text: For commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) trusts that file asset-level exhibits, open the filing detail in the SEC’s EDGAR database. Select the asset data file, Exhibit 102, and find the trust’s asset number. Confirm the property name and street address inside that asset. The explanatory exhibit, when available, is where the issuer can describe assumptions or exceptions.

Schedule AL distinguishes financials used to underwrite the loan from results in the most recent operating statement. Net operating income (NOI) takes operating expenses out of revenue before capital items and debt service. Net cash flow (NCF) also reflects capital costs before debt service. Divide each amount by the applicable debt service for the same period. Record the reported ratio as a multiple, such as 1.25×.

sections.heading: Why does the same property show coverage above and below 1×?

blocks.text: In the October filing for BBCMS Mortgage Trust 2024-5C25, asset 12 identifies Elevate at the Pointe at 707 Franklin Gateway in Marietta, Georgia. The reported operating statement covers April 1, 2025 through March 31, 2026. Both ratios use the same filed debt-service amount of $1,665,819.50.

rows: NOI ÷ debt service
NCF ÷ debt service

blocks.text: On the NOI calculation the numerator exceeds debt service by about $17,245. After the $36,200 difference between reported NOI and NCF, the NCF calculation falls short by about $18,955. The two ratios give different readings of the same statement. To establish whether payments were made as agreed, check the loan’s payment and servicing records for the relevant period.

items.label: Calculate coverage after checking the filing’s income and payment basis
Check how a lender modeled property taxes and set the escrow

sections.heading: Does a ratio next to an address apply only to that building?

blocks.text: Asset 15 in the same trust is the Acquisition America Portfolio. The exhibit places its 1.1929× NOI coverage beside 509–515 West 110th Street and reports scope code C, the CRE Finance Council code for consolidated borrower financials. Four additional collateral addresses sit under that loan with no individual coverage ratios. Store the 1.1929× value once at portfolio scope. Each address can link to that record and carry an empty value for its own ratio.

The trust’s October notes identify asset 15 as one of the loans with companion debt outside the trust. Before recomputing a ratio, use the reported debt service and read the deal’s definitions. A trust note balance alone cannot tell you which payments the reported ratio uses.

sections.heading: How old are the financials in a monthly update?

blocks.text: EDGAR dates the September and October filings September 29 and October 29. The loan rows have their own reporting-period ends, September 11 and October 13. In both releases, the latest operating statements for assets 12 and 15 still end March 31. A credit file made on either filing date should retain the available March financials and their actual statement periods. The October filing is evidence that the figures were carried forward.

sections.heading: How to test a commercial mortgage data feed

blocks.text: Use the original exhibits as a test for any data provider. A service such as Trepp lists property financial performance and debt service in its CMBS data feed. Ask for these two assets and compare its output with the exhibits, including both ratio types, financial statement dates, and portfolio scope. Ask whether the feed retains original and amended filings and how it handles missing values.

For a broader collateral file, use Invariant Earth to match an address to a parcel and retrieve available property and hazard fields. Keep the trust and asset number with the SEC financial data so either record can be rechecked independently.

faqs.question: Can I look up the DSCR of any commercial property by address?
faqs.answer: For properties in a reporting CMBS trust, the address can help identify the collateral in the public asset data exhibit. Coverage varies by trust, financing structure and available financial statements. For other properties, request the operating statement and the debt schedule from an authorized source.

faqs.question: What is the difference between NOI DSCR and NCF DSCR?
faqs.answer: NOI coverage uses income before capital items and debt service. NCF coverage uses cash flow after capital costs and before debt service. Compare the two on the same statement dates using the debt service reported for the same period.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a CMBS DSCR covers the whole portfolio?
faqs.answer: Check the assets and property records under the same trust and loan asset number. Read the financial scope indicator and the filing comments. Code C indicates consolidated borrower financials in the CRE Finance Council reporting legend.

title: Fire Sprinkler Records by Address for Underwriting
description: Find commercial sprinkler permits by address. Compare work scope, sign-off and inspection records using three NYC filings for one office building.
intro: To check whether a commercial building has sprinklers, match the address to the building ID and read the scope and status of each sprinkler job. Then request current inspection and impairment records for the space being insured. At 1221 Avenue of the Americas in Manhattan, New York City recorded a signed-off subcellar job and separate permits for work on floors 11 through 13 and floor 15.
coverAlt: Aerial view of 1221 Avenue of the Americas, with the New York City building footprint outlined in teal.
coverCaption: 1221 Avenue of the Americas, Manhattan. Cropped NYC OTI 2024 aerial imagery, CC BY 4.0. Invariant overlaid the city building footprint for BIN 1022693.
takeaways: The city files this building under both Avenue of the Americas and 6 AVENUE. BIN 1022693 links the records.
The subcellar permit is signed off. One level in that job’s description covers piping only.
Use the permit history for work scope and closeout. Ask the owner or sprinkler service provider for coverage by floor, the latest inspection report and any current impairments.

sections.heading: How do I look up sprinkler permits for an address?

blocks.text: Find the local building department’s permit portal and resolve any address aliases, suites or campus buildings. In NYC, start in DOB NOW and use the Building Identification Number, or BIN, to find filings for one structure. Check the older Building Information System when the work predates DOB NOW.

Open the sprinkler job and its work permits. Record the floors or spaces covered, what was altered, the permit status and the date of any closeout. NYC makes approved Letters of Completion available in the public portal by address or job number. Save the document and the date you checked it.

sections.heading: What three sprinkler jobs at one Manhattan building show

blocks.text: We matched three DOB NOW filings to three sprinkler work permits on November 24, 2026. One filing uses 1221 6 AVENUE and two use 1221 AVENUE OF THE AMERICAS. All six rows carry BIN 1022693. The city footprint shows the same BIN and base tax lot 1010010029. Using the BIN brings the alternate address into the same building file.

rows: Subcellars 2 through 4. The job describes heads and piping on two levels and piping only on the third.
Issued May 28, 2026. The work permit shows Signed-off. The job shows LOC Issued and a November 16, 2026 sign-off date.
Existing sprinkler system alterations on floors 11 through 13. Filed under 6 AVENUE.
Issued September 25, 2026. The work permit shows Permit Issued. The job row leaves the sign-off date blank.
Existing sprinkler system alterations on floor 15.
Issued October 20, 2026. The job shows Permit Entire and the work permit shows Permit Issued. The job row leaves the sign-off date blank.

blocks.text: The subcellar closeout applies to the job in that row. For a quote on floor 15, keep the permit and its scope and request a closeout or current protection record for that floor. The selected records leave the building-wide coverage percentage and current impairment status open.

sections.heading: What belongs in a quote or renewal file?

rows: Building and protected space
Match the schedule line to the local building ID and to the floors, tenant spaces or storage areas being insured.
Coverage and system type
Request the current protection schedule or as-built plans. Record covered areas and any exclusions using the same area basis as the submission.
Installation or alteration date
Use the issued permit for the authorization date and the scoped Letter of Completion or sign-off record for documented closeout.
Current operating condition
Ask for the latest inspection, testing and maintenance reports for the applicable system and any open deficiencies or impairments.

blocks.text: New York City’s Fire Code treats periodic inspection, testing and maintenance as ongoing records. Keep the date of the last verified report and ask about impairments separately. At renewal, add new evidence and retain the scope and supporting documents used at the previous quote.

Use Invariant Earth to retrieve footprint area and building characteristics for a location, along with parcel and hazard context. Verify the building in the local footprint layer, then attach city permit and completion records to its building ID. In a vendor trial, ask for separate fields for permit status, closeout and current inspection evidence, with a source for each.

faqs.question: Can I tell whether a commercial building has sprinklers by address?
faqs.answer: An address can lead to sprinkler permits, plans or closeout records. Match the address to the exact building and read the floors or spaces covered. Ask for current system records when the underwriting decision depends on its present coverage and condition.

faqs.question: Does a signed-off sprinkler permit cover the whole building?
faqs.answer: The sign-off applies to the work the permit covers. In the Manhattan example it applies to one subcellar job. Read the scope and check protection evidence for the insured space separately.

faqs.question: Where can I find the last sprinkler inspection date?
faqs.answer: Request the current inspection, testing and maintenance reports for the system from the owner or property manager. In NYC, the fire code requires those records to be maintained. Keep those report dates separate from permit issuance and job sign-off.

title: Foot Traffic Data by Address for Retail Site Selection
description: Compare pedestrian counts near an address using NYC DOT data. See why two Midtown storefront locations rank differently on weekdays and Saturdays.
intro: Start with a count on the block and during the hours your store depends on. In September 2026, NYC DOT counted 13,925 pedestrian passages on Sixth Avenue between 50th and 51st streets during its weekday afternoon sample, against 12,747 on Fifth Avenue between the same cross streets. On Saturday midday, Fifth Avenue led with 17,264 passages against 9,818. The May samples gave the same ordering for each window.
coverAlt: Two charts compare pedestrian passages per hour on Fifth and Sixth avenues. Sixth leads on weekday afternoons and Fifth leads Saturday midday in May and September 2026.
coverCaption: Published pedestrian passages divided by the hours in each sampled window. Source NYC DOT Bi-Annual Pedestrian Counts, locations 65 and 66. Calculations by Invariant.
takeaways: Use pedestrian passages to compare street exposure during matched windows. Measure the actual storefront approach separately.
Compare raw totals only for windows of equal duration. Use passages per hour when comparing an afternoon sample with a shorter Saturday sample.
Keep missing counts out of rankings. NYC DOT’s historical zero convention means a count was not collected. The selected Jay Street row omits all six 2026 fields.
For a store visitation trial, ask for the property boundary, visit definition, sample coverage and how the provider handles nearby activity.

guideActions.label: Compare pedestrian counts at two addresses

sections.heading: Find a count on the block you need

blocks.text: Map the proposed entrance and identify the block, frontage, and pedestrian approaches. Then find the city’s published count location and compare the cross streets. A count from a nearby avenue can reflect a different route to transit or another concentration of stores. Save the sensor or count location ID with the place you are evaluating.

NYC DOT’s biannual count program samples pedestrian passages across a line on the sidewalk. Its methodology describes both sides of the street where applicable, a weekday morning window of 7 to 9 a.m., a weekday afternoon window of 4 to 7 p.m., and a Saturday window from noon to 2 p.m. The case locations are Fifth Avenue, ID 65, and Sixth Avenue, ID 66, both between 50th and 51st streets.

blocks.text: Sixth Avenue recorded 9.2% more passages in the September weekday afternoon window. Fifth Avenue recorded 75.8% more on Saturday midday. A store that depends on evening commuters and one that depends on Saturday shoppers could shortlist different blocks. Use multiple comparable counts at the proposed entrance before treating either sampled window as a typical week.

We used the NYC DOT release updated November 17, 2026. The table labels the campaigns by month. The selected records give no exact date for each count, so the comparison matches the sampling windows and campaigns. Hourly figures are count divided by window length and rounded here. The downloads retain the raw values and the calculation to two decimals.
Use the replay guide to run the city query and calculate hourly rates from the returned counts. It keeps unpublished windows and the city’s zero marker visible in the output.

blocks.text: NYC DOT compiled the source counts. Invariant selected the rows and calculated the hourly averages. NYC DOT and the City of New York disclaim accuracy, suitability and liability for errors or omissions. Observe posted signs.

sections.heading: Keep missing observations visible

blocks.text: The same query returns a location record for Jay Street between Willoughby Street and Metrotech Walk in Brooklyn. Its May and September 2026 count fields are absent. Retain the location with a blank observation and ask the publisher or collect a new count before comparing it. NYC DOT’s methodology also treats an explicit zero in this series as a marker for no count collected.

Store the count location, exact source field, sample window, raw count, normalized rate, and missing-value status. Track the date you checked the source. For a store opening, add local conditions that can change passersby, including construction, weather, transit closures and unusual events.

sections.heading: Choose the measure that matches the decision

rows: Which block gets more street exposure during opening hours?
City pedestrian counts or your own screenline counts in comparable windows.
Check the cross streets, both sides of the street where applicable, period and uptime.
How many people enter an existing store?
An entrance counter or authorized estimates of visits to the mapped location. Placer documents separate visit and visitor metrics.
Validate the entrance or property footprint, count employees and repeat visits consistently, and check for indoor or adjacent activity.
What demand can this store draw from the surrounding area?
Travel-time and demographic data, customer origins where available, and competitor locations.
Preserve the travel mode and period. Check the sales or visits evidence separately.

blocks.text: In a vendor trial, use a real short list with an inline store, a stand-alone location and a space in a dense or multistory building. Ask how the vendor handles places it cannot measure. Nearby street activity can help compare areas when the estimate for a particular venue is unavailable.

Use Invariant Earth to resolve candidate addresses and match them to parcels before joining a count or visit dataset. Keep the storefront entrance, count point and parcel geometry as separate records so you can review the match later.

faqs.question: Can I get foot traffic data by address?
faqs.answer: Use the address to locate the proposed entrance, then check the nearest published pedestrian count on the same block and during the hours you need. For actual store entries, use a door counter or a visit dataset with a verified property boundary.

faqs.question: How do I compare a weekday afternoon count with a Saturday count?
faqs.answer: Divide each observed count by its own sampling duration to compare the passage rate. Keep each day and time window visible. NYC DOT’s weekday afternoon sample spans three hours, while the Saturday midday sample spans two.

faqs.question: What does zero mean in the NYC DOT pedestrian count file?
faqs.answer: NYC DOT’s methodology uses zero for a window in which the count was not collected. An omitted value has no published count either. Preserve both as unavailable when ranking sites.

title: How to verify a commercial property tax abatement by address
description: Find the records behind a commercial property tax abatement, estimate its value by taxing unit, and verify whether a buyer can assume it after a sale.
coverAlt: Aerial image of the early Samsung construction site next to farm fields and a road intersection in Taylor, Texas.
coverCaption: Early site work at the Samsung Taylor campus in June 2022. Aerial imagery from USDA NAIP via USGS The National Map.
intro: Start with the signed tax abatement agreement and its amendments. Then match the land, buildings and equipment to their appraisal accounts. For each account and tax year, check which taxing unit recognized the exemption and how much value it excluded. Those records let you estimate the levy reduction before you check the bill and any separate grant payments. For an acquisition, also check the signed assignment and model the first tax year after the benefit expires.
takeaways: Retrieve each jurisdiction’s agreement and verify which property, tax years and conditions it covers.
Calculate the tax effect separately for each authority. In the two Samsung equipment accounts below, Taylor’s appraisal exemption was 92.5% of the reported value and Williamson County’s was 90%.
Keep the appraisal exemption, billed tax, cash reimbursements and potential recapture as separate amounts.
A sale may require written consent. Carry the remaining term and any ongoing obligations into the buyer’s analysis.

sections.heading: How to look up a commercial property tax abatement by address

blocks.text: Use the address or parcel number to find the appraisal district’s accounts. Machinery and other business personal property may have separate accounts at the same address. Match the company, property description and taxing unit to the agreement. In Texas, start with the Comptroller’s local agreement database and Chapter 312 registry, then retrieve the signed agreement and amendments from the applicable authority.

rows: Signed agreement and amendments
The taxing authority, effective dates, eligible property and value, rates by year, construction and employment conditions, cure period and recapture terms.
Appraisal roll or account detail
The tax year, real or business personal property account, appraised value, exemption amount and taxable value by authority.
Tax statement and collector history
Billed amounts, later adjustments and what was paid, with a date for each. Reconcile each authority to its own tax rate.
Grant or reimbursement records
The basis for the payment, performance conditions, payment date, and any limits or repayment terms.

sections.heading: What did Taylor and Williamson County abate on two Samsung accounts?

blocks.text: At Samsung’s Taylor site, the city’s 2022 agreement and the county’s 2023 agreement apply separate Phase I percentages to qualifying new equipment. They also provide for separate equipment accounts and ten-year periods for qualifying annual renditions in Phase I. The 2025 county appraisal workbook shows two accounts at the same street address with first effective dates one year apart.

rows: P511639, effective January 1, 2024
City of Taylor
P511639, effective January 1, 2024
Williamson County
P515246, effective January 1, 2025
City of Taylor
P515246, effective January 1, 2025
Williamson County

blocks.text: The exemption value times the listed rate, divided by 100, gives about $960,511 in estimated 2025 levy reduction across these four lines. Both accounts still show their full equipment value on the Taylor ISD debt-service line. The Comptroller separately lists a Chapter 313 agreement for Taylor ISD maintenance and operations taxes. Keep those school records apart from the two city and county exemptions. Check the collector’s statements and the separate grant records before reporting what the project paid.

blocks.label: Download the two appraisal accounts, tax rates and calculations

sections.heading: What did Taylor’s 2025 amendment change?

blocks.text: Taylor reported the Zone 9 agreement amendment at its June 12, 2025 council meeting. The signed document replaced the construction schedule. It calls for three million square feet of occupiable improvements and three million square feet of non-occupiable improvements by December 31, 2026. It calls for another million square feet of occupiable improvements by December 31, 2028. Read the definition of completion and the amendment’s conditions when matching those milestones to records.

The amended city agreement provides for repayment of the prior abated city taxes with interest after an uncured default on the 2028 milestone. For certain other defaults it uses a three-year lookback, also with interest. Keep the city and county agreements separate. Before closing, request the current signed documents, eligibility or compliance records, and any approvals that affect transfer.

sections.heading: Does a property tax abatement transfer to a new owner?

blocks.text: Check the assignment clause and obtain any consent the agreement requires. At 2312 McLemore Avenue in Fort Worth, the city council authorized the transfer from PMA FW Presidio, LLC to Starboard Presidio DST on January 11, 2022. The signed consent gives that same effective date and requires the buyer to comply with the owner’s obligations under the existing agreement.

The amendment set January 1, 2022 through December 31, 2026 as the abatement and compliance period. The agreement covers 100% of the eligible increase in improvement value for city property taxes, capped at $27,663,000 of eligible value. The land stays taxable under this agreement. Under the signed schedule, 2027 is the first tax year after expiration.

The housing payment was $200 for each rental unit, or $27,600 a year at 138 units. Payment was due by April 1 in each abatement year. The agreement provides for loss of that year’s abatement when payment is missed. The amendment requires evidence of the prior year’s payment and other compliance records by March 1. Request both the receipt and the annual filing before carrying the abatement into an acquisition model.

The city forecast $675,438.25 in forgone revenue over five years. To verify actual savings, pull the appraisal account and collector statement for each tax year. Check the exemption amount on the city line and model the post-expiration year using the applicable assessment and rates. The signed records establish the transfer and obligations. The bills and payment receipts establish what was charged and paid.

blocks.label: Download the Fort Worth assignment timeline and payment calculation

sections.heading: How to calculate property tax abatement savings

blocks.text: Build one line per appraisal account, taxing unit and year. Start with gross assessed value and enter the eligible increase or equipment value separately. Apply the agreement’s percentage and cap to that eligible amount. Use the adopted rate for that year and carry the remaining taxable value through the model. Model grants on their payment dates and check the effect of losing an exemption or missing a milestone.

Use Invariant Earth to match the site to its parcel. Join the appraisal accounts, the taxing units and dated agreements before applying an incentive to the purchase model. An equipment-account exemption can start on a different date from the land account or the next equipment delivery.

faqs.question: Does a 90% tax abatement cut the entire property tax bill by 90%?
faqs.answer: It exempts the share of eligible value covered by the agreement for the participating taxing unit. Check the other taxing units and property accounts separately, then reconcile the final bill.

faqs.question: Can a buyer assume the seller’s tax abatement?
faqs.answer: Review the assignment clause, any required written consent, and the remaining tax years. In the Fort Worth example the buyer assumed the owner’s obligations under a signed consent, and the amended term ran through the 2026 tax year.

faqs.question: How can I estimate the annual dollar value of a property tax exemption?
faqs.answer: For each affected tax line, multiply the exempt value by the adopted rate and divide by 100 when the rate is quoted per $100 of taxable property. For the amount actually billed or paid, use the collector’s records.

title: Commercial Property Tax Assessment History by Address
description: Find commercial property tax assessment history by address. Compare NYC roll and tax charges, California reassessment, and a lender’s tax escrow.
coverAlt: Empire State Building actual and taxable assessed values for fiscal years 2023 to 2027. Both start at $407.8 million. In FY2027 actual assessed value is $577.4 million and taxable assessed value is $492.4 million.
coverCaption: NYC Department of Finance final assessment roll records for Manhattan tax lot 1008350041. Amounts on the chart are assessed values in millions of dollars.
intro: To find a commercial property’s tax assessment history, look up its parcel number in the local assessor’s map, then retrieve the published assessment for each tax year. Save the tax class, taxable value, and publication stage with each record. Use the tax collector’s account to check billed charges and payment status separately.
takeaways: Join the assessor and tax account using the jurisdiction and parcel number. Keep address aliases with the file.
Use the final roll for a finalized tax-year comparison. Retain earlier notices for decisions made before it was published.
Read taxable assessed value, the adopted tax rate, and posted charges together before setting an operating expense or escrow assumption.
For a California purchase, track the annual bill, any supplemental bills, the recurring expense estimate and the required escrow separately.

sections.heading: How to look up past property tax assessments by address

items: Search the local assessor or parcel map by the street address. Match the building and all of the parcels covered by the transaction.
Open the assessor’s current roll and historical archive. Record the tax year, tax class, parcel number and whether the value is tentative, final or revised.
Keep market value, actual assessed value, any phased-in assessment, taxable value and exemptions in separate fields.
Match the tax collector’s statements to that parcel and tax year. Keep billed charges, payments and balances in separate columns.

sections.heading: Five years of Empire State Building assessments

blocks.text: The landmarks designation lists the Empire State Building at 350 Fifth Avenue, Manhattan block 835, lot 41. The assessment records for the same tax lot list 338 as the lowest house number on 5 Avenue. Use Manhattan borough code 1 plus block 00835 and lot 0041 to form the ten-digit BBL, 1008350041. That identifier matches the assessment and the tax account.

The FY2023 taxable assessment followed the lower actual assessed value. By FY2024 the transitional value was lower, and it remained the basis through FY2027. In FY2027 the actual assessed value was $577,440,900 and the taxable assessed value was $492,419,019. The final taxable exemption field was zero for each of the five records.

For the FY2027 tentative row, the assessed figures appear in the tentative fields. The final fields still show zero. The Department of Finance dictionary defines period 1 as tentative and period 3 as final. Preserve that stage when building a historical view, especially when you need to show what was available on an earlier credit decision date.

blocks.label: Download the five final assessments
Download the assessment and tax-charge reconciliation

sections.heading: How to reconcile the taxable value to posted charges

blocks.text: Multiply the taxable assessment by the adopted rate for that fiscal year and class. NYC’s adopted Class 4 rates were 10.848% for FY2026 and 10.859% for FY2027. We compared the calculation with the two original entries coded TAX for each year in the public account. The account lists other charges and payments separately.

The FY2027 calculation is within one cent of the posted TAX total. The amount due January 1, 2027 was already listed when we checked on November 23, 2026. Use the posted charge column for the billing schedule and the payment and balance columns for collection status. For a new purchase or loan, also review abatements, exemptions, pending appeals, and any separate charges that could change the modeled expense.

sections.heading: Commercial property tax reassessment after a California sale

blocks.text: Ask the county assessor which interest transfers and whether the transaction triggers reassessment. The assessor generally values the transferred interest at fair market value on the date of a qualifying change in ownership. A purchase of an interest in a company can also trigger reassessment when it changes control of an entity that owns real property. Review the transaction structure and the assessor’s determination before relying on the seller’s tax expense.

For each affected fiscal year, subtract the applicable annual roll value from the new assessed value. Apply the local tax rate and the county’s proration factor. A reassessment event in January through May generally produces two supplemental bills or refunds, one for the rest of the current fiscal year and another for the next full fiscal year. June through December generally produces one. June events take effect on July 1 and apply to the next full fiscal year.

Consider a hypothetical March closing with an $8 million annual roll value for both years, a $15 million new assessment and a 1.25% tax rate. The modeled annual tax increase is $87,500. The April-through-June factor of 0.25 gives a $21,875 first supplemental bill. The next full fiscal year adds $87,500 on the same assumptions. Use the actual roll for each year and confirm the applicable rate and any separate charges with the county.

Supplemental bills generally go directly to the owner, even when the lender impounds regular property taxes. At closing, reconcile the existing annual bill with the supplemental estimate and confirm who will pay each bill. Ask for the actual county assessment notice and tax bill as soon as they are issued.

sections.heading: A Hollywood refinance shows what tax escrow actually measures

blocks.text: The BANK 2026-BNK52 prospectus lists a $23.7 million refinance for SoCal Self Storage Hollywood at 5900 Hollywood Boulevard. It reports three tax figures in the operating history and loan terms.

rows: Reported property tax expense
Trailing 12 months ended February 28, 2026
Underwritten property tax expense
Annual expense used to size the loan
Required property tax escrow
Monthly deposit at origination

blocks.text: The underwriting expense is $79,601 above the trailing figure. The prospectus describes applying the tax rate to the note amount to account for Proposition 13 and special assessments. The monthly escrow is based on estimated payments over the coming 12 months. Annualizing that deposit gives $247,236. Use the historical figure to reconcile operating statements, the underwriting figure to review loan sizing and the escrow amount to check monthly cash requirements. Obtain the county tax account for the actual bills.

An Oakland City Center appraisal shows why a sale analysis can also point toward lower taxes. The appraisal reports a $176,360,436 assessment and a $2,407,586 tax bill for tax year 2025. Its cash-flow forecast assumes lower taxes after a hypothetical sale at the appraised value. Treat the projected expense as an appraisal assumption and confirm any actual change in the county roll and tax account.

blocks.text: Keep the original assessment row, the parcel identifier, the assessed-value stage and the account statement used to verify the expense. Use market comps and underwriting assumptions for collateral value. The assessor’s market-value field is a tax input. For properties split across several parcels, record which portion of the billed expense belongs to the collateral.

Use Invariant Earth to resolve street addresses to parcels and join the resulting identifiers to dated property records. Build the tax line from the local assessor and tax collector evidence available for that jurisdiction.

faqs.question: Where can I find an old commercial property tax assessment?
faqs.answer: Use the assessor’s roll archive and search by parcel number and tax year. In New York City, search by borough, block, and lot and use the final roll when comparing published final values. Keep the original notice when you need to recover an earlier assessment stage.

faqs.question: Can taxable value be lower than actual assessed value?
faqs.answer: Yes. In the FY2027 Class 4 record for the Empire State Building, the lower transitional assessment set the taxable value because the record lists no exemption. Actual assessed value was $577,440,900 and taxable assessed value was $492,419,019. Review the published taxable field and the local treatment of exemptions.

faqs.question: How do you calculate commercial property tax from an assessment?
faqs.answer: Multiply the taxable value by the adopted rate for the class and tax year. Then check the actual account for abatements, additional charges, payments, and any corrections before using that amount in a closing or escrow calculation.

faqs.question: How many supplemental property tax bills could a California purchase trigger?
faqs.answer: A qualifying event from January through May generally produces two supplemental bills or refunds. One covers the rest of the current fiscal year, and the other covers the next full fiscal year. A qualifying event from June through December generally produces one.

faqs.question: Does a lender’s property tax escrow cover a California supplemental bill?
faqs.answer: California generally sends supplemental bills directly to the property owner. Check the loan terms and confirm with the lender who will pay the supplemental bill and whether you need a separate reserve.

title: Hurricane Wind History by Address for Property Underwriting
description: Check hurricane wind history for a street address. Compare observed station gusts, NOAA sustained-wind swaths, and the data needed for a building-level estimate.
coverAlt: Hurricane Milton over Florida with an 83-knot gust at Tampa International, 88 knots at Albert Whitted, and 89 knots in the incomplete Sarasota station record. The separate landfall estimate is 100 knots sustained.
coverCaption: Milton point observations from NWS Tampa Bay, with NHC’s final best-track center and selected 50- and 64-knot sustained-wind bands. Coastline from the U.S. Census Bureau.
intro: To check hurricane wind history by address, match the address to the insured building and set the event window in local time. Use the National Hurricane Center’s final storm report and wind swath to check the event footprint. Use weather stations for measured wind nearby, and request a documented wind model when the file calls for a gust estimate at the building.
takeaways: Store the coordinates and the building or unit the decision covers.
Record peak gust and sustained wind separately, with the observation height, averaging period and time zone.
Save the storm ID, source date and coverage flags so another reviewer can reproduce the check.

sections.heading: How to look up hurricane wind history for a property

items: Match the scheduled property to the right building footprint. Check each building separately for a campus or a parcel with several structures.
Convert the exposure or loss window to UTC. Search both UTC dates when the local event crosses midnight in the archive.
Pull the final storm report and GIS package. Check where the location falls in the cumulative sustained-wind bands.
Collect nearby station observations from the same period. Keep the station ID, distance from the building, instrument height, wind metric and any outages or incomplete-record flags.

sections.heading: Hurricane Milton at three Florida airport stations

blocks.text: Milton made landfall on Siesta Key at 00:30 UTC on October 10, 2024, or 8:30 p.m. EDT on October 9. NHC estimated the storm’s maximum sustained wind at landfall at 100 knots. We matched three NWS airport station rows to the final storm report and checked their published coordinates against the NHC cumulative wind swath shapefile.

blocks.text: Tampa’s 83-knot gust and its 50-knot swath band describe different wind metrics. The station CSV reports peak gusts separately from two-minute sustained readings at the station. NHC’s swath summarizes estimated sustained-wind extents across the storm. At Sarasota, NHC marks the wind record incomplete in Table 3, even though the NWS CSV has a blank flag for that row. Preserve the incomplete-record note in the underwriting file.

The original Tampa special report at 03:18 UTC carries an 81-knot gust and a peak-wind remark of 84 knots at 03:06 UTC. The final NHC report gives 83 knots at the peak time. The replay shows how to keep all three values with their own sources and reconcile standard time, daylight time and UTC.

To reproduce the join, use the highest RADII polygon that covers each exact station point in AL142024_windswath.shp. Use the best-track ZIP linked from the NHC archive and keep its revision. The download includes the selected coordinates, gust timestamps, units, instrument heights and source file hashes.

rows: Check for an event near the building
Final storm and time window, the applicable sustained-wind band, and recent station observations with instrument metadata.

An event-specific, location-level gust estimate with its height, averaging period, method version and uncertainty. Ask for the measurement evidence behind it.
Review construction or mitigation
The building code or design basis in force at construction or retrofit, plus records for the roof assembly, openings, and completed mitigation.
Compare long-run portfolio exposure
A consistent version of a hurricane hazard model. FEMA’s National Risk Index provides geography-level expected annual loss for screening.

blocks.text: For a vendor trial, send the same coordinates, event ID and date window to each provider. Ask for separate columns for station observations and modeled gusts. The public Wind Verification Report sample specifies a three-second gust at 10 meters. First Street documents how it estimates historical hurricane gusts from storm data. Check that the metric and time window agree before comparing results.

Use Invariant Earth to match the address to the correct parcel and enrich the location with sourced property and hazard fields. Join the dated wind evidence to that asset record with its own source, measurement scope and event ID. For multi-building sites, preserve the building geometry you used to assess exposure.

faqs.question: Can NOAA tell me the peak wind gust at a particular address?
faqs.answer: NOAA gives the measured gust at a station and the analyzed sustained-wind footprint of the storm. Use the station observations and swath as evidence near the building. For a gust estimate at the building, ask for a location-level model and its uncertainty.

faqs.question: Why does the same hurricane show different wind speeds at the same location?
faqs.answer: A peak gust is a brief high reading. Sustained wind uses an averaging period. Station readings also depend on the instrument height and what part of the storm it sampled. Compare the same metric, location, height and time before treating two values as equivalent.

faqs.question: Is hurricane wind history the same as a property wind risk score?
faqs.answer: Wind history describes selected past events. A risk score uses the assumptions, exposure measures and time horizon in its model. Keep event records, prospective exposure and building characteristics together so each can be reviewed.

title: How to Find a Parcel Number (APN) by Address
description: Find an assessor parcel number by address. Use county records or an API, and download a five-row CSV trial for bulk lookups, duplicates, and condo lots.
coverAlt: Map with city address points inside two neighboring San Francisco parcels. Asian Art Museum is parcel 0353001 and Main Library is parcel 0354001.
coverCaption: Civic Center, San Francisco. Dots mark city address points. Outlines show San Francisco Planning’s mapped base parcels.
intro: To find a parcel number by address, search the local assessor’s property portal or parcel map using the street address. Open the match and copy the full assessor parcel number (APN), including leading zeros. Check that the map highlights the property you mean. Save the county or equivalent jurisdiction with the number, since parcel identifiers are assigned locally.
takeaways: Search the physical property address. Include the unit when the record you need is for a specific condo.
Keep the APN as text. In San Francisco, lot 001 appears in many blocks, so the complete number includes the block.
For a portfolio, verify the address point, parcel match, and source date before joining tax, hazard, or permit records.

guideActions.label: Find a parcel number by address

sections.heading: Start with the assessor or local parcel map

items: Identify the assessor’s jurisdiction. A mailing city or ZIP can cover properties in more than one county.
Search the assessor or county GIS portal by street address. Start without the unit to locate the building and add it to check a separately assessed condo.
Compare the returned address and parcel on the map. For vacant land, start from a verified map point or the parcel reference in the listing, deed, or assessor record.
Store the full number as text along with the jurisdiction, source link, and date you checked it. Confirm any formatting changes against the assessor’s record.

sections.heading: Two addresses on Larkin Street, two different APNs

blocks.text: San Francisco’s Enterprise Addressing System returned one address point for each of these Civic Center properties. We checked each number against the city’s active parcel records and intersected each address point with the Planning Department’s base parcel layer. Each point matched one mapped parcel, and the number agreed with the address record.

Asian Art Museum, 200 Larkin St

rows: Identical parcel numbers in one county
Identify the city or town that issued the number. In Norfolk County, Massachusetts, both Medfield and Medway use 01-001 for different lots.
Condo or stacked parcel
Use the unit’s assessment record for taxes or collateral. Keep the base parcel for a ground-level map check, and record the link between them.
Several buildings or lots at one address
Compare the site plan or property schedule with the parcel map. Keep a row for each affected parcel and record which buildings it covers.
Old permit, deed, or assessment
Check the parcel as of the document date. Trace any splits, mergers, or renumbering before joining it to the current map.
Mapped line near a proposed improvement
Use the assessor map for identification. Review the recorded map, legal description, or survey to establish the boundary needed for the decision.

sections.heading: Look up parcel numbers in bulk from a list of addresses

blocks.text: To look up APNs in bulk, start with one stable ID per row in your CSV. Resolve the address to a point, check the match, and look up the parcel containing that point. Return an outcome for every input, including duplicate addresses and rows that need review. Then join the results back on the original row IDs.

In Invariant Earth, send the address to Geocode and pass the checked latitude and longitude to Enrich. Read the APN and parcel source when the parcel match is confirmed. Geocode reports whether the point comes from an address record, a building centroid, or an estimate along the street. Review estimated points, corrected addresses, and building-level results for unit-specific questions. Keep source outages separate from missing parcels and retain the returned vintage and field omissions.

sections.heading: Test a bulk parcel lookup with five CSV rows

blocks.text: This CSV uses two public buildings, one repeat address, a deliberately invalid address, and a commercial condo. We checked the city records on November 25, 2026. The expected outcomes come from city records, so you can use the same file to evaluate any provider.

rows: SF-01 · 100 Larkin St
San Francisco’s address and parcel layers agree on APN 0354001. Import it as text.
SF-02 · 99999 Larkin St
The exact address query found no row. Keep the input in the output with its match status and an empty APN pending review.
SF-03 · 200 Larkin St
The address and parcel layers agree on APN 0353001. Both Larkin properties are lot 001 on different blocks.
NY-01 · 432 Park Ave, commercial club
The unit tax record uses 1012921303 and links to parent 1012920033. The queried tax map layer has zero separate unit polygons.
SF-04 · 100 Larkin St again
The expected APN is still 0354001. Keep both input IDs even when one lookup serves both rows.

faqs.question: What is an assessor parcel number?
faqs.answer: An assessor parcel number, or APN, identifies a parcel in the local property records. Local offices may call it a parcel ID, tax parcel number, or block and lot. Save the jurisdiction with the identifier because formatting and assignment rules vary.

faqs.question: Can one street address have more than one parcel number?
faqs.answer: Yes. A building can contain separately assessed condo units, and a campus can span several lots. Read the property or assessment records for the unit or site assembly you need. The ground-level map is a starting point.

faqs.question: How do I match a CSV of property addresses to parcel numbers?
faqs.answer: Give each row an ID, geocode the addresses, confirm the property matches, and resolve each checked point to its containing parcel. Join the responses to the original CSV by row ID. Keep parcel numbers as text and send unmatched addresses, street estimates and unit-level questions to review.

faqs.question: Is the APN the same as a legal description?
faqs.answer: The APN is a reference used to find property records. To establish the extent of a transfer or the legal boundary, review the recorded deed, subdivision or parcel map, and survey as appropriate.

title: NYC Local Law 97 Building Lookup by Address
description: Check NYC Local Law 97 coverage by address, tax lot and building ID. Compare the 2025 and 2026 lists and see what to request before estimating penalties.
coverAlt: At 37 Wall Street, the 2025 covered buildings list flags tax lot 1000260014 as CP3. The 2026 workbook lists building 1078991 as CP0 and building 1078992 as CP3.
coverCaption: The Department of Buildings switched from reporting pathways by tax lot to identifying the pathway for each building in the 2026 covered buildings list.
intro: To check whether a New York City building is covered by Local Law 97, find its Building Identification Number (BIN) and look up that number in the Department of Buildings’ 2026 Covered Buildings List. Keep the borough, block and lot (BBL) as a second identifier, especially when one tax lot contains several buildings. Use the owner’s filing and current DOB records to verify compliance and any penalties.
takeaways: The 2026 workbook reports both the LL97 coverage flag and the compliance pathway by building ID.
At 37 Wall Street, the 2025 tax lot row flagged CP3. The 2026 release lists one building under CP0 and the other under CP3.
A listed pathway describes how a covered building reports. Filing acceptance, emissions above the limit and assessed penalties require separate evidence.

sections.heading: How to check Local Law 97 coverage by address

blocks.text: Search by borough and street address in the Department of Buildings’ Building Information System. Open the property profile and confirm the building’s BIN and the tax lot’s BBL. In the 2026 Sustainability Covered Buildings List, read columns C and D for that BIN. Column C gives the Local Law 97 coverage flag and column D gives the pathway code. On a shared tax lot, retain each BIN and the published code for that building.

The usual thresholds are more than 25,000 gross square feet for one building, or more than 50,000 gross square feet for multiple buildings on the same tax lot or condominium buildings governed by the same board of managers. The pathway depends on the building. DOB treats the workbook as preliminary and records approved corrections in its BEAM reporting portal.

Compare the two lists at the level each one represents. In 2025, the workbook flagged pathways for the tax lot and listed preliminary BINs. In 2026, it gives a pathway for each BIN. The agency says a difference may reflect a corrected record, information from a partner agency or a change in the building’s circumstances.

sections.heading: What changed in the 2026 covered buildings list?

blocks.text: We matched three tax lots by exact BBL in the published 2025 and 2026 workbooks. Addresses in the table are the city’s tax lot labels and can repeat across several BINs. The workbook row numbers and the source file checksums are in the download.

rows: 37 Wall Street · 1000260014
CP3
48 Beaver Street · 1000297501
CP1
No exact BBL row found

blocks.text: At 37 Wall Street, applying the 2025 lot flag to both building records would miss the CP0 entry in 2026. At 48 Beaver Street, the 2026 worksheet has three BIN entries and repeats the Department of Finance’s reported lot building count of two on each row. Keep that mismatch visible until the building inventory is reconciled. The lot square footage also repeats on every row, so keep it at lot level.

At 280 Broadway, the 2026 list gives BIN 1079215 the CP4 code for City or NYCHA buildings. The separate energy benchmarking disclosure gives the same BIN two Portfolio Manager reporting records with different floor areas. Use the BIN to connect the sources and retain each source’s individual reporting scope.

blocks.text: Track the emissions calendar year separately from the filing year. For an annual Article 320 report, the owner files for the previous calendar year. A pathway that begins in calendar year 2026 and an update to the filing-year 2026 workbook describe different dates.

sections.heading: How to verify Local Law 97 compliance and penalties

blocks.text: For an acquisition or refinance, obtain the filed report for each covered BIN and year, the BEAM submission status, the applicable emissions limit and the reported tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent. Confirm the gross floor area by use, energy records, qualifying deductions and any adjustment approved by DOB. Ask for the status of any separate reporting or emissions violation and the underlying DOB notice.

The city’s Article 320 formula for above-limit emissions applies $268 per metric ton of carbon dioxide equivalent above the applicable annual limit. An illustrative 100 metric tons over the limit would produce $26,800 before any applicable mitigation. DOB lists a separate monthly floor-area formula for failure to file. Keep modeled exposure, a penalty notice and the amount actually due in separate fields.

Request the certified emissions calculation when a screening estimate uses a public benchmarking record. The applicable limits use floor area by property type or occupancy category, and the energy calculation uses the fuel and electricity rules for the relevant year. A single energy-use intensity figure is insufficient for that calculation.

faqs.question: How can I check whether an NYC building is covered by Local Law 97?
faqs.answer: Look up the building’s BIN in the Department of Buildings’ current covered buildings list. Read the LL97 flag and pathway for the building, then verify any correction or special circumstance with the owner and DOB. A shared tax lot can have more than one BIN.

faqs.question: How do I look up a Local Law 97 fine for a specific building?
faqs.answer: Ask the owner for the applicable DOB notice, payment or resolution status, and the filed report for the relevant BIN and year. The covered buildings workbook gives a coverage flag and pathway. It has no assessed penalty amount.

faqs.question: Can buildings on the same tax lot have different Local Law 97 requirements?
faqs.answer: Yes. The 2026 workbook shows BIN 1078991 under Article 320 beginning in 2024 and BIN 1078992 under Article 321. Both are on the tax lot DOB labels 37 Wall Street.
