faqs.question: Who is responsible for an expired Austin building permit after a sale?
faqs.answer: Austin Development Services says the current property owner is responsible for expired permits even when another owner pulled them. Ask the city which permits need reactivation or another form of resolution before applying for new work at that property.

faqs.question: Does an issue date in a Chicago permit API mean work can begin?
faqs.answer: Check the review program, milestone and permit fees. Chicago’s general issue-date column records when a permit was ready to issue subject to payment. Express Permit Program records use the issuance date after full payment. Check the city’s current record before making a work-start decision.

faqs.question: How does Invariant Earth fit into building permit diligence?
faqs.answer: Use Invariant Earth to retrieve parcel identity, zoning, building characteristics and hazards together with sources. Link the issuer’s permit by its building and filing IDs to preserve the scope and dates of the work.

faqs.question: Which API should I use for building permits by address?
faqs.answer: Start with Invariant Earth for the cited parcel and building context. For permit records, compare Mireye and Shovels for area and date searches, West Kite for commercial property records, ATTOM within an ATTOM integration, and PermitStack for property permit history. Check the authority, dates, scope and coverage against the issuer.

faqs.question: Why does a building permit search return duplicate rows?
faqs.answer: An issuer can publish a row per work type or other part of the record. For the Brooklyn fit-out, six rows correspond to four distinct work permit numbers and three filings. Keep those counts separate.

faqs.question: Can I estimate roof replacement date from a permit?
faqs.answer: Match the permit to the correct building and check that its scope covers the roof assembly or area you are evaluating. Then look for a separate completion or inspection record. Rooftop equipment permits describe a different scope.

faqs.question: Does a building permit establish legal occupancy in NYC?
faqs.answer: Use the applicable Certificate of Occupancy or Temporary Certificate of Occupancy for legal use and occupancy coverage. Review which floors or spaces it applies to and any expiration or conditions.

title: Zoning data APIs for U.S. parcels and site selection
description: Compare zoning APIs and city GIS. Use NYC parcel tests to see how a lookup handles split zoning and a commercial overlay that covers part of a lot.
coverAlt: Aerial map of 2239 Forest Avenue in Staten Island. Five colored areas show the share of the tax lot in each base zoning district. The published point falls in C8-1.
coverCaption: 2239 Forest Avenue, Staten Island. The white line traces the MapPLUTO tax lot. Colors show the clipped NYC zoning polygons. Aerial imagery from USDA, USGS and The National Map.
intro: Use Invariant Earth to screen a U.S. location with a cited parcel ID, zoning code, parcel boundary and other site conditions in one lookup. Use city district geometry to measure zoning across a tract. For a U.S. parcel zoning lookup, compare Zoneomics for point and area queries, Gridics for development standards in supported jurisdictions, and Regrid for zoning fields attached to parcel records. Keep the local government’s map and ordinance as your reference. At one Staten Island address, a point lookup gives one district, the city’s tax lot record lists three, and a boundary overlay finds five.
takeaways: Decide whether you need zoning at a coordinate, a parcel summary, or each district intersecting the site.
Ask how the API handles small overlaps and where its source shows the adopted map and rule.
Verify the zoning lot, applicable rules and approvals with the local authority before committing to a use or floor area.

guideActions.label: Find the parcel to check for zoning

sections.heading: Which zoning API fits the work?

blocks.text: Give every provider the same parcel boundary and proposed use. The commercial comparison below uses published documentation. The five-district result comes from the city data queried for this article.

columns: What to check in a trial
rows: Zoneomics
Point and area lookups, with published options for use tables, controls and overlay data where available.
Submit the parcel polygon and ask for the geometry, source date and permitted-use reference for the affected portion.
Gridics
Parcel-level zoning, uses, setbacks and modeled development capacity.
Check jurisdiction coverage and ask which source rules and parcel assumptions drive a building envelope or floor-area result.
Regrid
Parcel IDs with local zoning codes, standardized categories on applicable plans and a matched zoning product.
Ask when you receive one parcel code, how the code is assigned and which product supplies more detail or a link to the city code.
Invariant Earth
A coordinate lookup returns parcel identity and a Regrid-sourced zoning code alongside other location fields.
Review the matched assessor parcel number. The published catalog allows a nearest-parcel fallback for parcel matching. Use the city district geometry to test the whole tract.
Land Use Labs
Address or coordinate lookups for base and overlay districts, with standardized land use and development rules in covered areas.
Submit a point inside the overlay and another outside it. Save both sets of results and verify precedence and effective dates in the local code.
LightBox
Standardized zoning and development controls by address, parcel identifier or spatial geometry where covered.
Run both the parcel-ID lookup and a geometry query. Compare the returned district IDs, allowed-use fields and source dates against the city map.
Municipal GIS and code
Local tax maps, district polygons, overlays and the adopted map and ordinance. Format and update process depend on the jurisdiction.
Confirm map and ordinance dates independently. Ask the authority which zoning lot and approvals apply to your plan.

sections.heading: One Staten Island parcel, three different lookup results

blocks.text: We used the MapPLUTO 26v2 boundary for 2239 Forest Avenue, Staten Island, borough-block-lot 5012500011. We also queried NYC Planning’s base zoning district polygons on November 23, 2026. The published parcel point falls in C8-1. MapPLUTO lists M1-1, C4-1 and C8-1 in that order and flags the parcel as split.

The polygon overlay finds five intersections. C4-1 and M1-1 each cover a little over 37% of the mapped tax lot. R3A and R3-2 together cover 7.17%. Both individual shares fall below the 10% minimum defined for MapPLUTO’s base district fields. The two largest districts switch order between the parcel fields and this overlay. The largest areas differ by only 0.35 percentage points in our calculation. Keep the original parcel fields and recomputed results with their own source dates.

rows: Largest overlap in the polygon calculation. MapPLUTO lists it second.
MapPLUTO lists it first.
Contains the published parcel point. MapPLUTO lists it third.

Appears in the geometry overlay.
Appears in the geometry overlay.

blocks.text: We projected the boundary and zoning polygons to New York State Plane Long Island in U.S. survey feet, intersected each district with the tax lot and divided by the mapped polygon area. The total is approximately 378,715 square feet. MapPLUTO’s separate LotArea field is 376,110 square feet. Use the polygon area as the denominator when reproducing these shares. Displayed percentages may differ from 100% because of rounding.

sections.heading: How do you check a commercial zoning overlay by address?

blocks.text: Match the address to its tax lot, then check the city’s commercial overlay layer for the site. In NYC, a C1 or C2 overlay can be mapped inside a residential district. The point tells you whether one location falls inside it. Intersect the overlay polygon with the lot to see how much of the site it covers, then compare the result with the space you plan to lease or build.

These three Union Street lots in Brooklyn share the R6A base district. We matched MapPLUTO 26v3 and the city’s Zoning Tax Lot Database by borough, block and lot, then measured the C1-4 overlap from the city’s GIS polygons on November 24, 2026.

blocks.text: At 682 Union Street, the point and tax lot record both return C1-4, but the mapped overlay stops partway through the lot. A retailer evaluating space toward the back needs to locate that space on a floor plan and verify the zoning lot, current use classification and any applicable limits or approvals. NYC’s retail and services provisions distinguish general allowances from uses that have size limits, other conditions or special permit requirements.

For a vendor trial, ask for the base district, overlay code and geometry as separate outputs. Invariant Earth’s parcel zoning field gives the sourced parcel code for the initial screen. Use the city geometries to test the overlay share and ask how the provider reports a confirmed absence or an unresolved lookup.

sections.heading: What should a zoning API return before you rely on it?

columns: What a usable result gives you
rows: Parcel identity
The exact boundary, assessor ID, match method and the coordinates used. A nearby match stays marked as nearby.
Districts and additional rules
Each base district and the geometry affecting the tract. Commercial overlays and special districts have their own records.
Which rules are in effect
The source map, ordinance section, effective date and any recent amendment. Keep a vendor’s refresh time in a separate field.
Proposed use
The local use classification and the approval process for the operation. A zoning district label alone leaves those questions open.
Site capacity
The zoning lot used in the calculation and any split-district rules, setbacks, height limits or approvals that change the result.

blocks.text: New York City defines a zoning lot separately from a tax lot. A zoning lot can include multiple lots of record under specified conditions. The city also has separate provisions when a zoning lot crosses district boundaries. Confirm the zoning lot and ask for a written determination when a lease, construction budget or loan depends on the result.

faqs.question: Can I get zoning by address from an API?
faqs.answer: Yes. Some APIs accept an address, then return the district at the matched point or a summary tied to the parcel. Ask which result you are getting and run a polygon check on split lots.

faqs.question: Why does one parcel have several zoning districts?
faqs.answer: A mapped district boundary can cross a tax lot. A polygon overlay returns the intersecting districts and their shares. A parcel summary may omit small intersections under its published reporting rules.

faqs.question: Can a property have a commercial overlay and a residential base district?
faqs.answer: Yes. NYC maps C1 and C2 overlays within residential districts. Check the official overlay polygon against the intended premises. At 682 Union Street, the published point is inside the C1-4 overlay and the polygon covers about 46.5% of the mapped tax lot.

faqs.question: Can I estimate buildable floor area from a zoning API?
faqs.answer: Use the API to screen a scenario. Verify the zoning lot, current rules, intended use and applicable approvals before applying a floor-area figure to a design or project budget.

title: EV charging station APIs for location and live availability
description: Compare EV charging APIs for station locations and live port availability. Verify port counts, shared power and which Ohio NEVI stations are open.
coverAlt: Aerial map of the I-70 and U.S. Route 42 interchange near London, Ohio, with Pilot 454 and TA London marked.
coverCaption: I-70 Exit 79 near London, Ohio. Pins use AFDC station coordinates. Aerial imagery from USGS, USDA and The National Map.
intro: Use Invariant Earth for site screening around a proposed charger location. One coordinate lookup can bring together parcel, road and utility context. Use charger feeds to plan trips and check connector availability. Use the U.S. Department of Energy’s AFDC API to locate charging stations and count installed ports. For a driver who needs a free connector now, use a timestamped availability feed from a mapping provider or charging network. The difference shows up at one Ohio interchange. The federal inventory lists 16 fast-charging ports across two stops. A routine sum of the equipment export returns 160 because it repeats the station total on each row.
takeaways: Count installed ports once per station ID. Preserve repeated equipment rows when the source supplies no equipment ID.
Keep connector compatibility, station access hours and live equipment status in separate fields.
Ask when the network observed the status. A station record can be updated today and still carry no occupancy data.

guideActions.label: Screen a charging stop and its access

sections.heading: Which EV charging API should you use?

blocks.text: Start with the decision you need to support. A planner can use an inventory to find gaps in a corridor. A routing app needs to know whether a compatible charger is free and how recently that was observed. The commercial comparisons below use provider documentation. We queried the AFDC feeds for the Ohio example.

rows: Invariant Earth
Screen a proposed charging location with parcel, road access and electric service territory context.
Check parcel match type and road class. Ask the serving utility to confirm the connection point and capacity for your charging load.
U.S. DOE AFDC
U.S. station inventory with public access, location, connector types and installed DC fast port counts. An equipment CSV adds connector counts and rated power.
Check how station counts repeat across equipment rows and whether the station ID survives a refresh.
TomTom
Charging availability grouped by connector type and power. TomTom documents a three-minute refresh for dynamic data.
Check that both networks appear on your corridor. Measure the age of the underlying status and ask how the feed represents unknown availability.
HERE
Place search with optional connector availability, grouped by type and power. The documentation also covers equipment-level status and operator IDs.
Ask which networks expose equipment detail and usable update timestamps on your routes.
Google Places
Place records with EV connector counts and, where available, compatible-group availability, out-of-service counts and an update time.
Check how often the availability fields populate for the places you serve. Google documents how several connectors can share one charger.
Operator feed via OCPI
Operator-provided Locations, EVSEs and Connectors. The OCPI Locations module defines EVSE status and update fields.
Confirm partner access and keep the country, party, location and equipment IDs needed to match updates.
Eco-Movement
Charging equipment and status through its Data API. The guide documents OCPI push updates with a last-updated timestamp.
On your corridor, measure how long updates take to reach you. Keep the equipment IDs and verify the feed distinguishes stale or absent status from availability.
ChargeHub
A charging infrastructure API for the United States, Canada and Mexico.
Request two operator samples along your route. Check which sites return equipment-level status and when each status was observed.

sections.heading: Two Ohio charging stops expose a 10× counting error

blocks.text: We queried AFDC for electric stations in ZIP 43140 and kept the two public locations with DC fast charging. Both sit at I-70 Exit 79. The equipment export below was captured on November 23, 2026 at 07:31 UTC. It reports equipment inventory and rated output.

rows: Pilot Travel Center 454 · 322368
Four identical rows, each listing one CCS connector rated at 350 kW. Each repeats the station count of 4.
Seven rows list one CCS connector and five list one J3400 connector. All list a 400 kW rating and repeat the station count of 12.

blocks.text: Summing the station field over the equipment rows gives 4 × 4 + 12 × 12 = 160. Counting one station total per AFDC ID gives 4 + 12 = 16. Dropping duplicate-looking CSV rows would also lose equipment detail. The four Pilot rows are identical in the export. AFDC allows an equipment row to describe more than one port or connector, so keep the three quantities separate in your data model.

The Pilot stop also shows why the kW field needs its own label. Before opening, DriveOhio specified up to 350 kW for a single vehicle. At opening, the Joint Office reported up to 175 kW per vehicle when at least four vehicles were charging. Keep the equipment rating for compatibility filters and use a separately sourced power curve or measured data for charging-time estimates.

blocks.label: Download the Ohio station records and port-count audit

sections.heading: Test the answer a driver will see

blocks.text: Suppose a driver with a J3400 inlet wants to stop at TA London. The AFDC export identifies five J3400 connectors there. The station has status E and reports 24-hour public access. That is enough to show a candidate stop. To say how many compatible chargers are free, match the station to a live feed, read the status for the compatible equipment, and retain its update time.

rows: A recent observation with compatible equipment free
Show the count, when it was observed and which connector type it covers.
A recent observation with zero free
Show that no compatible chargers are free. Distinguish ones in use from ones out of service when the feed does.
An old observation
Show when the status was last checked and offer another stop. Set the cutoff using observed delay on that network.
No status, an unknown value, or an unmatched station
Show that live status is unavailable. Keep the inventory and access hours visible.

blocks.text: For the trial, run these two station IDs and add locations from every network you expect customers to use. Compare the API with the operator’s view at the same times over a week. Log whether each station matched, whether it had a timestamp, and how old the observation was when your app received it. Include a known outage and a station with several connectors sharing one charger. Those cases reveal whether the feed can support a routing decision.

blocks.label: Evaluate other data APIs

items.label: Run the same vendor evaluation across workflows
Compare port uptime, live status and actual charge success

sections.heading: How much power can a free EV charging port deliver?

blocks.text: A free port can share power with another vehicle. Check the power available to the port while its neighbors are charging, then compare it with what the vehicle can accept. California utility program site visits documented three different charging configurations in 2023. Use them to test how a routing or fleet application handles shared power.

columns: Power available in the documented configuration
What the planning tool should handle
rows: Paired public fast charger, PG&E program
Up to 125 kW for one capable vehicle or 62.5 kW per port with the pair in use.
The same available port can have a different power limit when its neighbor is occupied.
Dual-inlet heavy truck, Southern California Edison program
The charger supplies up to 90 kW per output. The truck has 120 kW and 60 kW inlet limits, giving a 150 kW combined ceiling under this fixed split.
Apply the smaller limit to each active inlet before adding the results.
Shared bus charging cabinet, San Diego Gas & Electric program
180 kW to one connector or 60 kW per connector when all three are active.
Apply the cabinet limit and the allocation the operator reports for the active connectors.

blocks.text: On the paired public charger, 30 minutes at 125 kW gives a ceiling of 62.5 kWh at the charger output. At 62.5 kW it gives 31.25 kWh. Both calculations assume a constant rate. Estimate battery energy using the vehicle’s charge curve, losses and usable plug-in time. Where the provider cannot supply a simultaneous output rating, show the listed maximum and leave the shared-power estimate unresolved.

blocks.label: Download three power-sharing configurations and five calculation checks

sections.heading: Which Ohio NEVI charging stations are open?

blocks.text: On November 19, 2026, the Ohio Department of Transportation reported 19 public openings out of 120 stations in its National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (NEVI) program. Another 99 were in design and two were under construction. The 120 includes the 40 locations selected in Round 4. The state expected many of those sites to open by the end of 2027. Keep them in a corridor expansion forecast and count the 19 separately when reporting Ohio’s NEVI openings as of that release.

columns: What the project or host record shows
rows: Pilot Travel Center 454, London
The Joint Office announced public charging on December 13, 2023.
Station 322368 at 1365 State Route 42 NE reports four public fast-charging ports, status E and a December 8, 2023 open date.
Love’s, 540 Timmons Way, West Jefferson
The travel stop opened in June 2025. ODOT lists this address as Round 4 candidate 28.
ZIP 43162 returned one station at 97 E Main St and no match at the Love’s address.
Love’s, 2 Loves Dr, Conneaut
ODOT lists the address of Love’s store 389 as Round 4 candidate 21.
ZIP 44030 returned one public fast-charging station at Truck World, 780 St Rt 7. Its 12 ports belong to AFDC station 469704 at that separate address.

blocks.text: Store each award or construction update against the project address and keep the station ID in a separate field. Confirm the street address and network before counting installed ports. The nearest station or a matching ZIP can point to a different operator, as in Conneaut. A missing inventory match means the query found no record at that address. That leaves the project’s latest field status unknown.

Keep the source’s reported open date and the date of the public announcement as separate observations. AFDC revised the open-date logic for API imports in February 2026 after some planned stations received dates when they first appeared in network feeds. For navigation, first check public access and compatibility at the confirmed station, then read the operator’s latest port status. AFDC imports connected network data daily, and status E means the station is listed as available.

blocks.label: Download the Ohio NEVI stages and address checks

sections.heading: What can a charging availability API tell you?

blocks.text: Use live port status for routing. For procurement, ask for session outcomes and the dated outage log. Compare them by stable port ID. The California field tests show how operating status, access and payment can affect a charge attempt.

items.label: Compare uptime, successful charges and payment failures in the California field tests

blocks.label: Download the California field test summary

sections.heading: Use surrounding land and road data for expansion decisions

blocks.text: For network planning, this inventory can show where fast charging is concentrated. Invariant Earth supplies surrounding parcel and road context, including nearest major road name, road class and distance. A truck corridor study also needs the entrance location, usable turning geometry, and a route that fits the vehicle and trailer. Take a proposed load and operating schedule to the serving utility when evaluating a new site.

items.label: Screen a truck depot against a 5 MW utility limit

faqs.question: Does the AFDC API show current EV charger availability?
faqs.answer: The AFDC station status describes the facility. Use the AFDC inventory to find stations and installed ports, then use a live operator or aggregator feed for occupancy.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a charging station, an EVSE and a connector?
faqs.answer: A station is a site with charging equipment. In OCPI, one EVSE can charge one vehicle at a time. A connector is the plug or socket on that equipment. An EVSE can offer several connector types.

faqs.question: Can an available EV charger deliver less than its advertised kilowatts?
faqs.answer: Yes. A power cabinet can split its output across several active ports, and the vehicle can impose a lower limit. One California evaluation documented a paired charger that could deliver 125 kW to a single capable vehicle or 62.5 kW per port with both in use.

faqs.question: How do I count public DC fast-charging ports from AFDC?
faqs.answer: Filter electric stations by public access and DC fast charging, then sum the installed DC fast port count once per station ID. Keep equipment rows for connector detail and use a status feed for the current free count.

faqs.question: Are all 120 Ohio NEVI charging stations open?
faqs.answer: Ohio reported 19 public openings as of November 19, 2026, with 99 sites in design and two under construction. The 120 includes 40 Round 4 selections. Check the station address and the operator’s latest status before using an individual stop.

title: Geoforge alternatives for data center power screening
description: Compare Geoforge, Paces, PVcase, GridCARE and Invariant. Use 49 PJM upgrade records to test the dates and assumptions behind a data center power forecast.
coverAlt: Illustrative aerial view of transmission towers and a construction lane crossing harvested fields.
coverCaption: AI-generated illustration of a transmission corridor in agricultural terrain.
intro: Start with Invariant for a power study tied to the proposed campus, its load ramp and the dates each phase needs service. Compare Geoforge for candidate connections and modeled offtake, Paces for portfolio screening, PVcase Prospect for grid constraints and GridCARE for utility programs that evaluate flexible load. Give each provider the same test. Ask which facility limits service, when the relevant upgrade enters service and how a delay changes the first phase.
takeaways: In one PJM plan, the same 765 kV line segment had a June 2030 required date and an October 2031 projected date, a gap of 517 days.
AEP Ohio used separate service estimates for different groups of studied customers. One group needed an additional regional upgrade.
A usable power forecast names the connection, the case year, the limiting element and the work required for each load phase.

sections.heading: Which Geoforge alternative fits your site search?

blocks.text: The table summarizes public product descriptions. Use the Ohio example below to test what a provider can explain about its output for your location.

columns: What to ask in the demo
rows: Geoforge
Site reports with potential connections, modeled offtake by year and scenario, queue context and an energization estimate. It also offers deeper power-flow studies.
Ask which grid case and upgrade records drive the range for the first phase. Request the basis for any competing load in that case.
Paces
Regional capacity screening, project-level connection evaluation and support through interconnection studies.
Ask how capacity layer results carry into a study of your site, and which grid, land or permitting issue changes the shortlist.
PVcase Prospect
Modeled injection and withdrawal, with limiting elements for different scenarios. The published documentation distinguishes base-case and contingency coverage by market.
Check the available scenarios for your region and whether the constraint is already present before your load is added.
GridCARE
Utility work on grid capacity for flexible loads. National Grid describes its use in New York and work with UK Electricity Transmission.
Confirm the serving utility is involved and get the MW, hours, operating limits and dispatch conditions for any flexible service.
Invariant
The published site-study workflow covers AC power flow, contingency analysis, candidate connections, and indicative costs and timing.
Request the case vintage, phased results and limiting facilities. Ask which assumptions can be rerun as utility evidence changes.

sections.heading: An Ohio power forecast can contain several valid dates

blocks.text: AEP Ohio’s November 2025 study letter covered about 13 GW of new data center load. It found that the studied projects needed regional transmission work under the scenarios evaluated. Its initial estimate was Q4 2031 for Clusters 1 and 3 with the regional project and applicable parallel upgrades in service. Cluster 2 had a 2033 planning estimate and needed another regional solution. A buyer needs the customer’s actual service plan to determine which work applies.

PJM cross-references the first regional proposal, 2025W1-570, to upgrade package b4068. In the March 2026 assessment, b4068.2, the AEP portion of the Greentown to Teddy 765 kV line, had a required date of June 1, 2030 and a projected date of October 31, 2031. The first is the planning need date. The second is the forecast in that report. A particular customer’s electric service date has its own evidence.

rows: Planning need for b4068.2
June 1, 2030
Keep it as the date the reliability plan requires the work.
Projected in-service date for b4068.2
October 31, 2031
Use it as a dated component forecast and check the latest schedule.
AEP Ohio Cluster 2 service planning estimate
Check the second regional dependency, local work and actual customer schedule.

blocks.text: AEP Ohio later reported that 5,642 MW had signed binding contracts under the new tariff as of February 12, 2026. That update gives the scale of the committed cohort. It leaves the distribution by bus, year and cluster open. Ask your provider how it treats unconfirmed demand, then test a scenario with a different set of competing projects.

sections.heading: What the 49 PJM upgrade rows show

blocks.text: We extracted the required and projected dates for each b4068 sub-ID in the March assessment. Two rows projected June 2028, 21 projected October 2030, and 26 projected October 2031. These are counts of published sub-IDs. A project forecast should identify the subset the connection actually depends on.

Two rows in that assessment show an invalid calendar value in the required-date column. The February board recommendations show June 1, 2030 for both sub-IDs. The download retains the February dates and the March source values separately, with the latter normalized to null. Ask a provider which source its model used and how it handles this sort of discrepancy.

blocks.label: Download the 49 PJM upgrade rows and AEP Ohio study evidence

sections.heading: How to test the first phase before paying for a site option

blocks.text: Give the vendor the parcel, the minimum load needed on day one, the full facility load, the two service dates and how much load you can curtail. For example, ask for 50 MW by July 2030 and 200 MW by January 2032 at the meter. Those are illustrative targets, with the utility service for your project to be confirmed.

items: Ask for the modeled MW on each date at the same connection point. Record the model year, the limiting equipment and the outage assumption.
Request a second run with the relevant upgrade out of service through your target date. Ask which phase remains feasible and what changes the answer.
Get the utility’s written service terms, required work and estimated start of service. Keep energization and facility handover as separate milestones.

faqs.question: What are the best Geoforge alternatives for finding power for a data center?
faqs.answer: Consider Paces for portfolio screening, PVcase Prospect for modeled point-of-interconnection constraints, GridCARE for opportunities that depend on utility-supported load flexibility, and Invariant for a phased site study. Test your actual service dates with each provider.

faqs.question: What is the difference between required and projected in-service dates?
faqs.answer: The required date expresses when the planning case needs an upgrade. The projected date is the schedule estimate in that record. PJM’s March 2026 assessment lists June 1, 2030 and October 31, 2031 respectively for b4068.2. Use the relevant utility agreement and construction schedule to evaluate customer service.

faqs.question: Can a power screening report tell me when I can energize a data center?
faqs.answer: A power screen can estimate when the grid could support a proposed load under a specific case. The serving utility’s agreement and work plan establish the commercial service terms and estimated date. Confirm energization through a commissioning or utility record.

title: How to Check Commercial Roof Age by Address
description: Verify commercial roof age by address, work scope and closeout records. See how Beverly Hills documents a partial replacement and a separate phased project.
coverAlt: The Beverly Hills library roof project replaced about 1,100 square feet and repaired about 500 square feet.
coverCaption: Beverly Hills Public Library roof work quantities reported to City Council on May 16, 2023. The report gives no total roof area.
intro: Start with the work address and the insured building. Find the most recent documented replacement for each roof section and check the scope against a closeout record. Keep repairs on their own line. At the Beverly Hills Public Library, one project replaced about 1,100 square feet and repaired about 500 square feet, leaving the replacement date for the rest of the roof unknown in the city packet.
takeaways: Use an address to find candidate records, then confirm the building and roof area against the work description or plan.
Record the installation, inspection and acceptance dates in separate fields. Label the date you actually verified.
For a partial replacement, record the replaced area, the repaired area and the remaining sections with unknown dates.

guideActions.label: See the Beverly Hills roof case

sections.heading: Where to look up roof work

blocks.text: Search the building department’s permit portal by street address and parcel ID. Look for reroofing, membrane replacement, recovery and repair. When several buildings share an address, match the permit to a building ID, tenant building name, footprint or roof plan. Check the work address in the document before using the applicant or owner address. For municipal buildings, search council minutes and contract closeout packets by site name and project number as well.

columns: What to carry into the property file
rows: Permit or contract
Work address, building identifier, permit or project number, stated scope and issue or award date.
Roof plan or itemized scope
Roof sections covered, work performed in each section, material and area where reported. Record whether the membrane, deck, or both were included when the documents specify.
Final inspection or closeout
Event type, date, status and the work that the document covers. Request an installation record or contractor statement when the exact installation date matters.

blocks.text: For a commercial roof that was recently replaced, ask the owner for the roof plan, contractor scope, closeout and applicable warranty. Aerial imagery can help you identify a visible change or locate different roof sections before you review the records. Carry that observation with its imagery date.

items.label: Cross-check a named contractor against municipal permit records

sections.heading: Beverly Hills library roof work, by area

blocks.text: The Beverly Hills Public Library at 444 N. Rexford Drive had about 1,100 square feet of its single-ply roofing system replaced and about 500 square feet repaired under bid 23-350-1. City staff reported that Public Works and Community Development had inspected the work. City Council accepted the project on May 16, 2023. The project report gives no full-roof replacement date or total roof area.

rows: November 15, 2022 · contract award
The council approved agreement 706-22 for the library roofing repair and partial replacement project.
May 16, 2023 · staff report
Staff described the work quantities and reported that the work conformed to the construction documents.
May 16, 2023 · council minutes
Item E-14 was approved, accepting the work and authorizing the City Clerk to record the notice of completion.

blocks.text: The proposed notice in the agenda packet lists the owner at 455 N. Rexford Drive. Its work address is 444 N. Rexford Drive. The packet copy has blank signature and recording fields. The documented council approval establishes the acceptance date. To verify the exact installation date by roof section, ask for the contractor’s installation record.

sections.heading: How to read a phased roof project

blocks.text: Beverly Hills budgets list a separate roof project under two addresses, 439 N. Cañon Drive and 438 N. Beverly Drive. The FY 2024–25 budget forecast phase 1 completion in FY 2023–24. The FY 2025–26 budget reported that phase 1 was completed in FY 2024–25. Record the forecast and completion as separate events.

rows: Listed among the priorities for FY 2024–25.
Listed among the priorities for FY 2025–26.
Listed among the priorities for FY 2026–27.

blocks.text: Retain all three planning observations with their budget editions. Record phase 1 as completed in FY 2024–25 according to the city’s FY 2025–26 budget. The reviewed budget pages give no phase 2 closeout or roof-section geometry. Request those documents before assigning a replacement year to that section.

sections.heading: How to record roof age for underwriting or lending

blocks.text: Put each documented roof section on its own line in the property file. Include the building ID or work address, section reference, work type, area and units, source page, date and event type. At renewal, compare those rows to the prior submission. A newer document may describe the same work under a different date or report a new phase.

For the library case, record approximately 1,100 square feet of replacement and approximately 500 square feet of repair. Use May 16, 2023 for project acceptance. Leave the exact installation date and the age of the remaining roof unknown until you have section-level evidence. When a submission asks for a single year, retain the section-level record and confirm how the recipient wants partial replacements reported.

faqs.question: Can I use a roof permit date as the replacement date?
faqs.answer: Use the permit date as the date of issuance. Check inspections, closeout or a contractor installation record to establish when the scoped roof work was completed. Keep the date and event type together.

faqs.question: How do I record a partial roof replacement?
faqs.answer: Record the roof section, work type, replaced area and verified date for each section. Keep repairs and roof sections with unknown dates separate. Calculate the share replaced only when you have a verified total area on the same basis.

faqs.question: Does a city capital budget show that a roof was replaced?
faqs.answer: Read the project status and budget edition. Beverly Hills reported phase 1 completed in FY 2024–25 and separately listed phase 2 as a priority in successive budgets. A completion or acceptance record for phase 2 would establish its status.

title: Ageospatial alternatives for commercial roof underwriting
description: Compare Ageospatial, Moody’s, ZestyAI, Verisk and Invariant Earth with a real test for building identity, roof replacement dates and source evidence.
coverAlt: Aerial view of the Rosemead Public Works warehouse with its county building footprint outlined.
coverCaption: 2022 USDA NAIP imagery via CDFW. The outline marks the building identified on the city site map. The photo predates the 2025 roof work.
intro: Use Invariant Earth to start underwriting with a cited building and parcel record, then attach the roof evidence to the structure that the submission covers. Compare Ageospatial for a workflow that collects imagery, maps and records, and Moody’s, ZestyAI and Verisk for dedicated roof products. Give each provider a submission with two addresses and three dates for the same roof project. Check which structure and event the result describes.
takeaways: Compare products on the exact building and roof scope. The owner’s mailing address can point to a different property.
A replacement project has an award date, a completion date and a date when the evidence became available to your team. Keep all three.
A roof age estimate, a report of completed work and a current condition rating answer different underwriting questions.

sections.heading: Which Ageospatial alternative fits your workflow?

blocks.text: Decide what the underwriter needs to do with the answer. An inspection team may need a roof and imagery report. A quoting team may need a structured age field with a confidence signal. A data team may need the building match, its source and a way to store later corrections. The comparison below uses public product descriptions. The municipal records provide an independent case you can run with each vendor.

columns: What to ask for in a trial
rows: Ageospatial
Workflow examples tie a submission line to the parcel and footprint, show a dated roof image, and flag changes and nearby exposures.
Have the tool link each finding to the original record. Export the resolved building, both addresses and the dates behind the replacement finding.
Moody’s Commercial Property Intelligence
Commercial building and roof data, including imagery-derived age and condition, with API, batch and application delivery.
Ask what drove the age estimate for the selected commercial roof and whether the output can show a date range or leave the age open.
ZestyAI Roof Age
Roof replacement estimates from imagery and permit records, with confidence and modeled values where direct evidence is sparse. ZestyAI describes use in a commercial portfolio.
Ask how the model distinguishes a full replacement from partial work and which fields expose the evidence or model basis.
Nearmap Roof Age API
Predicted roof installation age for residential and commercial buildings, using aerial imagery and additional records.
Submit the River Avenue footprint and ask how the estimate treats partial work. Compare its observation date and the estimated replacement period with the city’s completion record.
Verisk Roof Underwriting Report
A commercial roof report with age, condition, material, equipment and an estimated roof replacement cost.
Review the target location and scope of the reported age and cost. Ask what can be retained as machine-readable data.
Invariant Earth
A coordinate-based API with fields for the primary building footprint area, height, floor count and class where supported.
Use the field catalog to choose the spatial inputs. Establish the roof event from the city record and retain it alongside the matched building in your workflow.
EagleView
Roof measurement reports include photographs, facet diagrams, pitch and area. Use the image or report to review the specific roof under consideration.
Match the report to the insured building and verify the observation date. Request the city completion record separately to establish when the replacement work was done.

sections.heading: The Rosemead test starts with two addresses

blocks.text: Rosemead’s July 2025 notice attachment gives 8838 E Valley Boulevard as the city’s address and 2714 River Avenue as the location where the roof work took place. The project documents identify the Public Works Office and Warehouse Building at the River Avenue site. The site map on page TP-1 points to that building among several neighboring roofs.

Even the correct street address can produce different coordinates. The Census Geocoder returned an address-range coordinate that intersects no outline in the county’s 2023 building layer. The county address point was about 64 meters away, carried assessor parcel ID 5282026900 and intersected county outline 2920695. The outline matches the building shape pointed to on the city’s map. The county address record itself has a blank building ID.

That matters in a coordinate-based API. Invariant Earth describes its primary footprint field as using the enclosing Overture building or searching within 100 meters for the nearest one. Keep the input coordinates and review the returned match against the project map before using the result in the file. The county outline in the aerial cover is shown for identification. The photograph is from 2022.

sections.heading: When did the roof actually change?

rows: January 14, 2025
The city awarded the roof replacement contract.
A named project and planned scope.
June 2, 2025
Completion date stated in the notice attachment in the July packet.
The reported date of the replacement work and the later source document date.
July 8, 2025
The council accepted the work and authorized recording the notice.
The acceptance action and authority to record. The county recording date remains unverified.

blocks.text: The staff report says the old metal roofing system was removed and a new metal system installed. The final project cost included additional cooler work. Store that amount as project expenditure and request a cost breakdown or a separate estimate when you need the replacement cost of the roof alone.

For a hypothetical June 30 quote supported only by the records dated by then, keep the replacement completion field open. At a July 31 review with the July packet in hand, add the reported June 2 completion as a new piece of evidence and keep the prior quote snapshot. A dated inspection would answer a separate question about the roof’s current condition.

blocks.text: Give each provider the same submitted location and owner address. Ask for the building it selected and the evidence behind the roof update. Include a second case from your portfolio where the work covered only part of a roof.

items: The selected building and candidate alternatives, with a geometry or a building identifier you can inspect.
The date, material and parts of the roof that the evidence covers, with a distinction between completed work and an estimate.
The original source and date it became available to the workflow, along with the earlier value that a reviewer saw at quote.

title: West Kite Alternatives for Commercial Property Data
description: Compare West Kite, ATTOM, Regrid, and Invariant Earth. Use a 25 Water Street case to test address matching, unit counts, permits, and occupancy history.
coverAlt: 2024 aerial photograph of 25 Water Street in Lower Manhattan with its tax lot outlined and a construction crane on the roof.
coverCaption: 25 Water Street during conversion. Cropped NYC OTI 2024 aerial imagery, CC BY 4.0. Invariant added the MapPLUTO 26v2 tax lot outline.
intro: Use Invariant Earth to match a parcel and evaluate it against sourced terrain, hazards and nearby infrastructure in one API. Compare West Kite for commercial property records and owner research, ATTOM for property and transaction data, and Regrid for parcel geometry. At 25 Water Street, a property lookup and the city’s occupancy records give different unit totals for the same conversion. Ask each provider to show which records explain the change.
takeaways: West Kite’s public lookup resolved three addresses to the same property and returned 1,323 units. MapPLUTO reports 1,323 total units and 1,320 residential units on that lot.
DOB NOW has four issuances of the same general construction permit and ten occupancy issuance records under the related job. Keep each event and its date.
Ask a provider which entity and source each field describes, and whether a historical query retrieves what was known at the time of a decision.

sections.heading: Which property API fits the job?

blocks.text: Invariant makes Invariant Earth. We reviewed the providers’ public documentation and ran the West Kite unauthenticated address lookup on November 22, 2026. The other rows describe documented capabilities and give tests for a paid trial.

rows: West Kite
Commercial property records, ownership research, sales, assessments, and permits.
Resolve address aliases and request the permit sequence and original sources. Check whether an occupancy certificate is available for the exact building and date.
ATTOM
Property characteristics, deeds, mortgages, sales and building permits for an integration.
Use the same address and assessor ID. Confirm county coverage and ask which permit dates and identifiers the feed exposes.
Regrid
Parcel boundaries, assessor IDs, and matching across county records.
Verify how the current and prior parcel versions link after a split or merger. Join building and permit records from their issuing agencies.
Invariant Earth
Location and parcel fields with source URLs, dataset vintages and field status, including terrain, hazards and nearby infrastructure.
Check match type, distance and boundary before joining site conditions to a building. For a permit or occupancy history, use the issuing agency’s records or test a provider that indexes them.

sections.heading: One building, three addresses and two unit counts

blocks.text: The city’s Office Adaptive Reuse Task Force identifies 25 Water Street, 115 Broad Street and 4 New York Plaza as addresses for the same building. We sent each address to West Kite’s public Try endpoint. Each response marked the match exact, returned the same property ID and displayed 115 Broad Street with 1,323 in the units field.

rows: West Kite public lookup
1,323 units on a property labelled Multifamily.
Use the matched property ID for research. Check the unit definition before using the number in a pro forma.
NYC MapPLUTO 26v3, lot 1000050010
1,323 total units and 1,320 residential units.
Keep these two fields separately. The assessor aggregates the buildings on the tax lot.
NYC DOB NOW, building 1000007
1,320 dwelling units in each of the ten returned occupancy issuance records for job M08013214.
Check the actual certificate and the floor-use schedule for the building or space under review.

blocks.text: The public lookup’s number agreed with the assessor’s total-unit field in the November 22 check. The city’s November 24 query returned a newer MapPLUTO edition with the same two unit counts. The public response alone does not establish where the provider obtained it. NYC’s Comptroller also reports 1,320 apartments at the conversion. Use the residential count for an apartment-level analysis and verify the current rent roll and occupancy documents for the deal.

sections.heading: Reconstruct the conversion from permits and occupancy records

blocks.text: The tax lot ties together records at these addresses. The Department of Buildings uses a building identification number, or BIN, to identify the structure. Join the general construction permit M08013214-I1-GC to the occupancy filings under base job M08013214. Keep the original permit, renewal sequence, certificate number and issuance dates.

rows: October 18, 2023
Initial general construction permit issuance. Its row gives an October 6 approval date.
Keep approval and issuance as distinct events.
February 7, 2025
First occupancy issuance in the reviewed dataset, certificate 1000007-0000001.
The index reports an issuance. Read the certificate to see the applicable spaces, use, and terms.
December 17, 2025
Fourth issuance of the same general construction permit, a renewal with changes.
A later work permit can coexist with an earlier occupancy issuance.
September 30, 2026
Latest occupancy issuance in the reviewed data, 1000007-0000010, listed as a renewal without change.
Check the certificate type and applicable expiry directly with DOB.

sections.heading: Run a trial on the records your team uses

blocks.text: Pick a recent conversion, a property with multiple buildings or parcels, and a sale you can verify in the recorder’s file. Ask each provider for the matched IDs, relevant date and original record. Keep the date an event happened separate from the date the provider observed it. For an acquisition or a loan decision, save the actual evidence available on that date.

Ask how you can retain the history in your system. A provider may return the current assessed use, a list of dated permits, or historic snapshots as different products. Ask which prior versions you can query and whether missing results mean no published record, no coverage, or a retrieval failure.

title: Mireye Alternatives for U.S. Property Screening
description: Compare Mireye, Invariant Earth and other U.S. property screening APIs. Test parcel matching, point versus boundary results, source dates and parcel history.
coverAlt: Illustrative aerial view of an industrial building beside winding wetlands.
coverCaption: AI-generated illustration of an industrial site beside wetlands.
intro: Use Invariant Earth when your property screen must show which parcel matched, which source supplied each field, and when the source was retrieved. Compare Mireye and Invariant on the same coordinates, then test how your workflow handles a tax lot that changed boundaries while keeping its identifier. The trials below cover current fields and a dated parcel example.
takeaways: Compare the coordinates and geometry behind each field. The same field name can describe a different search or source.
Both Mireye and Invariant use wetland_acres for an entire selected wetland polygon. To estimate affected acreage, calculate its intersection with the property or project area.
Bring the same assessor parcel, hazard map and required service level to each trial. Record the provider’s matching, missing data and source dates.

guideActions.label: Run the Invariant Earth site screen

sections.heading: Which tool should you evaluate?

blocks.text: Invariant makes Invariant Earth. This comparison uses public product documentation and published evidence. Use the same properties across APIs and map-based tools to verify coverage and exports for your account.

columns: What to check in a trial
rows: Invariant Earth
Location and parcel fields with field-level source, dataset vintage and status.
Inspect parcel_match_type and parcel_match_distance_m. The parcel ID can fall back to a nearest parcel within 250 meters. Check the match before joining another dataset.
Mireye
Point data through Fetch or parcel records through Enrich.
Compare the input coordinate with Enrich’s analysis_point. Its documented example resolves a parcel and uses the stored parcel centroid for analysis.
Regrid
Parcel IDs and boundaries for use in your own GIS or pipeline.
Use the county record to verify a recent split. Regrid explains which events preserve its ID and which retire it.
West Kite
Commercial property research and a report using the parcel outline for flood and wetland area.
Check the property match and whether each layer is published for the county. The documented response identifies fields that could not be answered.
Acres Intelligence
Map-based land diligence with comparable sales, flood and terrain layers, and property reports.
Use the same waterfront tax lot. Record the layer date and whether the report provides geometry you can intersect or a map you inspect visually.
Land id
Interactive parcel, ownership and terrain overlays with current aerial and historical topographic basemaps.
On a recently changed parcel, pin the aerial collection date and the assessor boundary vintage separately. Check which records are available in an export.

sections.heading: Four fields to verify before switching

blocks.text: Mireye publishes separate catalogs for Fetch and Enrich. Invariant lists parcel-match fields in its location catalog. Check the catalog for the endpoint that will serve the workflow. The download records the field name, published unit, source identifier, and what to verify for each output.

rows: Is the location in a mapped flood zone?
Both document within_floodplain_polygon as a FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area test at a point.
For land or buildings, intersect the full geometry with the effective FEMA polygons. Keep the map date and area by zone.
How many wetland acres affect the tract?
Both define wetland_acres as the total area of the selected National Wetlands Inventory polygon. It can be the nearest wetland, including one outside the tract.
Intersect mapped wetlands with the tax lot or proposed disturbance area, then calculate the acreage inside it.
Which substation should we investigate?
Both expose nearest_substation_distance_m. Invariant lists a 10 km search. Mireye describes an EIA layer for substations at 69 kV or above.
Save the returned facility, layer and method. Confirm the serving utility and proposed connection before relying on a capacity estimate.
How reliable is the water service map?
Both expose water_service_area_provenance. Invariant describes the boundary method and original provider. Mireye describes source-based and modeled categories.
Save the original evidence. Ask the utility about pressure, flow, and a service commitment for the intended use.

blocks.label: Download the property screening API field comparison

sections.heading: When is Invariant Earth a good Mireye alternative?

blocks.text: Choose Invariant Earth for a workflow that needs to explain each current parcel match and preserve the underlying evidence for later comparison. In our Brooklyn example, one tax lot kept its identifier through a split and retained about 53% of its former mapped area. The downloadable case has dated geometries from the city and separates archived boundaries from current point and parcel queries.

In a trial, ask each provider to return the current parcel and match distance, then show the earlier boundary for the same site or identify the archive you would need. Check whether you can recover the date and source of both geometries. Pin a snapshot so you can explain what changed when an underwriter or developer reopens the file.

items.label: Replay the Brooklyn parcel split
Check which fields you can query in Invariant Earth

sections.heading: Run the same test on your own property

blocks.text: Pick a candidate whose boundary you already know. Submit the assessor’s location point and a second point inside the proposed work area. Keep the site address and county parcel ID fixed. Request the parcel boundary separately and record where each result was evaluated. Include a multi-parcel site in the trial when that is part of your usual work.

Use the same source layer and edition when reconciling values. At Brooklyn Army Terminal, for example, the published location point returned FEMA Zone AE. Intersecting the parcel boundary with the same map showed that about 20% of the lot was in Zone AE. The parcel overlay below includes the source queries so you can repeat the calculation.

Save the field status with the value. Mireye Fetch and Invariant Earth document a distinction between a successful value, no data at a location, and a failed field request. A successful response can include a failed field. Store the dataset edition separately from the fetch time, especially when you are recreating an earlier decision.

sections.heading: What to ask for before signing

blocks.text: Ask each provider for one response from a county you know well and another from an area where coverage is uncertain. Check that someone on your team could reconstruct each property match and find the original source months later. Agree on which fields you can store, how source editions change, and how the provider reports gaps. For utility capacity, ask for a study and service evidence at the proposed connection.

faqs.question: What is a practical alternative to Mireye for property screening?
faqs.answer: Evaluate Invariant Earth for source-backed point and parcel fields, West Kite for commercial property reports that measure area over a parcel, and Regrid for parcel boundaries and IDs. Try each on the same property and source dates before selecting a provider.

faqs.question: Does Mireye Enrich use the same location as Fetch?
faqs.answer: Fetch reads fields at a point. Enrich resolves a parcel and reports its analysis_point separately. The Enrich documentation shows a case where the analysis point is the stored parcel centroid, which differs from the input coordinate.

faqs.question: Does wetland_acres mean acres of wetlands on my property?
faqs.answer: The Invariant Earth and Mireye catalogs describe this field as the size of the selected mapped wetland polygon. Calculate its intersection with your project or parcel boundary to estimate acreage inside it. The National Wetlands Inventory describes mapped habitat.

title: How to Check Wildfire Risk by Address for Commercial Property
description: Match the right building, verify the wildfire map and its date, and document what needs inspection. Includes two reproducible Los Angeles address checks.
coverAlt: Illustration of a commercial building at the edge of dry Southern California hills.
coverCaption: Illustration of a fictional site. The Los Angeles checks below use public map records.
intro: Start with the building on the submission. Match its address to a footprint, check which wildfire map applies, and save the map result with the source and date. At Griffith Observatory, two county address points for the same facility are about 33 meters apart. The two points return the same hazard category. Only one intersects the mapped building. The location check is useful even when the zone result agrees.
takeaways: Keep the matched building ID and the way the address was located. A street point can return a valid map category for the wrong building.
Keep the published hazard category, map edition and source record. A mapped NonWildland result is different from missing coverage.
Request current evidence for the roof, vents, nearby combustibles and access before evaluating the building’s susceptibility to wildfire.

guideActions.label: Check wildfire hazard at an address

sections.heading: Match the address to the building on the submission

blocks.text: Use the street address, ZIP code and building or suite identifier to find candidate locations. At a commercial campus, check the building on the statement of values, which lists the locations and amounts submitted for insurance. Confirm the address against an owner-provided site plan or other building record. Keep each building as its own record when several structures share a parcel or mailing address. County address datasets can contain multiple source points and omit some units.

Record whether the location came from a building, parcel, street segment or ZIP code. A point that falls inside a building is stronger evidence than a street estimate. Review the footprint’s source date and compare it with current records for additions, replacements or multiple structures at the same address.

sections.heading: Two Los Angeles buildings on the 2025 CAL FIRE map

blocks.text: We matched the facilities’ published addresses to county address points and building outlines, then queried the complete polygons against the State Fire Marshal’s 2025 recommended layer for Local Responsibility Areas. Both buildings were within a single mapped class. The county outlines report 2008 source imagery with an Unchanged status in the queried service.

rows: Griffith Observatory, 2800 East Observatory Road
County building ID 470757865499. One of two candidate points intersects the outline. The other is about 25 meters from it.
Very High, raw code 3. The complete mapped footprint falls within a single Very High feature.
Los Angeles Central Library, 630 W. 5th Street
County building ID 484322840870. The address point intersects the outline.
NonWildland, raw code −3. The complete mapped footprint falls within that mapped category.

blocks.text: CAL FIRE’s layer returned NonWildland as a record for the library. A service timeout, a query outside map coverage or a point that returned no features should have a different status. The city’s separate Very High zone layer also matched the Observatory footprint and returned no intersection for the library. Confirm the locally applicable map and its effective date with the jurisdiction for any dated decision.

blocks.label: Download the Los Angeles address checks and source queries

sections.heading: Save the map version and the relationship to the zone

blocks.text: California’s Fire Hazard Severity Zones describe long-term hazard using vegetation, terrain, fire weather and other factors. To find the map for an address, start with the responsibility area. CAL FIRE publishes State Responsibility Area maps, and the State Fire Marshal provides recommended Local Responsibility Area zones. Ask the local jurisdiction which map was in effect on your decision date. Record the publisher, layer, version, effective date where verified, retrieval date and original class.

Compare the full building outline with every intersecting polygon. Keep the classes and whether the building is inside, crosses a boundary, or only touches its edge. Route uncertain matches and mixed footprints for review, especially when a source point or older footprint can change the result. Keep the raw response so the decision can be reviewed after the source updates.

For portfolios outside California, start with the applicable state or local source. The U.S. Forest Service’s Wildfire Risk to Communities data can help prioritize regions to investigate. The Forest Service describes it as a community-scale resource and cautions against using it at the individual-property scale.

sections.heading: What to keep in the underwriting file

blocks.text: Use public mapping to document exposure and direct the next review. The California Department of Insurance describes CAL FIRE’s severity maps as planning tools and explains that insurers use separate wildfire risk models for underwriting and pricing. Keep the map result beside the carrier’s distinct model result and version, where your workflow uses one.

rows: Identity
Submitted address, building ID, match method, footprint date and unresolved matches.
Owner’s building schedule or a site plan when a parcel contains more than one structure.
Mapped hazard
Publisher, map version, date, zone label, footprint relation and any coverage gap.
Local map or adoption record for the decision date when required.
Fire history
Perimeter source, data version, time period and relationship to the building.
Inspection, repair or loss records for questions about damage to a specific structure.
Building susceptibility
Roof covering and condition, vents, openings, vegetation, combustible storage and access.
Dated inspection, photographs or maintenance records that identify the building and conditions reviewed.
Insurance decision
Which evidence informed the referral, unresolved questions, and the carrier’s applicable terms or model output.
Carrier guidance and the applicable policy or binder.

blocks.text: A historical perimeter indicates a mapped past event. CAL FIRE describes gaps and generalization in those records, including areas inside a perimeter that may have escaped burning. A building intersection is a reason to check loss or inspection records. For the condition review, IBHS’s commercial guidance identifies components worth examining, including roofs, vents and nearby combustible material.

sections.heading: How to test a wildfire API before using it on a portfolio

blocks.text: Send the same address and building outline to each vendor. Ask it to return the matched building, location method, original source class, map or model version and the state of any missing data. Include a campus with shared addresses, a building that crosses a map boundary, and an address outside the provider’s coverage. Record whether the system returns distinct results for those cases.

The downloadable Los Angeles checks can serve as two public reference cases for the identity and map steps. For a proprietary risk score, test whether the vendor reports what the score measures, its date and time horizon, and whether you can reproduce the same output for the same building and model version.

sections.heading: Check the wildfire bulletin separately at renewal

blocks.text: For California renewals, check the insurer’s notice against the applicable Department of Insurance bulletin. Look up the insured ZIP and the policy in-force date. The Dove and Gann example shows why a single ZIP can require two declaration dates.

faqs.question: Which tool should I use to check a California address for wildfire hazard?
faqs.answer: Start with the Office of the State Fire Marshal’s map lookup. Confirm the matched building and responsibility area, then ask the local jurisdiction which map applies when an effective date matters.

faqs.question: Does a CAL FIRE zone determine the premium or availability of coverage?
faqs.answer: California’s Department of Insurance describes the severity zones as planning maps. The carrier’s underwriting model and applicable terms are separate evidence for insurance decisions.

faqs.question: Does a NonWildland result mean there is no wildfire exposure?

faqs.question: What should I do when the parcel and the building give different wildfire results?
faqs.answer: Keep both spatial relationships and put the building result first for a building-specific review. Confirm the footprint, map date and nearby exposure, and refer mixed or uncertain geometry for review.

title: California wildfire insurance nonrenewal moratoriums by ZIP code
description: Check California wildfire insurance moratoriums by ZIP code. See Mile Post 18, Dove, Gann, Gifford and Pack Fire dates and residential or commercial scope.
intro: To check California’s wildfire insurance moratorium, match the insured property’s ZIP code to a Department of Insurance bulletin. Then check whether the policy was in force on the emergency declaration date, the policy type and the reason for the notice. Our November 26 review covers 69 ZIP codes across five bulletins, including the new Mile Post 18 Fire bulletin.
coverCaption: AI-generated illustration of a fictional California foothill town.
takeaways: The Mile Post 18 Fire bulletin lists six ZIP codes. Its one-year period starts November 10, 2026. The bulletin was issued November 25.
For commercial property, check the policy type, property use, annual premium and the prior 12 months of employment where relevant.
The Gifford and Pack Fire bulletins in this snapshot address residential policies. The three bulletins for 2026 fires also address eligible commercial policies.

sections.heading: Mile Post 18 Fire moratorium ZIP codes and dates

blocks.text: The Mile Post 18 Fire bulletin lists ZIP codes 95525, 95546, 95548, 95555, 95556 and 95573. Bulletin 2026-13 starts the one-year period on November 10, 2026, and addresses residential and eligible commercial policies in force on that date. Use the signed bulletin and the Governor’s proclamation for the start date. The November 25 date shown in the Department’s directory is the bulletin’s issue date.

For example, a policy in ZIP code 95546 that first took effect November 15 began after the declaration. A policy already in force on November 10 stays in review. Verify the policy type and the stated reason for the notice before relying on the ZIP match.

blocks.text: This November 26 snapshot covers the five published bulletins with one-year periods underway at the time of review. Use the ZIP list to find the bulletin. The one-year anniversary is a review date. Check the current bulletin and the policy before acting on a notice.

sections.heading: Which commercial property policies does SB 547 cover?

blocks.text: California Insurance Code section 675.55 applies to eligible commercial property policies already in force at the time of the emergency declaration. The one-year protection concerns cancellation or nonrenewal based solely on the structure’s location in an area where a wildfire occurred. Section 675.1 addresses residential policies.

For ordinary commercial property, the size exclusion requires both an annual premium of at least $25,000 and an average of at least 25 employees in the preceding 12 months. The statute overrides that size exclusion for policies covering loss or damage to real property used primarily for commercial residential or habitational purposes, such as apartment complexes and qualifying association property. Inland marine, transit and transportation policies are separately excluded. Section 675.55(b) sets out additional exceptions.

These examples use the same ZIP code, a policy in force on October 15 and a notice based solely on wildfire location. The premiums and employee counts are illustrative. The table applies the size exclusion only. Review the policy form, property use, notice and any exceptions under Section 675.55(b) before deciding whether a policy qualifies.

columns: What to flag for renewal review
rows: Warehouse, $24,000 annual premium and 40 employees on average
The premium is below the statutory threshold. The policy stays in review for the other conditions and exceptions.
Retail property, $30,000 annual premium and 20 employees on average
The employee count is below the statutory threshold. Use the average over the prior 12 months. The current headcount may differ.
Warehouse, $25,000 annual premium and 25 employees on average
Both thresholds include the exact cutoff. The size exclusion applies to this ordinary commercial property example.
Apartment complex, $30,000 annual premium and 40 employees on average
The statute exempts policies on primarily habitational real property from the size exclusion. Confirm the principal use and the policy form.

sections.heading: A renewal in ZIP code 95370

blocks.text: ZIP code 95370 appears in both bulletins. Suppose a commercial property policy for a building there first took effect October 1, 2026. It was in force on the Dove declaration date and began after the Gann declaration date. Bring the Dove bulletin into the review and record the policy inception date alongside both matches. The reviewer still needs the policy type, applicable exclusions and the insurer’s stated reason.

For notices that meet the bulletin’s conditions, the Department directs insurers to offer to rescind wildfire-related cancellation or nonrenewal notices and offer reinstatement or renewal. A policyholder can ask the carrier to review the notice against the applicable bulletin and contact the Department for assistance when needed.

sections.heading: What to save in the underwriting file

items: Save the insured address and ZIP from the policy schedule, with the bulletin number and source page. Keep one record per fire and ZIP so overlapping events remain visible.
Record the declaration date, bulletin issue date, policy effective date, notice date, notice reason and proposed end date.
For commercial property, capture the policy form and principal use, and record the annual premium and average employment when the statutory exclusion requires them.
Route conflicting dates, uncertain address matches and policies covering multiple locations for review with the supporting records.

blocks.text: The Department distinguishes CAL FIRE’s Fire Hazard Severity Zone maps, used for planning, from insurers’ wildfire risk models. The bulletin ZIP list answers a separate question about which areas the agency identified for a specific renewal protection.

faqs.answer: Bulletin 2026-11 starts the one-year protection on October 15, 2026, the date of the Governor’s emergency proclamation. The bulletin was issued November 10.

faqs.question: Does the wildfire insurance moratorium cover commercial property?
faqs.answer: California Insurance Code section 675.55 covers eligible commercial property policies in effect at the declaration. faqs.question: What happens when a ZIP code appears in two wildfire bulletins?

title: How to verify a shovel-ready industrial site
description: See what industrial site certification covers and verify buildable land, power, water, wastewater and permits. Compare two certified Tennessee sites.
coverAlt: Two certified Tennessee sites compared against an example requirement of 25 developable acres and 3 million gallons per day of water system headroom.
coverCaption: Published figures for the Canterbury and I-40 Advantage sites against an illustrative screen. Water figures refer to the system’s reported excess capacity.
intro: A shovel-ready designation tells you what a site program reviewed. To decide whether a factory can start on schedule, check the exact tract, the accepted land use, the usable acreage and the utilities that can commit to the project. Two sites in the same Tennessee certification announcement illustrate the difference. One clears the example acreage requirement. The other clears the initial water screen.
takeaways: Keep the certifying program, date and tract boundary with the designation.
Compare usable site area with the latest layout and keep related acreage figures tied to their original boundaries.
Ask each provider for a service offer at the proposed connection point, including the project’s volume, required upgrades and delivery date.
Publish an evidence date and a next action for every open constraint in the inventory.

sections.heading: What shovel-ready certification covers

blocks.text: Select Tennessee generally requires at least 20 developable acres, truck-quality access, documented site conditions and utilities onsite or a formal extension plan. A site in an industrial park in a Tier 3 or Tier 4 county can qualify with 15 developable acres. The program accepts current zoning or an expedited rezoning plan. For a buyer, the difference between an installed connection and an extension plan can be months of work.

Read the actual program rules when comparing badges. Kentucky’s separate Build-Ready designation builds on its shovel-ready criteria and requires a completed, engineer-certified pad for a building of at least 50,000 square feet, with room to expand to at least 100,000. The building pad and its expansion area are distinct from the gross tract acreage.

sections.heading: Compare two certified Tennessee sites

blocks.text: Tennessee named Canterbury in Dickson and I-40 Advantage in Brownsville in the same September 2024 certification announcement. The state’s public listings report different combinations of acreage, zoning and utility characteristics. The table uses the public records as reviewed on November 22, 2026. Confirm present availability and which tract is offered before using either site in a live search.
