blocks.text: Suppose a manufacturer needs at least 25 contiguous developable acres and 3 million gallons per day (MGD) of water. Canterbury’s listed 24 developable acres are below the acreage requirement. Brownsville’s listed 154 developable acres clear the numerical acreage screen, subject to a layout and contiguity check. Its 2.5 MGD of reported system excess water capacity is below the initial water screen. The public figures leave a blocker at each site. For a live decision, ask the water provider what it can actually commit to at the parcel, including flow and pressure at peak demand.

The equal 161 kV entries describe voltage at the substation. To compare deliverable electric service, request MW, voltage at the meter, reliability, deposit and upgrade requirements, and the service date. Wastewater also needs its own confirmation for flow, pollutant limits and pretreatment. A rail line next to a park only identifies a connection to investigate.

blocks.label: Download the two site records and example screen

sections.heading: Check what land each study reviewed

blocks.text: TVA’s Canterbury assessment covered proposed work on 28.4 acres of a larger site it described as 55 acres. It placed that project area outside the identified 100-year floodplain on its cited FEMA panel. It also documented a roughly 0.14-acre wetland on the larger site outside the project area. The acreage in the report answers a different question from the 24 developable acres in the state listing. Use the report boundary and map date when repeating the comparison.

At Brownsville, TVA completed a June 2025 environmental review of proposed work on 110 acres, including clearing, grading for a dirt pad and rerouting a gravel road. That report follows the September 2024 certification announcement. Ask for the dated as-built pad certification or survey to establish what work is in place for the tract being offered.

sections.heading: What to publish in an industrial site inventory

blocks.text: Build the inventory around an identifiable tract. Retain each source record with its own date and geographic scope. Publish certification and project fit as separate fields so a buyer can see why a site is listed and which evidence would move it onto a shortlist.

rows: Tract and availability
Parcel IDs, a boundary for the offered land, current owner or option holder, last confirmation date and any partial disposition.
Buildable land
Survey and measured usable acres, development envelope, pad status, access easements, flood map dates and delineation limits.
Zoning and approvals
Jurisdiction, zoning district, permitted use or approval needed, and the approvals and conditions that apply to the buyer’s proposed layout.
Utilities
Provider, point of service, status of the extension, service offered to the project, delivery date, cost responsibility and signed or dated evidence.
Verification history
Source publication date, date the field was checked, evidence owner and next action. Retain previous values when a tract or utility status changes.

faqs.question: Does shovel-ready mean utilities are already connected?
faqs.answer: Check the certifying program and the provider’s evidence. Tennessee’s program can accept a formal extension plan. The provider’s service offer should identify the connection, offered capacity, upgrades and date for your project.

faqs.question: What is the difference between shovel-ready and pad-ready?
faqs.answer: Shovel-ready describes the work and evidence required by the program. A pad-ready claim concerns a specific building pad. For example, Kentucky’s Build-Ready standards require a completed pad certified by a licensed engineer. Ask for the certification and the pad dimensions.

faqs.question: How do I verify a listed site’s water capacity?
faqs.answer: Ask the water provider for written confirmation of the available project volume, peak flow, pressure, connection location and service date. Keep the number labeled as system capacity until the provider confirms what it can allocate to the project.

title: FEMA’s 50% Rule for Commercial Property
description: Check the FEMA 50% rule for a commercial building. Compare local thresholds, permit lookback periods, repair costs and building-only value before underwriting or renovation.
coverAlt: Illustrative comparison. The same proposed work is 43% of building value under the Miami Beach one-year procedure and 49% under the Charleston County five-year rule, which counts a prior permit.
coverCaption: Illustrative improvement costs for a $1 million building. The published local rules determine which prior work enters each calculation.
intro: The FEMA 50% rule compares the cost of improving or repairing a building with the market value of the building itself. Before using it to review a commercial property, verify the local threshold and how far back the authority counts work. Miami Beach publishes a one-year cumulative improvement period at 50%. Charleston County’s current flood ordinance uses 49% and a five-year period for substantial improvement.
takeaways: Use the market value of the building at the required date, excluding land. Ask which valuation method the floodplain authority accepts.
For damage, estimate the cost to restore the building to its pre-damage condition. For improvement, confirm which prior permits, work and costs the local rule counts.
Record the floodplain determination separately from the policy terms. An insurer may need both before evaluating coverage for required compliance work.

sections.heading: How do you calculate the FEMA 50% rule?

blocks.text: Divide the eligible cost of work by the accepted market value of the building and multiply by 100. The federal substantial improvement definition uses value before the start of construction. The substantial damage definition compares the full cost to restore the building with its value before the damage. For example, $500,000 of qualifying work on a building the authority values at $1 million is exactly 50%.

Use the building value, excluding land, accessory structures and landscaping. Ask the local administrator which appraisal or adjusted assessment they accept. Have the contractor itemize the full scope, including labor and materials. When reviewing damage, carry the cost to restore the building even when the owner plans to repair only part of it.

sections.heading: How far back does the 50% rule count permits?

blocks.text: Start with the jurisdiction that issues the floodplain or building permit. Match its adopted rule to the date of review, then record the work it counts and the period it uses. A statewide rule of thumb can send a portfolio analyst to the wrong set of permits.

rows: Federal NFIP baseline
50% of pre-construction building market value
Check the adopted local rule for cumulative treatment.
City of Miami Beach, Florida
50% in the city’s published procedure
One year of prior work. The city directs applicants to sum the job values on its relevant permits.
Charleston County, South Carolina
49% in Ordinance 2306
Qualifying improvements over any five consecutive years. The county building official determines the building value.

blocks.text: Charleston County’s hurricane FAQ describes a 50% threshold, while its Building Inspection Services page lists Ordinance 2306 as current. The ordinance gives 49% for both substantial improvement and substantial damage. Use the adopted text for a preliminary screen, then ask the building official which rule governs the particular address and work.

sections.heading: Can a prior permit make a renovation substantial?

blocks.text: Consider a commercial building with an accepted building value of $1 million. The proposed renovation costs $430,000. Another $60,000 of qualifying improvements took place 30 months earlier. Assume the work is within the applicable flood hazard area, the local authority accepts these costs and the value, and there are no other qualifying improvements. This is an illustration using published rules.

rows: Miami Beach, one-year period
$430,000. The older work is outside the period.
43%. Below the published 50% threshold.
Charleston County, five-year period
$490,000. The older work falls inside the period.
49%. Meets the 49% threshold in Ordinance 2306.

blocks.text: For a real building, reconcile the permit ID, address, structure identifier, scope, cost and relevant date. Check for phased work or duplicate records before totaling costs. Request the authority’s written determination before using the result to budget repairs, code work or a reopening date.

blocks.label: Download the comparison, calculations and evidence fields

sections.heading: What belongs in the underwriting or loan file?

items: Confirm the structure and the applicable flood map. Keep the building identifier, map panel, effective date and any relevant map change with the file.
Record the administering authority, rule version, threshold and lookback period. Attach the contractor’s scope, local permit history and the accepted building valuation.
Log the written determination and any required work. Ask which documents establish elevation or floodproofing, along with the related repair budget, completion dates and open approvals.

blocks.text: The permit decision and the insurer’s coverage decision have different inputs. The NFIP General Property Form provides up to $30,000 in Increased Cost of Compliance coverage for eligible flood losses on buildings with building coverage, subject to policy terms and the statutory combined limit. Ask the insurer how the actual policy and the written determination apply before carrying any expected payment in the project budget.

faqs.question: Does land value count toward the 50% rule?
faqs.answer: The federal calculation uses only the market value of the structure, excluding land, accessory structures and landscaping. Confirm which valuation the local authority will accept for the building.

faqs.question: Does prior renovation work count?
faqs.answer: Some jurisdictions count multiple improvements over a specified period. Miami Beach publishes one year for its cumulative improvement procedure. Charleston County Ordinance 2306 uses five consecutive years and a 49% threshold in its jurisdiction.

faqs.question: Does the rule apply only to flood damage?
faqs.answer: The federal substantial damage definition covers damage from any cause. The local floodplain authority determines whether its requirements apply. Insurance eligibility, including NFIP Increased Cost of Compliance, follows the policy and the cause of loss.

title: How to check FEMA flood zone history for commercial property underwriting
description: Check the FEMA flood zone on a quote or loan date. Trace effective map panels, Letters of Map Amendment and revalidation records to the property they cover.
coverAlt: Current FEMA map zones within the Huntington revision area, beside a timeline of the July 2021 issue date, December 2021 effective date and January 2024 Alexandria panel.
coverCaption: Current FEMA flood zones inside the Huntington revision boundary. The revision took effect in December 2021 and FEMA later incorporated it into a revised Alexandria panel.
intro: To check a commercial building’s FEMA flood zone on a past date, match the insured building to its footprint, find the map panel effective on that date and apply any map changes that were already in force. Save the map and change records with the decision. An address-only lookup against today’s National Flood Hazard Layer gives you a current result and can miss the history that mattered on the quote date.
takeaways: Record the insured building, map panel and effective date, applicable FEMA case number, and when the result was retrieved.
Track issue dates, effective dates and later panel publication separately. A single FEMA revision can have all three.
For a Letter of Map Amendment, verify the subject in the determination and trace any revalidation to the panel in effect on the decision date.
Keep mapped flood zones, modeled depth, expected loss and any required lender determination in separate fields.
Send ambiguous building matches, boundary touches and missing historic maps to review rather than counting them as outside the hazard area.

sections.heading: Match the building before you look up the zone

blocks.text: Start with a stable building ID and the insured location or collateral schedule. Confirm which structures belong to the account and retain the geometry that supports each match. A mailing address may resolve to a driveway, parcel centroid or neighboring building. On a multi-building site, two structures can have different map results even though they share an address.

Intersect each confirmed footprint with the map polygons. Preserve zone code, zone subtype and the Special Flood Hazard Area flag. Record boundary contact separately from an area overlap. Where the footprint, map or positional accuracy leaves the outcome uncertain, record the exception for review. Do not silently assign all the buildings on the parcel to the zone at its address pin.

blocks.label: Property matching examples

items.label: Check a commercial building’s identity and roof records
Compare a parcel overlay with a single coordinate
Check where the regulatory floodway crosses the parcel
Check elevation units, vertical datum and source date

sections.heading: Find the map that applied on the decision date

rows: Effective map panel
Panel ID, revision suffix and effective date. Retrieve the historical panel for the date you are replaying.
Map changes
Case ID, scope, issue date and effective date. Check whether a later panel incorporated it or whether FEMA revalidated or superseded it.
Preliminary or pending maps
Map status and publication date. Use for forward-looking review. For the effective-map result, use the adopted panel and applicable effective changes.
Retrieval evidence
Retrieval time, source URL and a preserved response or file identifier. A map made effective in 2021 may only have been retrieved by your team in 2026.

blocks.text: FEMA’s Map Service Center provides historic and effective map products. The National Flood Hazard Layer, or NFHL, is useful for current effective GIS data. FEMA’s separate Flood Map Changes Viewer also shows preliminary and pending layers, which FEMA describes as information for review and awareness.

Retain both the date a map change took effect and the date you obtained it. That lets a reviewer distinguish a replay against the best available historical source from a replay of the records actually on file when the decision was made. Keep the historical match geometry and its own vintage, too.

sections.heading: The Huntington revision has three distinct dates

blocks.text: Fairfax County reports that the Cameron Run levee revision removed the levee-protected area in Huntington, Virginia, from the Special Flood Hazard Area. FEMA case 21-03-0303P records the change. The county describes the revised designation for the protected area as shaded Zone X and continues to advise residents that flood risk remains.

rows: Fairfax County reports FEMA issued the revision.
When the revision was issued.
December 13, 2021
Federal notice lists the modification date for Alexandria and unincorporated Fairfax County.
When the modification took effect.
January 11, 2024
FEMA’s final summary lists the revision as incorporated into Alexandria panel 5155190037F when the revised panel took effect.
When the change appeared in that revised panel.

blocks.text: We queried the current NFHL revision polygon and intersected it with current flood-zone polygons sharing its FEMA source citation. About 44% of the revision footprint is mapped as a Special Flood Hazard Area, and about 14% is Zone X with reduced flood risk due to the levee. These percentages describe area inside the revision boundary. They do not describe the share of buildings or policies affected. The protected area is only part of the revision footprint.

The download includes the revision boundary, 11 clipped zone records, source queries and the three dates. The comparison uses current zone geometry. Retrieve the superseded panel and applicable changes to replay a historical building determination.

blocks.label: Download the FEMA revision and clipped zones

sections.heading: Does a FEMA Letter of Map Amendment apply to the whole parcel?

blocks.text: A Letter of Map Amendment (LOMA) can cover a structure, a whole lot or a defined part of a property. In Augusta, Georgia, FEMA’s January 8, 2016 determination for 2501 Reynolds Industrial Road applied to only the portion described by survey bearings and distances. The determination reported unshaded Zone X for that portion and flagged that other parts of the property remained in the Special Flood Hazard Area. In an underwriting file, match the insured building to the area the letter actually covers.

The original letter names panel 13245C0020F. FEMA’s revalidation letter 16-04-5708V lists the same case under panel 13245C0020G, effective November 16, 2019. For two of the four cases we checked, Augusta’s GIS lists a different panel from the one in the federal revalidation. Join on the FEMA case number and community ID first, then save each source’s panel reference and check the newer map and change documents.

rows: Single structure, labeled storage by Augusta
Single lot
Single structure
Surveyed portion of property

blocks.text: Treat a point in FEMA’s amendment layer as a way to find a case. FEMA describes the coordinates as approximate. Its point index labels all four sample records “Not incorporated,” while the 2019 letter explicitly revalidates each case as of that letter’s effective date. Preserve both records and their dates. To assess a later decision, look for a newer panel, determination or revalidation and verify the legal property description in the original letter.

blocks.label: Download the four Augusta case comparisons and source records

sections.heading: What a portfolio flood API should return

blocks.text: Trial a provider with a schedule that includes more than clean one-building addresses. Ask it to return the correct building, footprint source and match status, the map vintage and applicable revision, the intersection result, and unresolved rows. Require a clear answer on whether its as-of feature actually uses retained map vintages or queries only the effective layer today.

rows: Two insured buildings on one parcel
One result per building. Keep each zone intersection and the matched footprint ID.
A footprint touching a zone boundary
Keep the boundary-touch flag and review match and map precision.
A building within an effective revision
Record the map case ID, effective date and which map supported the result on the requested date.
An address without a reliable match or historic map
Return an unresolved status and a reason. Keep the insured value in the unresolved exposure total.

blocks.text: Roll up by building identifier and keep the unmatched and ambiguous totals visible. The mapped share of a footprint is an exposure screen. Estimating water depth or expected financial loss requires additional hazard, elevation, vulnerability and policy inputs. Lending teams should retain the documented flood determination required by their process. Federal banking agencies discuss the Standard Flood Hazard Determination Form and how to handle multiple collateral buildings.

For a historical portfolio, verify that the footprint reflects the building in service on the decision date. Keep the footprint vintage and map effective date in separate fields. We used later building outlines to demonstrate how to reconcile selected values from Appanoose County’s 2021 schedule. A report on the county’s 2021 exposure would also need evidence of the buildings in service during that term.
To screen current conditions before looking up older maps, check the effective FEMA zone at the verified address and calculate parcel overlap through the Invariant Earth API.

faqs.question: Can I use the current FEMA layer to verify a flood zone from a previous year?
faqs.answer: Use the map panel effective on the date you are checking and any applicable revisions in force then. The current NFHL describes current effective mapping. Record both the map effective date and when you retrieved the evidence.

faqs.question: Does a Letter of Map Revision apply on its issue date?
faqs.answer: Check the stated effective date. FEMA’s Huntington revision was issued July 28, 2021 and became effective December 13, 2021. A revised Alexandria panel incorporated the case in January 2024.

faqs.question: What does shaded Zone X behind the Huntington levee mean?
faqs.answer: Fairfax County describes the protected area as shaded Zone X because of reduced flood hazard due to the accredited levee. The county advises that flood risk remains. Read the source zone subtype and assess the property’s actual exposure separately.

description: Compare Invariant Earth, Regrid, LightBox, Landstats, BatchData, Parceled and other GIS MCP servers. Test parcel matches and original source records.

intro: Use Invariant Earth to compare the U.S. parcel at an address with flood zones, terrain and nearby infrastructure in one agent workflow. Regrid, LightBox and West Kite offer different property and parcel workflows. ArcGIS Enterprise can expose the maps and tools your organization already runs. Test each connector against the same sites and save the tool responses alongside the agent’s answer.
takeaways: Choose the server by the decision you need to support. Identify the datasets and tool permissions available through that connection.
Test the address, parcel and building separately. Keep the original identifier, the source and the date returned with each result.
Use the same locations and evidence requirements across providers. Ask the serving utility for a project-specific service record before using mapped infrastructure for a power decision.

sections.heading: Which GIS MCP server should you evaluate?

blocks.text: An MCP server gives an AI client a catalog of tools it can call. The connection determines which records and actions are available to the client. The comparison below uses the providers’ published documentation. Check the tool list and account entitlement in your own client.

rows: Invariant Earth
U.S. point facts, parcel enrichment, address geocoding, field catalog search and proximity.
Can you match the parcel, return a mapped field with its source, and show the nearest infrastructure in the same screening workflow?
Regrid
Parcel and property data through its MCP connector, using API credentials for data queries.
Can you match a parcel by address and return the boundary and zoning attributes included in your account?
LightBox MCP
Read-only property and parcel research for selected customers and partners through early access.
Can you trace a parcel match to the correct assessment when a single geometry covers several units?
West Kite
U.S. commercial property research, including owners of record and people behind LLCs.
Can you distinguish the recorded owner from a linked person or entity and show the evidence for the relationship?
MCP for ArcGIS Enterprise
Access to permitted GIS content and tools in an organization’s ArcGIS Enterprise deployment.
Can you find the approved internal layer and use it to answer the same site question within the user’s permissions?
CARTO MCP Server
Publish geospatial workflows built by your team as tools an agent can call.
Use the same parcel polygon with two dated layer versions. Check that the workflow returns the layer version and shows when a repeated call reuses a cached result.

sections.heading: Compare property MCP servers by the job

blocks.text: Use Invariant Earth to resolve an address, check the matched parcel, and inspect terrain, flood, or infrastructure fields with the available source references. To choose a connector for a portfolio or new integration, compare all candidates on the same inputs and save what each one returns.

columns: What to check in your trial
rows: Landstats
Query parcel polygons at coordinates, filter attributes, or search for centroids in a shape. Bring a separate geocoder for street addresses. The older LandRecords.us documentation redirects here.
At the published Brooklyn Army Terminal coordinate, run parcel_at_point. Compare the returned boundary with the shoreline-clipped city parcel. Save which boundary was tested.
BatchData
Look up property details, search for candidate properties and request comparables for data enabled on the account.
At the same address, check the property matched before using its comps. Save the reported sale date, source, and record identity for each comparable.
Parceled
Check which datasets are available at a point, then request parcel, zoning, building, assessor, or permit fields from the catalog.
Check availability first. For any roof permit returned, retain the permit number, issue date, and issuer link. Record whether a field was unavailable or returned no matching rows.
MAIA Analytics
Import an address CSV or GeoJSON into a project and check parcel-match and unmatched-row counts.
In a test project, import the same public address sample. Compare the matched, unmatched and out-of-county totals before trusting the joined layer.

blocks.text: Try longitude −74.0271955 and latitude 40.6451992 at Brooklyn Army Terminal. The city comparison placed that point about 9 meters outside the clipped lot. A connector can return a nearby match or a different boundary edition. Check geometry, match type, and source vintage before using it to join owner, permit or flood records.

sections.heading: How do you connect Invariant Earth?

blocks.text: Add https://api.invariant-ai.com/mcp as the remote server using Streamable HTTP. Follow the installation guide for your client to sign in or use the client’s secret storage for an Invariant API key. The public registry lists io.github.in-variant/invariant-earth. On November 24, the endpoint returned an authentication challenge and linked to its OAuth resource metadata.

Start with an address lookup. Use invariant_geocode for the normalized address and point, invariant_enrich for a parcel match, and invariant_fetch for facts at a point. Ask the agent to show the result status and the available sources in the response. For driving distance or proximity, use invariant_proximity. The separate invariant_request_field tool creates a request for missing data.

items.label: Connect Invariant Earth and copy the setup prompt

sections.heading: Run the same three tests across providers

blocks.text: Give every agent the same prompt, keep the raw tool response and check it against the dated city and FEMA references. Preserve a leading zero in a parcel number. When a coordinate falls outside a lot, ask the agent to explain the match status before it assigns ownership or lot-level risk.

rows: San Francisco Main Library
Which parcel matches 100 Larkin Street? Preserve leading zeros and report how the address matched.
City records identify parcel 0354001 and place the address point inside it.
Brooklyn Army Terminal
Does the published facility coordinate fall inside the shoreline-clipped MapPLUTO lot? Which FEMA zone contains the coordinate?
The coordinate fell about nine meters outside city tax lot 3057780001 and was in Zone AE.
214 3rd Street, Brooklyn
Compare the address point, tax lot and building with the effective FEMA layer.
The address point fell outside the special flood hazard area. The mapped area covered 52.7% of the lot and 24.7% of the building.

blocks.text: The findings above come from the reference records. To score a provider, log the matched geometry, source, map or dataset date, and missing fields beside its answer. When results differ, compare the vintages and methods first. A connector may answer a point question while its available tools leave a building-overlap question open.

blocks.label: Download the trial prompts and dated reference observations

blocks.text: The versioned GitHub release has the dated reference files, checksums and an offline replay script. Use those files to check the references before scoring live answers.

sections.heading: Which parcel tools give an agent source evidence?

blocks.text: Start with one field that matters to the decision, such as the parcel boundary or the current flood zone. Ask the agent for the record or layer that produced it, the date it applied, and the retrieval time. Save the raw tool result to see which of those details came back. A link to a provider’s catalog can explain the dataset. To verify a specific value, ask for the issuing agency’s record, a query against its layer, or a source file you can inspect.

columns: What to check in a trial
rows: Invariant Earth

Earth documents a source, source URL, result status and retrieval time for field results, with dataset vintage where available. Its elevation example points to a USGS tile. The field catalog identifies Regrid as the source of parcel_id.
Keep the elevation and parcel evidence separate. Check whether each URL opens a source file, a dataset page, or a provider reference. Use the local tax map for independent boundary confirmation.
Regrid
The parcel schema distinguishes sourceurl, a county record URL where supplied, from ll_last_refresh, the county data refresh date, and ll_updated_at, the row modification time.
Ask for sourceurl and ll_last_refresh on your county sample. For an as-of boundary, confirm the local map edition and the date any split took effect.
LightBox
The parcel API documents lookup by county FIPS and assessor parcel number, plus links to related assessments. LightBox describes MCP access separately through its Early Access Program.
In the early-access connector, ask for the local assessor number, its linked assessment, the original source, and the relevant dates. Check which items the tool returns.
West Kite
The property API documents source IDs on typed items including sales, assessments and permits. Its source catalog describes the publisher, coverage, and last load for each entry where recorded.
Resolve the source ID to its catalog entry. Ask for the local permit or deed reference and event date as separate evidence.

blocks.text: These are documented fields and access paths. Use your plan and client to confirm which details appear in the MCP response. For underwriting, keep the source identifiers and dates beside the value that drove the decision so someone else can repeat the check.

sections.heading: Replay a parcel answer against the city record

blocks.text: Give each connector commercial unit lot 1012921303 at 432 Park Avenue in Manhattan. Ask whether the unit has its own polygon in the Digital Tax Map and which IDs refer to the billing lot and the underlying land. Ask for the city query supporting each result, with the source edition or tax year where available.

columns: What to keep in the agent’s answer
rows: Unit record
Unit 1012921303 links to base lot 1012920033. The unit row lists effective tax year 2016–2017.
Keep the unit BBL as the tax record ID and label 1012920033 as its parent.
Geometry
The Digital Tax Map polygon layer returns zero rows for unit 1012921303.
Report zero in the named layer. Label a returned parent polygon as parent geometry.
Billing lot
MapPLUTO 26v3 lists 1012927502 at 432 Park Avenue. The Finance condominium table links it to base lot 1012920033.
Keep the MapPLUTO billing ID, edition, and Finance relationship as separate evidence.

blocks.text: Review the saved tool response before accepting the answer. A catalog link can identify the provider’s dataset. The city query shows whether the precise lot and geometry claim holds. Keep the lookup time separate from the effective tax year and the MapPLUTO edition. Flag a discrepancy when a connector reports the whole building as a match for the individual unit.

Download the Python replay for the four city queries

blocks.text: The replay uses public city endpoints and reports any difference from the saved record values. It needs no API key. Run the prompt separately through Invariant Earth, Regrid, or LightBox to record what your connector returns under your account.

sections.heading: What should an agent show before you use a site answer?

blocks.text: Ask for the matched address, the parcel identifier and the named source for each fact. For a time-sensitive decision, ask for the date the record applied as well as when it was retrieved. Check missing or unmatched data explicitly before the result enters an underwriting file, a land shortlist or a site approval memo.

The power screen can identify a mapped utility territory and nearby substations. Record the serving utility, facility megawatts and date needed, then request written evidence for the point of connection, the first available service phase and its conditions.

title: Best GIS APIs for U.S. site selection
description: Compare GIS APIs for U.S. site selection. Replay parcel pagination in NYC and test parcel matching, flood overlap and source evidence in three locations.
coverAlt: Aerial map of Brooklyn Army Terminal with the shoreline-clipped tax lot outlined in white, Zone AE on the lot shaded blue, and the published coordinate marked just outside the boundary.
coverCaption: Brooklyn Army Terminal. The white outline is the MapPLUTO 26v2 tax lot, blue shows FEMA Zone AE within it, and the gold dot marks the published coordinate. Aerial imagery from NYS ITS, spring 2024.
intro: Use Invariant Earth to screen known U.S. sites across parcels, terrain, hazards and infrastructure with sources for each field. When the search starts with a drawn area, identify which parcel boundaries intersect it, then screen the matches. The examples below show what changes when you query a point, a parcel or a building. For a large electrical load, use a project study to find which connection options warrant review by the utility.
takeaways: Test the exact counties and fields where you plan to operate. A national map can still have uneven coverage for permits, zoning, or owner data.
A site pin, a tax lot, and a proposed building can return different hazard results. Ask which geometry an API evaluated.
For every decision-critical field, keep the source, observation date, and status alongside the value.

sections.heading: Which provider fits the job?

blocks.text: Invariant makes Invariant Earth. We reviewed public product documentation from November 22 to 25, 2026. The San Francisco and Brooklyn checks use city and federal records. The comparison describes documented capabilities and checks to run in a vendor trial.

rows: Invariant Earth
Screening known sites with parcel, terrain, hazard and infrastructure fields, with source links, vintages and status.
Run the same inputs through Fetch and Enrich. Check the parcel match near a boundary and retain the source and date for each field.
Esri ArcGIS Location Platform
Geocoding, basemaps, routing, and publishing spatial layers.
Check how geocodes resolve on large campuses. Confirm that the plan supports storing geocodes and serving your own data layers.
CARTO
Spatial analysis in a cloud data warehouse, with datasets available through the Data Observatory.
Ask for the parcel and zoning datasets needed in your counties. Check the licensed fields and update dates, then rerun the polygon query in your warehouse.
Google Earth Engine
Geospatial processing across image collections and vector assets, with JavaScript, Python and REST interfaces.
Bring the same parcel polygon and select a named image collection and date range. Record the projection and scale used for an area statistic, then verify what the export preserves.
Regrid
Parcel boundaries, APN lookups and searches by GeoJSON geometry.
Test a recent split and a narrow polygon that crosses parcel boundaries. Check county refresh dates for the fields you need.
GetParcelData
Parcel searches by point, radius or WKT polygon.
Check whether partial overlaps qualify and whether pagination returns every match. Confirm data vintage for the counties in scope.
Parceled
Parcel lookups, hosted parcel tiles and linked assessor, permit and zoning fields.
Check parcel and permit coverage separately for each county. Test a parcel whose permit history you can verify.
West Kite
Commercial property research across owners, deeds, assessments, permits, and site context.
Start with its county-level coverage. Test whether the deed, permit, or mortgage that matters to your team is available for the exact property.
Mireye
Location enrichment and screening with source information across land, hazards, and infrastructure.
Ask for the source, spatial method, and missing-value behavior for the same point and parcel. Check which tools accept a polygon.
Geoforge
Shareable power screening reports with modeled load and generation headroom, queue context, and planned upgrades.
Check the study year, load direction, and assumptions for each candidate connection. Ask how you can export the data behind the report.
Paces
Finding and screening data center sites with power and development constraints in one workflow.
Ask for a shortlist using your phased load and service dates. Verify how the workflow handles utility feedback, site control, and evidence for each milestone.
PVcase Prospect
Map-based site screening, with withdrawal capacity studies for data center loads.
Check which connection, load case, and study year the capacity layer represents. Verify the site and power questions that still need utility evidence.
Ageospatial
Property and infrastructure intelligence for insurance and credit workflows.
Give it a schedule with multiple buildings at one address. Inspect the evidence behind the building match and risk inputs.

sections.heading: Find parcels that intersect a drawn area

blocks.text: Our Civic Center test in San Francisco used a narrow rectangle to find parcels along Larkin Street. It intersected city lots 0353001 and 0354001, even though neither lot’s centroid fell inside the rectangle. Run the same geometry against an area-search API and check which parcels it returns, whether it includes edge touches and how it pages the result. Preserve the parcel numbers as text so both leading zeros survive.

Once you have the full parcel list, verify an interior point for each candidate. Use Earth to check the parcel match and enrich the selected sites with fields such as slope and flood classification. Save the area search and enrichment responses separately so you can trace which record supports each result.

sections.heading: How do you know a parcel API returned every match?

blocks.text: Run a count with the same polygon, filters and source edition, then compare it with the unique feature IDs collected from every page. A successful request can still return a partial list. For a buyer screening an area, those missing rows never reach the eligibility check.

A November 26 replay around Brooklyn’s Sunset Park waterfront returned 2,244 features in NYC MapPLUTO 26v3. The first page stopped at the layer’s 2,000-record limit and reported that more records matched. Starting the second request at offset 2,000 returned the remaining 244. The two pages contained all 2,244 object IDs from the independent ID query.

blocks.text: Use object IDs to reconcile records within the queried layer. Keep the borough, block and lot number (BBL) as text for joining to other property records. ArcGIS documents returnIdsOnly=true for listing matching feature IDs. Regrid documents return_count for the count and offset_id for paging. For Invariant Earth, keep the area-search result beside the parcel and site evidence you retrieve for each candidate.

sections.heading: A real parcel test at Brooklyn Army Terminal

blocks.text: For Brooklyn Army Terminal tax lot 3057780001, FEMA returned Zone AE at the coordinate published in MapPLUTO. The point was about 9 meters outside the shoreline-clipped tax lot. When we intersected the lot itself with the same FEMA layer, 19.9% of its area was in Zone AE and 80.1% was in Zone X. Zone X within this lot includes both the 0.2% annual chance hazard area and the area FEMA maps as minimal hazard.

We queried NYC MapPLUTO 26v2 by borough, block, and lot, then pulled FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer polygons from layer 28 around the lot. We projected the geometry to UTM zone 18N, intersected and grouped the polygons by FEMA zone and subtype, and divided each overlap by the clipped parcel area. The calculation uses mapped land area. For a particular structure, run the intersection again on its building footprint. The downloadable file contains the exact source queries, coordinate, lot, and clipped zone geometry.

sections.heading: Run the same checks before you sign

blocks.text: Give each vendor the same three inputs. Use a tract whose county record you have in hand, a parcel that recently split, and a site where a hazard boundary crosses the property. Agree on the reference records and the assessment date before looking at any result.

columns: What you should be able to verify
rows: Parcel match
The returned assessor parcel number and geometry correspond to the tract, including where an address spans multiple parcels.
Owner and date
You can identify the owner of record, the record that supports the result, and the relevant filing or publication date.
Hazard coverage
You can see the exact layer and distinguish a point lookup, a parcel intersection, and a building-footprint intersection.
Infrastructure
You can identify the actual asset, the source and date, and how the distance was measured. A capacity figure comes with a connection point, study case, and project assumptions.
History
You can tell what was known at an earlier decision date, how later corrections are handled, and what happens to identifiers during splits and merges.
Gaps and rights
You can tell an unmatched record from unavailable coverage or a failed request. The license covers how you plan to store and share results.

sections.heading: Run a GIS API trial with five requests and three reference sites

blocks.text: Start with a clean parcel match, an address point outside a published lot and a hazard boundary that crosses a building. The download gives you the coordinates and request bodies for all three. We checked the request fields against the public API catalogs and the request shape against the deployed specification. The reference observations come from city and FEMA records. Run the authenticated requests with your own API key to collect the responses.

rows: San Francisco Main Library
The city address point falls inside parcel 0354001.
Request the parcel boundary and APN. Check the returned geometry, and preserve the leading zero in the city identifier.
Brooklyn Army Terminal
The published city point lies 9.06 meters outside the shoreline-clipped lot and is in FEMA Zone AE.
Run both endpoints at the same coordinate. If the point call uses a nearby parcel, keep its match type and distance. Check which shoreline convention the returned boundary uses.
214 3rd Street, Brooklyn
The city address point falls outside the mapped Special Flood Hazard Area. The dated overlay puts 52.7% of the lot and 24.7% of the building inside it.
Keep the point result, parcel overlap and building-footprint overlap in separate fields. Compare the fraction returned for the parcel with the percentage in the reference.

blocks.text: POST /v1/fetch answers fields at the requested coordinate. Its parcel fields can fall back to the nearest parcel, so read the match type and distance. POST /v1/enrich requires a containing parcel and reports nearby candidates without enriching them. When a field has no value, check partial_failures and field status for Fetch, or field_omissions for Enrich. Use the returned analysis point when comparing point fields from Enrich.

Run the three reference cases from one ZIP with Python 3.10 or newer. The release includes the script, the dated JSON and GeoJSON files, and SHA-256 checksums. The default run works offline. Add the API key and live flag when you want to compare an Earth response.

sections.heading: What Invariant Earth returns

blocks.text: The public catalogs listed 371 point fields and 504 parcel enrichment fields across 14 presets when checked on November 24, 2026. Enrichment includes some of the same point fields. Use the live catalogs to confirm the fields you need, then save each response’s source and retrieval time. Keep the dataset vintage when it is supplied.

Use the coordinate API to build an initial evidence file. For a historical boundary, ask for the exact prior dataset or a working as-of lookup before building around it. For a load study, carry the parcel, phased megawatts, target dates, and candidate connection points into a project-specific review.

faqs.question: What is the best GIS API for parcel boundaries?
faqs.answer: Regrid is a starting point for standardized U.S. parcel boundaries and APN searches. Test its results against the assessor or cadastral record in each target county. Include a known parcel split to see how identifiers and geometry behave across releases.

faqs.question: Can a GIS API tell me how much power a site can get?
faqs.answer: A GIS API can identify candidate substations, lines, and service territories. Some products also expose utility capacity maps or model estimates. For a specific load and schedule, confirm the proposed service point, study conditions, needed upgrades, and utility service terms.

faqs.question: Can I compare a property now with the same property at an earlier date?
faqs.answer: Ask which historical snapshots, source-effective dates, and revisions are available for each field. To reconstruct an earlier decision, you need the records or versions available at that time. A recent fetch timestamp only tells you when the source was read.

title: Hail History by Address and APIs for Commercial Insurance
description: Compare hail history APIs with a real Denver storm. Check NOAA radar, nearby reports and FEMA tract frequency before using a result in property underwriting.
coverAlt: Radar map for May 30, 2024 in Denver. Sample points A and B both match a nearby 2.75-inch hail report. Their nearest radar cells show 1.42 and 0.55 inches.
coverCaption: Four-hour peak radar estimates and selected reports for the Denver storm. A and B are sample locations. Source data from NOAA MRMS and NCEI Storm Events.
intro: To check hail history by address, locate the building on the policy or submission. Then search dated hail reports around it and read the radar grid over the building for the same time window. Nearby reports document what was reported at other locations. Radar estimates help decide where to look more closely. Roof condition comes from records or an inspection tied to the building.
takeaways: Use Invariant Earth for the property match and tract-level hail frequency. Compare dated weather records at the matched coordinates.
Store the distance and reported hail size separately from the radar estimate at the building.
Record missing radar data and unresolved roof condition explicitly.

sections.heading: Two points in the same Denver hailstorm

blocks.text: On May 30, 2024, severe storms crossed metropolitan Denver. We took two illustrative locations 4.15 km apart and searched the same NOAA hail episode from 8 p.m. to midnight Mountain Daylight Time. For each point we kept records with a published start location and a reported hail size within 5 km. Both searches returned the same 2.75-inch report as their largest. The point nearest that report had a radar estimate of 1.42 inches. The other had a radar estimate of 0.55 inches.

blocks.text: The radius search describes the neighborhood around each point. The radar product estimates hail size for cells about a kilometer across. The sample uses the nearest grid center without interpolation. For a real address match, identify the building footprint and the relevant roof sections before using either result.
Run the Python example on the original NOAA archives to verify the report counts and radar estimates. You can change the search radius or coordinates for this same storm.

sections.heading: Check the time zone and the units

blocks.text: Storm Events records the 2.75-inch report start as May 30 at 21:12 with the offset MST-7. That converts to 10:12 p.m. on May 30 in Denver daylight time and 04:12 UTC on May 31. The matching radar window spans 02:00 to 06:00 UTC on May 31. A search restricted to May 30 UTC would miss the evening storm.

The radar product is NOAA’s Maximum Estimated Size of Hail, or MESH. Its 240-minute file stores each cell’s peak estimate for the preceding four hours in millimeters. Divide by 25.4 to compare those values with reports in inches. Keep the timestamp and window length together so a later reader can reproduce the search.

An earlier file ending at 8 p.m. local time returned the raw code −1 for both cells. NOAA lists −1 as missing and −3 as no coverage. Store the numeric estimate as unknown alongside the original code. In the download, each source file has a URL and checksum. The download uses a later version of the bulk archive. For a point-in-time review, use the file version you actually had on the decision date.

sections.heading: How to compare hail history APIs on the same two points

blocks.text: Run the same coordinates and storm window through each provider. Save the geometry each result actually describes. A tract frequency helps screen the portfolio. A radar cell or reported event helps review a particular storm. For building-level underwriting, link both to the confirmed roof and its inspection or repair history.

blocks.text: The two FEMA annualized frequencies agree to two decimals, even though the coordinates fall in different tracts. Half Mile Hail returned one detection day for the same tile in both 2024 lookups. The eight rows for that date contained seven distinct combinations of time, radar, cell identifier and location. Count distinct storm days or deduplicated records as the job requires. Half Mile Hail uses NOAA’s NEXRAD Level III hail detections. The finer NOAA estimates above come from the separate MRMS MESH product.

Parceled describes hail history as an intersection of MESH swaths with parcels. We checked the documented public availability endpoint. Its anonymous response supplied no event date for either point. A true flag is a reason to request history for that parcel, and a false flag is a reason to resolve availability before scoring the property. Both points had dated evidence in the independent NOAA check.

sections.heading: Which hail history API fits an underwriting workflow?

blocks.text: Use Invariant Earth for cited parcel and building context and the tract-level hail frequency that helps prioritize a portfolio. For a dated event, pair that property record with a source that exposes the storm time and the radius, radar cell or parcel intersection behind its result. The public checks above cover FEMA, Half Mile Hail and Parceled availability. The other capabilities below come from published product documentation.

columns: What to ask for in a trial
rows: Invariant Earth
Parcel and building context plus FEMA tract-level hail frequency in events per year.
Return the matched parcel and building evidence, the source vintage and hail_annual_frequency. Verify the roof separately when an address spans multiple structures.
Parceled
Parcel intersections with radar-estimated hail swaths.
For matching parcels, request dated event history, the swath unit and size threshold, and the meaning of missing coverage in that market.
PerilIQ
Nearby observed weather reports with a configurable radius and source links.
Get the original NWS report and distance. Check whether a date filter follows the report date, local calendar day or UTC.
Verisk Benchmark
Location-specific weather history for claims and underwriting. Its sample shows separate estimates at an address and within one and five miles.
Request all three result scopes and the date of loss. Keep the address estimate separate from each radius maximum.
NOAA Storm Events, SWDI and MRMS
Original reports, radar detections and archived grids for a reproducible reference check.
Save event IDs and exact file versions. Record the cell resolution, time window, and the original missing-data code.

Address and building identifier, footprint, geocode precision and match date.
Links the record to the building. A campus address can cover several roofs.

Documents a report near the building. Report counts can include multiple records from one storm.
Radar estimate
Product, source file, window, cell center, units, estimate or missing code.
Shows modeled exposure near a location during that window and helps prioritize follow-up.
Roof record
Roof section, covering, last verified installation, inspection date and scope of any repair.
Helps establish which roof was present during the storm and which sections have evidence of condition or work.

blocks.text: For a new submission or renewal, confirm the building and get the roof’s installation and repair history. Ask for a dated inspection or contractor record tied to the roof sections when condition is material to the review. Keep the weather finding with the evidence used for that decision date. When a report or repair record arrives later, add it with its own date so the prior review remains reproducible.

faqs.question: How can I find hail history by address?
faqs.answer: Locate the insured building, run a dated radius search for NOAA hail reports, then sample the radar grid at the building for the same window. Keep each report’s distance and date, the radar product and any missing-data flag.

faqs.question: Can a nearby 2.75-inch hail report tell me the hail size at the building?
faqs.answer: It gives the reported size at the recorded location. The building needs its own exposure assessment. Radar estimates the size over an area, and inspection evidence helps establish the roof’s actual condition.

faqs.question: What does a missing radar value mean?
faqs.answer: The product did not provide a numeric estimate for that cell and window. For the NOAA 240-minute MESH product, −1 marks missing and −3 marks no coverage. Keep the code and leave the numeric estimate blank.

faqs.question: Does annualized hail frequency show what happened at an address on a specific day?
faqs.answer: FEMA’s annualized hail frequency estimates long-run events per year across a Census tract. To check a date of loss, use dated report and radar records for the location and retain the matched building and roof evidence.

title: Best commercial property data APIs for insurance underwriting
description: Compare commercial property data APIs for underwriting. See how to match buildings, verify roof permit closeout, and check historical flood and hail evidence.
coverAlt: Aerial view of Brooklyn Army Terminal, with the small footprint returned by the city’s Building A identifier marked in gold for review.
coverCaption: The gold outline is the footprint returned by the city building-ID lookup. Aerial imagery from NYS ITS, spring 2024. Tax lot from NYC MapPLUTO 26v2.
intro: Use Invariant Earth when your underwriting team needs to verify the parcel and inspect the sources behind building and hazard fields. Evaluate Cotality for building prefill and reconstruction cost, Moody’s CAPE for imagery-derived roof attributes, Verisk for commercial underwriting reports, and Guidewire HazardHub for peril and fire-protection data. First Street provides modeled flood depth and damage. Compare Ageospatial for building and property evidence workflows. Use the scorecard below to test shared addresses, roof records and evidence that changes after the quote date.
takeaways: Match each line of the statement of values to a building before pulling construction or hazard attributes.
Keep permit issuance, the work it authorizes, and evidence of completion as separate fields.
Keep parcel-level hazard flags, a building’s modeled flood depth, and potential insured loss distinct in the record.

guideActions.label: Verify the building in your submission

sections.heading: Which building is on the submission?

blocks.text: A statement of values lists the locations and values submitted for insurance. Consider a line for Building A at Brooklyn Army Terminal, 140 58th Street. The city’s municipal benchmarking report identifies Building A as Building Identification Number (BIN) 3257059 on tax lot 3057780001. The operator’s specification describes eight stories, a height of 89 feet, and approximately 500,000 square feet of floor area. We used those records to check what the building lookup returned.

The exact BIN matched a footprint in NYC’s building dataset on that tax lot. The footprint record reported a roof height of 14 feet and a construction year of 2022. Those values disagree with the operator’s description of Building A. Preserve the returned outline as a candidate, ask for a verified building plan or footprint, and leave building-level exposure pending. This is a useful test even for providers that report a confident address match.

The same campus illustrates what can happen downstream. Our parcel screen found a FEMA Zone AE overlap on 19.9% of the shoreline-clipped lot. Copying that result to a building record would change the scope of the evidence. After resolving the building outline, intersect it with the relevant map edition and keep the map, geometry and date used for the result.

sections.heading: What does a roof permit tell you about roof age?

blocks.text: NYC issued permit B01209484-I1-GC on June 17, 2026, for work including re-roofing on Building A. The description covers the main roof and tank house roofs and excludes the stair tower and mechanical penthouse roofs. Another record for October 6 covers temporary roof protection. Keep both events with their own dates and scopes.

The June record supports the scope of authorized work. To use it for roof age, look for a completion record, a signed contractor document, or inspection evidence that ties the installation date to the sections being insured. The checked records leave the last replacement date open. On renewal, keep the June and October evidence and append any new completion record with its own date.

Seattle reports completion separately from issuance. For the Alki Community Center, the city records a March 2018 closeout for 5,400 square feet of permitted re-roofing. Use the same checks on scope and dates when comparing results across cities.

sections.heading: How to verify a roof permit and final inspection by address

blocks.text: Start with the permit number and insured building. A search of Los Angeles’s inspection feed using the hyphenated permit numbers returned zero rows for three roof permits. The feed stores the same number groups with spaces. The space-separated query returned three inspection rows for one of those permits, including the final inspection. Keep the original strings from both systems and use the normalized number to join them.

columns: What to enter in the underwriting file
rows: Permit issued September 28, 2026, for 20 roofing squares over existing sheathing. Final inspection October 20. Permit status date October 21.
Retain both dates and 2,000 square feet of permitted scope. Ask which roof sections and layers the work covered before dating the whole roof.

Both permits were issued November 17, 2026, at the same address and parcel. One lists 810 roofing squares and the other 81. Both descriptions also mention coating. The queried feed returned no inspection rows for either permit.
Keep the two issued scopes separate. Ask for the permit plan or roof diagram to determine whether the areas overlap, describe different sections, or reflect a correction.

blocks.text: A roofing square is 100 square feet. Converting the permitted quantity gives the area named in the permit. For coverage of the insured building, compare it with a dated roof plan. The Los Angeles re-roofing certificate includes fields for the building address, permit number, signer and date. Request the completed certificate, scope and any roof diagram to tie the work to an insured roof section. Keep the exact installation date and current condition open when the record only shows permit closeout.

sections.heading: What can an API prefill for commercial property?

blocks.text: Commercial property underwriters organize building information around construction, occupancy, protection, and exposure, often called COPE. Start with the submission and compare its answers with the records you can trace to that building. Keep the construction and hazard evidence alongside the values the insured has submitted for the property and its contents.

rows: Construction
Year built, stories, gross floor area, roof cover, and dates of recorded work.
Confirm which structure the source describes. Separate footprint area from total floor area and a permit date from completion.
Occupancy
Use documented for the premises, tenant entries, and building or suite identifiers.
Ask the applicant about actual operations, storage, and vacancies. A property’s land-use category describes a different unit than a tenant’s operation.
Protection
Documented fire protection, hydrant and station context, and system inspection records.
Verify sprinkler coverage and condition for the premises being insured. Use the carrier’s data rules for protection class.
Exposure
Map or modeled evidence for flood, wildfire, wind, and surrounding properties.
Save whether the analysis used an address pin, parcel or footprint. Keep the map edition or scenario, and separate hazard intensity from damage.
Reported values
Building, business personal property, and business interruption values in the submission, plus a reconstruction estimate where available.
Reconcile valuation scope with the insured. Check the estimator’s assumptions about materials, local costs, and excluded items.

sections.heading: Which providers should you test?

blocks.text: The options below are based on public product documentation. Invariant publishes this guide and makes Invariant Earth. The Brooklyn example tests public records directly and gives you an input to run through a trial or demo with each provider.

columns: Ask to see in a trial
rows: Cotality
Commercial prefill, occupancy information, and commercial reconstruction cost estimates.
A multi-building site with a cost result tied to each building and a list of assumptions behind the estimate.
Moody’s CAPE
Commercial building and roof attributes from imagery, including condition ratings, reason codes, and change detection.
The imagery date and building ID for each condition result. Ask how the API and review interface handle unclear imagery or more than one roof on a schedule line.
Verisk
Commercial underwriting reports through its API, including U.S. LOCATION and ProMetrix products.
Which U.S. report covers your commercial portfolio, the property ID it uses, and the fields returned at building versus location level.
Guidewire HazardHub
An API for property characteristics, peril scores, and fire-suppression context.
The underlying variables, source dates, and the location geometry used for a flood or fire-protection result.
ZestyAI
Roof age and condition signals from imagery and records, with an API for its roof age estimates.
Whether the result is an estimate or based on observed work, which roof sections it covers, and whether the product supports your property types.
Nearmap Betterview
Imagery-derived property insights, roof condition indicators, and hazard information for insurance workflows.
For two buildings on one lot, verify the building that received each roof result. Check the imagery capture date and whether you can retain it with the quote record.
First Street
Modeled flood depths and damage metrics with scenario, return period, and time horizon.
A footprint result and a coordinate-only case. Verify how the model reports depth when an outline is unavailable.
Ageospatial
Building evidence for insurers drawn from imagery, maps, records, and documents.
How a line on a schedule is tied to a footprint, how conflicting building attributes surface, and what history can be exported.
ATTOM
Property characteristics such as year built, construction type, and roof cover in its property API.
A large commercial property split across structures. Ask which fields describe the primary structure and which aggregate across the site.
West Kite
Commercial property records and permits tied to properties, with dated sources.
A permit lookup for Building A and a walkthrough of how the API preserves the filing date, issuance, scope, and later status.
Invariant Earth
Location and parcel context, including hazard layers and field-level provenance and status.
The coordinate and parcel response for a known property, with the source and dataset vintage. Validate the building separately before attaching exposure to it.

sections.heading: How to evaluate an underwriting data API

blocks.text: Start with the public scorecard in the underwriting guides. It gives every provider the same four cases and seven checks, with expected handling and links to the evidence. Record the product and version you tested, run the same requests, and keep the original responses. Use Pass, Fail, Needs review, or Unsupported for each check. An API passes a case such as Brooklyn Building A when it makes the uncertainty visible and leaves the affected field unresolved.

blocks.text: Then run a sample of your own book with a verified single-building control, shared addresses, partially replaced roofs, and unmatched inputs. Include different building uses, size bands and jurisdictions. Score matches against independently verified references. Keep ambiguous cases in the review queue and use them to test how the provider handles uncertainty.

rows: Correct building match rate
Divide verified correct matches by all submitted building lines with an independently verified building. Report wrong matches and unresolved lines separately against the same denominator.
Evidence-backed field coverage

For each requested field, divide the number of eligible trials with a usable value, source, date and correct scope by all trials eligible for that field. Include unsupported results in the denominator and record confirmed errors separately.
Review rate
Divide the number of lines referred to an underwriter by all submitted lines. Measure time from referral to disposition and record API latency separately.
Replay at renewal
Re-run a previous quote using the recorded inputs and date. Count a replay as successful when you can reproduce what the underwriter saw and explain any changes in the later review.

blocks.text: Set the acceptance criteria before the trial. For fields that change a quote, specify which wrong-building matches or unsupported values require manual review. Confirm you can retain the original evidence and share what the carrier or client needs under the provider’s license.

faqs.question: Can a commercial property API tell me when a roof was last replaced?
faqs.answer: Some providers supply a recorded date or an estimate. Check which roof sections the claim covers and what supports it. A permit issue date establishes when the work was authorized. A dated completion or inspection record can substantiate when the work happened.

faqs.question: What is the difference between flood zone and flood damage?
faqs.answer: A flood zone comes from a particular mapped layer. Modeled flood depth describes inundation for a stated event and scenario. A damage estimate also depends on factors such as first-floor elevation and building vulnerability. Insured loss requires applying coverage terms to the damage.

faqs.question: What should a prefill response include when the building cannot be matched?
faqs.answer: Keep the submitted building and candidate identifiers, state that the match requires review, and leave building-level fields unfilled. Include the evidence that disagrees, such as a footprint height or building name, and name the document needed to resolve it.

faqs.question: Which date should an underwriter use for a re-roofing permit?
faqs.answer: Store the issue date, final inspection date and date of the permit status separately. Use a completed certificate, contractor record or similar evidence for the installation date, and identify the roof section before applying that date to a building. At 403 S Mathews St, the final inspection was October 20, 2026 and the finaled status date was October 21.

title: Historical parcel boundaries API guide for splits and mergers
description: Trace an old parcel ID through a split or merger. Compare two real NYC tax map changes with dated boundaries, source queries, and a downloadable crosswalk.
coverAlt: Side-by-side boundary maps show Brooklyn block 3947 before and after its November 20 split. Lot 1 shrinks from about 45,290 to 24,121 square feet, and new lot 105 takes about 21,169 square feet.
coverCaption: Brooklyn block 3947. Same scale before and after. Boundaries from MapPLUTO 26v2 and NYC Tax Lot Polygon, checked against tax map alteration 738545. Areas are calculated from mapped geometry.
intro: A historical parcel lookup needs two things. The boundary that applied on the date you care about, and the relation between that parcel and the lots that came before or after it. A current parcel ID can survive even when its footprint changes. In Brooklyn on November 20, 2026, lot 1 on block 3947 kept its ID after a split, with about 53% of its former mapped area. A merger on another block that day retired two IDs and enlarged a third.
takeaways: Store dated geometry separately from the parcel number and keep both versions when the source preserves the same ID.
Use the local alteration record to tell a split from a merger, a map correction, or a new survey.
Validate the match with the old and new geometries, then keep source edition, change date, and observation date in the result.

guideActions.label: Trace a parcel split or merger

sections.heading: A split where the old ID stayed in use

blocks.text: On Brooklyn block 3947, NYC’s older tax map shows one lot, numbered 1, at the Atlantic Avenue end of the block. The November 20 map shows lot 1 and lot 105 separated by a new internal boundary. Alteration 738545 labels lot 1 affected and lot 105 new. The borough, block, and lot identifier, known as a BBL in New York City, gives lot 1 the same value of 3039470001 on both versions.

The predecessor footprint measured about 45,290 square feet in the earlier geometry. After the split, the two footprints measured about 24,121 and 21,169 square feet. A query for the old BBL against today’s parcel layer can return lot 1 successfully and still omit almost half of the original footprint. The crosswalk returns both successors for an old record and assigns each boundary its own record ID.

sections.heading: A merger where two IDs disappeared

sections.heading: How to reproduce the join

blocks.text: Query the city’s alteration tables by transaction number for the change date, type, and lot actions. The example uses the older MapPLUTO 26v2 geometry and the city’s later Tax Lot Polygon service. Check the IDs and shapes against the before and after maps in the tax map library. The GeoJSON includes the exact queries and both map URLs for each transaction.

Keep geometry in longitude and latitude for interchange. For the area check, reproject the downloaded shapes to the New York Long Island State Plane coordinate system, EPSG:2263. For each event, union the polygons on each side and compare the mapped coverage. In these two cases, the difference between the old and new unions was below one square foot. This confirms the shape relationship at the precision of these files. The alteration record supplies the event classification.

Run the Python example against the downloaded GeoJSON to retrieve both versions of a lot that kept its number, or follow a retired lot to its successor. For a new site, use the local archive for past boundaries and record the current parcel match, boundary and source dates through Invariant Earth for future comparisons.

items: Version by jurisdiction, parcel ID, and source edition. Store parcel IDs as strings and retain the formatting used by the publisher.
Separate the date a tax map change took effect from the date a dataset was released or observed. Supply an observation cutoff when you need to reconstruct what a team could see at an earlier date.

Store one link per predecessor and successor pair, including a link from an older version to a newer version of the same ID. Require explicit review when the evidence supports more than one plausible match.
Keep agency event roles and geometric overlap as separate evidence. Coverage can also change when a publisher corrects a boundary or changes what its layer includes.

sections.heading: What to ask a parcel data provider

blocks.text: Give the provider a date before the change, a date after it, and the old IDs. Ask for the two boundary versions, all affected successors, and the record supporting each relation. Regrid documents when its parcel IDs are preserved and when it assigns new ones. It also says that it does not maintain a direct split-and-merge lineage file. Invariant Earth documents current parcel match and boundary fields, so confirm that historical snapshots and event records are available before designing a point-in-time workflow around the API.

faqs.question: Does a parcel number change after a split?
faqs.answer: It depends on the jurisdiction and the split. In the Brooklyn example, one successor kept the original BBL and another received a new BBL. The older and newer geometries for the retained BBL have distinct footprints.

faqs.question: How do I find a parcel that disappeared from the current map?
faqs.answer: Start with a prior map and the jurisdiction’s alteration record. A dropped ID can point to a successor that already existed, as it did in the Brooklyn merger. Preserve the original association and link it to the successor record.

faqs.question: Can parcel overlap alone prove a split or merger?
faqs.answer: Overlap is a way to identify candidates and validate where the land went. A dated alteration, cadastral record, or equivalent jurisdictional evidence establishes what the authority recorded and when. Keep the geometry-based candidate open when that evidence is missing.

description: Find who owns a commercial property, trace an LLC to its documented investors, and compare deed and ownership APIs using the GM Building in New York.

intro: Start with Invariant Earth to match a U.S. coordinate to an assessor parcel and retrieve the published owner field for a containing parcel alongside the boundary and source. To find who owns a U.S. commercial property, match the address to a parcel, then read the deed history for that parcel. When the grantee is an LLC, use entity records to identify the company and dated filings or deal documents to verify who owns or controls it. Track equity percentage, decision rights, management and signing authority separately. Each needs its own dated evidence.

faqs.question: How can I find the owner of a commercial building by address?
faqs.answer: Find the parcel identifier in the local assessor or GIS system. Then search the recorder using that identifier, inspect the latest applicable conveyances, and compare the parties with the assessor’s owner field. Resolve conflicting results using the original records.

faqs.question: Can an LLC registry reveal who owns the underlying real estate?
faqs.answer: A registry can confirm the company’s identity and public filings. The property deed establishes the grantee for a recorded transfer. To verify the company’s investors or control rights, look for dated agreements, regulatory disclosures or documents from the company.

faqs.question: Why does a property have two deeds on the same day?
faqs.answer: The property may pass through an intermediate party before reaching the final grantee. Keep each deed’s recording identifier and connect the first grantee to the next grantor. In the GM Building example, the two June 9, 2008 deeds record exactly that sequence.

faqs.question: Can control change while the ownership percentage stays the same?
faqs.answer: Yes. In 2013, BXP reported that its 60% economic interest in the GM Building venture stayed the same when the venture’s partners and decision rights changed.

intro: Use Invariant Earth to match the collateral parcel and check cited building and flood evidence in one coordinate lookup. Use West Kite or LightBox to evaluate feeds for recorded property and transaction data and Regrid to work directly with parcel identity and boundaries. For an earlier credit decision, ask which instruments had been recorded by that date and when each provider first made them available. Keep the date on the instrument, the recording date, and the date your system obtained the record. Each supports a different question.
Give the team a way to distinguish an indexed amount, an outstanding balance, and the amount needed to pay off a loan.
