title: Warehouse site selection for rail, trucks and trailer parking
description: Find a rail-served warehouse or transload terminal. Compare Kansas carrier and project records, then verify the siding, legal truck route and trailer parking before leasing.
coverAlt: Aerial map of 3801 and 3750 CenterPoint Way in Joliet, Illinois. The owner’s map pins are about a quarter mile apart. The listings report 133 and 256 trailer spaces respectively, with rail access marked No at both properties.
coverCaption: Two CenterPoint Way listings in Joliet. The map shows the owner’s location pins. Aerial imagery from USDA and USGS The National Map.
intro: To screen a warehouse for rail and truck access, start with the specific loading doors, yard, and gate you would lease. Find the railroad and route that can serve those doors, check a truck route from the interstate to the actual gate, and count the trailer spaces your operation can use at its busiest hour. Nearby tracks and a large parking count are useful leads. Verify each requirement at the property before using it to select a site.
takeaways: For direct rail delivery, get the track identifier, the carrier that will place cars, and written service terms for the particular building.
Keep railcar storage, loading positions and the largest train an operator can handle as separate numbers. Verify which tracks and services are available now.
Route the actual vehicle to the correct gate. Check clearance, posted limits, turns, and tolls along every segment.
Two Joliet properties about a quarter mile apart list 133 and 256 trailer spaces. The owner marks rail access as No at both, even though Union Pacific lists an intermodal terminal on the same road.

guideActions.label: Check rail and truck access for a warehouse

sections.heading: What data finds a warehouse with usable access?

rows: Direct rail siding
North American Rail Network lines and trackage rights, carrier service maps, and the site plan.
The carrier’s confirmation it can spot your railcars at the specific siding. Request track condition, usable length, car types, switching schedule, and who is responsible for repairs or construction.
Intermodal or transload access
Rail terminal directory and operating information from the carrier or transload operator.
The terminal or facility that accepts your freight, who handles the transfer or truck leg, what equipment they can accept, and the route between the facility and your gate.
Interstate truck access
State designated truck routes, local road and clearance records, and a routing API such as HERE configured for your truck dimensions and weights.
The route for the intended vehicle, including each jurisdiction, posted weight and clearance, allowed turns, toll, and any temporary restrictions. Confirm the route to the gate in use.
Trailer parking and gate access
Property listing, current site plan, lease plan, and the operator’s yard records.
Dedicated positions by type and size, peak parked trailers, docks and staging reserved for other uses, turning envelope, and gate throughput.

blocks.text: A rail spur is a track connection that can let the carrier deliver cars to a particular site. At an intermodal terminal, a container can move between rail and truck. At a transload facility, freight can be transferred between the railcar and the truck. Decide which operation your business needs, then verify the facility and route that can actually provide it.

sections.heading: Two properties on the same road in Joliet

blocks.text: Union Pacific lists its Global 4 Intermodal Terminal at 3000 CenterPoint Way in Joliet, Illinois. We checked two CenterPoint property listings on the same road. Their published map pins are about 399 meters apart in a straight line, about one quarter mile. We measured between the owner’s pins using the WGS84 ellipsoid. The result describes proximity, and the site gates and road route are separate checks.

rows: 3801 CenterPoint Way
No
3750 CenterPoint Way
No

blocks.text: For a tenant that needs railcars at the building, the terminal address offers evidence of intermodal infrastructure in the area. Ask the owner and carrier about direct service to the exact tract. For a tenant using containers by truck, check the route to the terminal and confirm operating and access terms. The parking count belongs to each listed property. Confirm which spaces the proposed lease actually includes.

sections.heading: How do you verify that a warehouse is rail-served?

blocks.text: Give the railroad the warehouse address, the lease plan, and the track where cars would be placed for unloading. Ask which carrier handles the final switch, how many cars it can deliver at once, and which days it serves the site. Have the owner identify the track it controls and any track inspection or repair required before service.

At Elion Logistics Park 55 in Wilmington, Illinois, BNSF describes direct rail access at the park level. The city’s February 2026 redevelopment plan, published in its May 5 council packet, identifies a spur serving two transload warehouses, one refrigerated and one frozen. The same plan discusses additional spurs as future work. For a different building in the park, ask which track reaches its unloading area and who can authorize use of that track.

Get the carrier’s service terms before setting a lease start date around rail delivery. Union Pacific requires an active track agreement for new industrial-track shipments, including a customer’s first shipment at a location that the railroad served before. Ask whose agreement covers your business, who maintains the track, and what must be completed before the first car arrives.

items.label: Trace a spur from crossing rights to the first delivered car

sections.heading: Where can you find rail-served industrial sites and transload terminals?

blocks.text: Start with the railroad’s site directory and a transload operator’s terminal list. BNSF and Norfolk Southern publish both types of listings. Match each lead to the parcel or building you would actually use. The Kansas records below show how to tell park service, terminal opening and a construction bid apart.

rows: Great Plains Industrial Park, Parsons
Watco lists active switching and transloading, Union Pacific connectivity and 400 terminal railcar spots.
The track and loading position assigned to your building, the number of cars the operator can place there, and the switching schedule.
Stafford County Transload Facility, St. John
A September 2026 congressional newsletter reports the ribbon cutting. Adams lists BNSF service and describes the unit-train loop as underway.
Which tracks and commodities the operator accepts today, and whether it can handle your proposed train or individual cars on your schedule.
Kansas Logistics Park, Newton
Newton’s Phase 1 rail-extension bid lists 6,520 track feet of new rail in one item. The bids were opened September 25, 2025.
The completion and railroad acceptance records for the phase that reaches your site, plus the confirmed first service date.

blocks.text: In Stafford County, the federal award lists $25 million for the transload and grain terminal project. The grant application describes room for 475 railcars of 62 feet each across the planned facility, including a 120-car unit-train loop and a separate 292-car manifest track capacity. A unit train moves one type of freight together. A manifest train can carry a mix of railcars and freight. Keep the proposed capacities tied to their tracks and ask which portions the operator can serve today.

To compare options, send each operator the same commodity, loaded car length and weight, origin and destination, typical shipment size and target start date. Ask how many cars it can place at once, what it charges for switching, unloading and storage, and who handles the truck leg. For a direct siding, also request the service agreement and maintenance responsibilities for the exact track.

blocks.label: Download the Kansas rail service, terminal and bid records

items.label: Screen marketed industrial sites by usable acreage and zoning

blocks.text: Use the Invariant Earth warehouse workflow to screen mapped rail and road access before asking the operator to confirm service for the property.

sections.heading: Check the truck route to the gate and price each crossing

blocks.text: Use the proposed gate as the endpoint. Start with a truck routing service that accepts the complete vehicle profile. Compare its result with state and local designations and the route conditions the carrier can confirm. Check ramps and turns, underpasses, posted limits, and the road between the interchange and yard. Record the equipment type, the date and the authority behind each restriction.

The Houbolt Road Extension provides a tolled connection between I-80 and CenterPoint Intermodal Center. Its schedule effective April 1, 2026 lists a Class 3 toll of $9.15 with a qualifying transponder and $14.65 without one. At 200 tollable Class 3 crossings, the illustrative totals are $1,830 and $2,930. Price the route using the operator’s vehicle class and payment method, and recheck the schedule before contracting for the truck moves.

sections.heading: Measure trailer parking at the busiest point in the shift

blocks.text: Start with the spaces reserved for your operation on the current lease plan. Check whether the longest trailers fit, whether access lanes stay clear, and how many spots are taken by staging, maintenance, or shared operations. Then track arrivals, departures, and trailer dwell by time of day. Use your highest simultaneous count of parked trailers to size the yard.

In an illustrative layout with 133 marked positions, reserving 12 for staging and taking six out of service leaves 115 for parked trailers. If 118 need to park at the same time, the layout is three short. The reservations and peak count are example assumptions. Bring a current yard plan and a peak operating schedule to the site visit so you can test your own numbers.

faqs.question: How do I find a warehouse with an active rail spur?
faqs.answer: Use property and rail maps to shortlist sites with a plausible track connection. Ask the serving railroad for confirmation that your cars can be spotted at that siding, along with track condition, usable length, switching frequency, and any work needed.

faqs.question: Does being near an intermodal terminal mean a warehouse is rail-served?
faqs.answer: An intermodal terminal supports moving containers between rail and trucks. Ask the carrier whether it can instead deliver a railcar directly to the property. In the Joliet example, both property listings mark rail access as No and the operator separately lists its intermodal terminal on the same road.

faqs.question: How many trailer spaces does a warehouse need?
faqs.answer: Calculate the highest number of trailers parked at one time. Count the spaces available under the lease, then account for shared, blocked or staging positions and check the geometry for your trailers. Use truck arrival and dwell data to test the peak.

faqs.question: Can I ship by rail without an on-site siding?
faqs.answer: A transload terminal can transfer freight between railcars and trucks. Confirm the serving railroad, commodity, equipment, shipment size, loading schedule and truck route to your property with the operator.

title: Business fiber availability by address: maps, APIs and quotes
description: Check reported business fiber by address. Compare Invariant Earth, Connectbase, FiberLocator, and the FCC, then test a vendor on two documented addresses.
coverAlt: Mapped address points and parcel boundaries for Main Library and the Asian Art Museum in San Francisco’s Civic Center.
coverCaption: The Main Library and Asian Art Museum address points from San Francisco’s Enterprise Addressing System.
intro: Start with the exact building and suite. Use the FCC or your state broadband map to see which providers report fiber at that location. For a property portfolio, use an address or parcel API to keep the site identity and source date with each result. Ask the carrier for a written quote for the exact service, install date, and build charges before you rely on it for a lease.
takeaways: Match the building and suite first. An area-level result gives you providers to investigate.
Keep business and consumer offers separate. Check technology, advertised download and upload, and the date of the records.
For a lease or build, get a written quote for the exact service address, installation timing, costs and performance terms.

guideActions.label: Check business fiber at an address

sections.heading: What can you check on the FCC National Broadband Map?

blocks.text: Search the exact address, select the location point, and open the Fixed Broadband results. Filter for business service and the technology you need, such as fiber to the premises. Record the data as-of date, provider, technology and the paired advertised download and upload values. An FCC gray location identifies a building likely to use specialized commercial service. Ask enterprise sales for a quote at that address.

For many addresses, the FCC publishes fixed availability downloads with location IDs and service attributes. Keep the provider record tied to its source location ID and vintage. For a bulk join to street addresses or location geometry, check your rights to the Broadband Serviceable Location Fabric and match the versions. The FCC map lets you check individual addresses without rebuilding the Fabric.

sections.heading: Two addresses on Larkin Street returned different wireline options

blocks.text: We joined the city address points for San Francisco’s Main Library and Asian Art Museum to the California Public Utilities Commission’s December 2024 broadband map layers. The points are on the same street. The provider layers returned different results, and the consumer speed layer reports a maximum for a census block.

columns: Business wireline rows intersecting the point
rows: 100 Larkin Street, Main Library
Xfinity cable at 1,200 Mbps down and 35 Mbps up. AT&T California ADSL at 10 Mbps down and 1 Mbps up.
1,200 Mbps maximum advertised downstream in census block 060750124051006.
200 Larkin Street, Asian Art Museum
AT&T California ADSL at 10 Mbps down and 1 Mbps up. The query returned no Xfinity business row.
The consumer downstream layer returned no intersecting row at this point.

blocks.text: Neither point returned a business fiber row under code 50 in this CPUC layer. Both returned business fixed wireless and satellite rows. This was an intersection with provider polygons from a dated map. A carrier can quote a dedicated circuit at a building that lacks a matching mass-market record. A consumer block maximum alone gives neither the business upload speed nor the service terms.
Run the business broadband lookup to repeat the California provider-layer query at both addresses. The example keeps each provider’s technology, download speed and upload speed together.

blocks.label: Download both address points and the broadband query results

sections.heading: How to use broadband data in a site-selection API

blocks.text: Use a verified address or parcel as the starting point. Keep the reported service area, location, technology and date with each result. Invariant Earth lists fiber_broadband_available and fiber_provider_count for the cell containing the lookup point. These fields summarize reported mass-market fiber in a hexagonal area and require an operator key. Use the FCC or state map and ask providers for address-level confirmation.

sections.heading: Which business fiber availability API should you trial?

blocks.text: Start with Invariant Earth when you need to join connectivity indicators to site, parcel and infrastructure records. Use the FCC or a state map for reported availability, and evaluate a telecom API when you need carriers, building connection status or a dedicated service quote. The comparisons below come from published documentation. Run the same addresses through a trial account before buying.

rows: Invariant Earth
Parcel and location screening with operator-access fiber availability and provider-count indicators for the surrounding cell.
Ask for site identity, cell-level scope and data date. Keep the carrier quote attached to the same building and suite as a separate record.
Connectbase
Address validation and provider lookup across locations. Connection statuses distinguish on-net, near-net and limited-access buildings.
Choose a multi-tenant property. Check that the response matches the suite or building and identifies how it determined the connection status.
FiberLocator
Carrier-supplied lit-building records and fiber maps available through a subscription API.
Check the matched building, contributing carrier and vintage. Ask which services can be ordered at the suite and what missing coverage means.
FCC National Broadband Map
Provider-reported fixed broadband availability by location, technology and advertised speed.
Use the business filter and preserve the data date. Check whether the map treats the building as a mass-market serviceable location.
California Public Utilities Commission
Dated provider polygons and consumer speed summaries for California.
Use the business rows and save both advertised speeds for each technology. A result on a consumer census block gives less specific evidence.

blocks.text: On the December 2024 California map, the 1,200 Mbps cable record at 100 Larkin Street pairs that download rate with 35 Mbps up. Neither address returned a business wireline row meeting an illustrative 100 Mbps upload requirement. Each point did intersect business fixed wireless rows above that threshold. Use the worksheet to test whether a provider keeps the speed pair and technology together and can supply a written quote for the requested service.

blocks.label: Download the business fiber API trial scorecard

sections.heading: What to get from the carrier before signing a lease

blocks.text: Request a serviceability quote for the street address, suite and network room. Confirm the access technology, download and upload rates, shared or dedicated service, the construction charge and the earliest committed install date. For dedicated service, ask for the committed rate and the service-level agreement. Put the provider’s response and any building-access requirements on the opening schedule.

When a site needs two independent circuits, ask each provider for the physical route, entrance and upstream handoff. Compare any shared conduit and the traffic the surviving path can carry. Two carriers can resell service over the same local network.

items.label: Check the operator-only point fiber indicator
Check how the FCC fiber provider count is defined
Verify physical fiber route diversity

faqs.question: Does a 1 Gbps result prove fiber is available?
faqs.answer: Check the transmission technology. Cable and fixed wireless can both report gigabit speeds. The FCC uses technology code 50 for fiber to the premises. Check both advertised speeds and ask the provider what reaches the exact suite.

faqs.question: Why is business fiber missing from a broadband map?
faqs.answer: The location may have only other technologies reported or use specialized commercial service that the mass-market map does not cover. Check the point, date and filters, then ask carriers for written serviceability at the address.

faqs.question: How do I challenge an incorrect FCC availability result?
faqs.answer: Use the availability challenge on the selected FCC location. Keep a quote, denial or record of the provider conversation. FCC guidance describes when ordinary installation delays or charges qualify as an availability issue.

faqs.question: What do on-net and near-net mean for business fiber?
faqs.answer: On-net generally indicates that a carrier has a network presence at the building. Near-net indicates a nearby network that may be extended to the site. Check the vendor’s status definition, then ask the carrier for access to the exact suite, any construction work, and an install date.

title: How to verify data center fiber route diversity
description: Verify data center fiber service by address. Check carrier routes, building entrances, install dates, cloud handoffs and capacity after one circuit fails.
coverAlt: Diagram of two Equinix buildings on Secaucus Road. AWS lists NY5 as a Direct Connect location and shows it is also accessible from NY4 at a different street address.
coverCaption: Equinix lists NY4 and NY5 at different addresses. AWS lists NY4 as an access option for the NY5 Direct Connect location. The diagram shows the directory relationship.
intro: To verify fiber route diversity at a data center, identify the exact endpoints of both circuits and ask the providers for evidence of their physical paths. Check the building entrances, internal paths, outside conduits and crossings, and where each circuit hands off to the next network. A directory can tell you which carriers or cloud services to investigate. For a lease or service commitment, document what the surviving circuit can carry when one route or facility fails.
takeaways: Look up the exact building and service address. Record the carrier, underlying operator, connection endpoint, and whether the proposed service has been ordered or built.
At Secaucus, Equinix lists two different building addresses, while AWS lists one Direct Connect location for the access relationship shown in this example.
Check cloud peering and physical routes separately. Cloud edge domains, buildings and circuit orders describe different parts of the connection.
Check both route separation and surviving throughput. Two 10 Gbps circuits leave 10 Gbps of nominal capacity after a single circuit loss.

sections.heading: What can you verify from a data center address?

rows: Who reports service nearby?
FCC National Broadband Map for reported fixed availability and operator service maps or quotes.
Exact building, provider, technology, and date. Ask the carrier to qualify the specific service and endpoint.
Which network or cloud handoffs are offered?
Facility operator pages, its connectivity contacts, and the cloud provider’s location directory.
Building ID, named handoff location, connection product, underlying carrier where known, and the organization providing the interconnect.
What is the physical route for each circuit?
A carrier route exhibit or a written route comparison for the proposed or installed circuits, including both endpoints.
Path and entrance identifiers, common segments, route version, associated circuit order, and the comparison scope.
What survives a loss or scheduled maintenance?
Service terms, circuit design, equipment and port assignments, and a coordinated acceptance test.
Agreed failures to test, surviving throughput and failover behavior, observation date, exceptions, and the owner of any remediation.

blocks.text: A carrier name by itself leaves several questions open. Ask who owns and operates the access segment and whether either provider leases facilities from the same third party. In a multi-building campus, confirm the service address, point of entry, handoff room and equipment for the specific circuit you intend to buy.

sections.heading: Compare fiber maps and route APIs for data center site selection

blocks.text: Start with the parcel and building you intend to use. Invariant Earth helps keep those records alongside terrain, hazards and infrastructure evidence. A network map can help find candidate carriers and handoffs. Get the circuit-specific route and building evidence from the providers before accepting a diversity commitment.

rows: Connectbase Network Path
Path lookup between two supplied endpoints, with segment identifiers and a comparison for two returned segments.
What endpoints and operators are in scope? Is the route comparison for modeled candidates or for the actual services being quoted?
FiberLocator
Street-level fiber maps and lit-building records from participating carriers.
Can you identify the carrier and exact building, and obtain a separate route confirmation for the circuit order?
Transect
A fiber layer with parcel proximity filters and operator, service type and status attributes where available.
Is the mapped segment operational, and do you know who can quote a connection to the parcel?
LandGate
Dark fiber route context for screening potential data center sites.
Which mapped routes are near the parcel, and what evidence can you get from the carrier about orderable service and construction?

items.label: Run the business fiber availability API trial

sections.heading: Two Secaucus buildings, one listed AWS location

blocks.text: We checked Equinix’s facility pages and the AWS Direct Connect location directory on November 22, 2026. Equinix lists NY4 and NY5 at different street addresses. In the Direct Connect table, AWS lists Equinix NY5 as the location and shows that it is also accessible from NY4. AWS separately lists a CoreSite NY1 location in New York City.

rows: Equinix NY4
755 Secaucus Road, Secaucus, NJ
Access option for the Equinix NY5 location.
Equinix NY5
800 Secaucus Road, Secaucus, NJ
Named Equinix NY5 location in Secaucus.
CoreSite NY1
32 Avenue of the Americas, New York, NY
Separately listed CoreSite NY1 location.

blocks.text: The count depends on what you’re counting. For NY4 and NY5, the public records establish two buildings and one named AWS location in this comparison. If your design requires two AWS locations, use the cloud provider’s location records to choose candidates, then verify the transport from your site to each handoff. The next evidence you need is the route comparison for the two circuits you plan to order.

blocks.label: Download the facility cross-reference and failover calculation

sections.heading: Compare AWS, Azure and Google Cloud interconnect redundancy

blocks.text: A cloud peering location is where a connection meets the cloud provider’s network. Count the location or maintenance domain in the provider’s own terms. Then identify the parts of the circuit on the customer and carrier side that each availability commitment covers.

rows: AWS Direct Connect

The Maximum Resiliency design uses separate devices across more than one Direct Connect location. Two devices at one location protect against device failure. The applicable SLA depends on the deployment and its eligibility.
Request the ordered location, connection ID, port assignment and resiliency model. For a hosted service, request the partner’s contract.
Azure ExpressRoute

A standard circuit has a primary and secondary link. ExpressRoute Metro connects to two peering locations in a supported city. Microsoft’s guidance for geographic disaster recovery covers circuits in different peering locations.
Request the circuit and peering location mapping for each link. Match the facility and access path for each handoff.
Google Cloud Dedicated Interconnect

Google documents both multi-region and qualified single-region configurations for 99.99% availability. The designs require at least four connections plus the specified placement, VLAN attachments and routing configuration.
Request the location codes and edge availability domains, the facility for each connection, the attachment design, and the terms that cover the order.

blocks.text: Use the directory checks as controls. In Dallas, Google’s dfw-zone1-4 and dfw-zone2-4 share the Equinix DA1 facility label and have separate edge availability domains. In its New York Metro listing, Microsoft names Equinix NY5 and 165 Halsey Street as the peering pair. In the Secaucus AWS example above, the NY4 and NY5 building records point to one named AWS location. Confirm which entries apply to your circuit before comparing the carrier paths.

blocks.label: Download the AWS, Azure and Google Cloud directory checks

sections.heading: How to verify two independent fiber paths

blocks.text: Draw the comparison from your equipment to the two remote handoffs. Check the building entrances, risers, cross-connect rooms, conduit, and any crossings where the routes could come back together. Include shared access equipment and maintenance domains where those risks matter to your design. Network engineers sometimes call links that share a physical failure risk a shared-risk link group.

items: Ask both providers for current route exhibits or a written comparison that names the circuit orders, endpoints, and parts of the path covered. Use the providers’ agreed process for reviewing sensitive drawings.
Ask for exceptions in writing. A shared conduit, building entrance, or wholesale local loop may affect both circuits. Identify what fails together and whether the design accepts that risk.
Compare the installed route and endpoint records at acceptance, then track changes to the route or the facility. Confirm the contracted installation scope and any notification terms for rerouting.

blocks.text: The AWS Direct Connect resiliency models also distinguish device failures from complete location failures. Pick the level of resilience your workload requires, including any separate facility or device requirements, and verify the last-mile design that connects your equipment to those AWS locations.

sections.heading: Does fiber near the property mean a carrier can deliver service?

blocks.text: Ask the carrier for a current serviceability quote for the exact parcel and building. The quote should name the building entrance and remote handoff, identify any new construction, and give a delivery date with its dependencies. For a greenfield site, give both carriers the same concept plan and opening date so they price the same job.

Gateway in Forney, Texas, shows how far a public site package can take that check. The Forney Economic Development Corporation places the target area about 30 fiber-route miles from downtown Dallas and identifies several nearby providers. Its 2018 engineering study shows an example duct layout linking three proposed interconnection vaults on part of the development. The published drawing helps a buyer ask where an entrance could go. The route mileage describes distance, and the design describes proposed civil works. The public records reviewed here provide no carrier order, installed route record or service date for a specific building.

rows: Shortlist
Exact parcel and building, intended entrances, provider contact and proposed handoffs.
Decide which candidate warrants a carrier field survey.
Before signing
A quote for each circuit. Ask who builds the extension, which permits or easements are open, when service can start, and when the quote expires.
Check whether fiber can meet your opening date and who pays for the build.
Before accepting service
Current carrier records for the installed circuit pair, acceptance results and agreed capacity after a circuit loss.
Verify service against the order and the workload’s failover requirement.

blocks.label: Download the carrier serviceability request worksheet

sections.heading: What to request before accepting a diversity claim

rows: Customer access
A dated statement for the ordered circuit pair naming both endpoints, the underlying operators and any shared segments or equipment.
Carrier or last-mile operator
Building entry
Written confirmation of independent entrances, internal pathways and handoff rooms, scoped to the suite or server hall.
Facility operator
Cloud edge
Cloud location and port assignments, cross-connect orders, applicable resiliency model and service-level terms.
Cloud provider and connectivity partner
Failover
An authorized acceptance-test record with direction, surviving path, traffic demand, measured throughput, packet loss and recovery time.
Customer and providers

blocks.text: Give the buyer or reviewer the same acceptance limits for traffic in both directions. In an authorized test, the AWS toolkit can take a selected BGP session out of service so the operator can observe rerouting. Treat the test as evidence of the recorded routing event. Keep the written route comparison and any exclusions with it.

sections.heading: Can the surviving circuit carry the workload?

blocks.text: Suppose two nominal 10 Gbps circuits must carry a 15 Gbps peak workload after either one fails. With one down, 10 Gbps of nominal capacity remains and the shortfall is 5 Gbps. This example uses link rates before protocol overhead. Use measured usable capacity and your own traffic profile for procurement.

Agree on an acceptance test with the providers. Exercise each failure the contract and design are meant to cover in a coordinated window, then record which path carried traffic, the transition time, and delivered throughput at the expected load. Keep the test evidence and the route evidence together so a reviewer can see both the physical design and what happened during failover.

faqs.question: Can I look up exact fiber routes by address?
faqs.answer: An address lookup can identify reported providers, facilities, and cloud access locations. Ask the proposed providers for a route comparison tied to your circuit orders and endpoints. Verify building entry and shared physical segments as part of that review.

faqs.question: Do two carriers guarantee two physical fiber paths?
faqs.answer: Check the actual routes and facility handoffs for both carriers. Different service providers can share the same underlying conduit, local access facilities, or building entrances. Ask each provider which parts of the path its diversity commitment covers.

faqs.question: Do two Google Cloud Interconnect locations guarantee diverse fiber?
faqs.answer: Compare the edge availability domain in each location code. Google lists dfw-zone1-4 and dfw-zone2-4 at Equinix DA1, so their cloud maintenance domains differ while the catalog facility is the same. Request proof of the customer’s physical paths and compare the ordered design with the SLA.

faqs.question: Do two 10 Gbps circuits support 15 Gbps after one fails?
faqs.answer: On nominal rates, one surviving 10 Gbps circuit leaves a 5 Gbps shortfall against a 15 Gbps requirement. Check measured throughput and failover behavior under the workload you plan to carry.

title: How to Check Environmental Restrictions by Address in NYC
description: Look up NYC E-designations and environmental easements by address. Trace the tax lot and check what the zoning, title and cleanup records actually cover.
coverAlt: 2024 aerial photo of Brooklyn showing the boundary of block 980, lot 77 at 380 Fourth Avenue.
coverCaption: 380 Fourth Avenue, Brooklyn. Invariant annotated the Digital Tax Map parcel on 2024 imagery © City of New York, CC BY 4.0.
intro: To check environmental restrictions on a New York City property, start with its borough, block and lot. Search the city’s zoning index for an E-designation or environmental restrictive declaration. Then read the underlying requirements, the project approvals and any recorded easement. At 380 Fourth Avenue in Brooklyn, the city dates its air and noise rows to January 22, 2026. The hazardous-materials row has a blank date, while the state records a 2024 cleanup certificate and a separate recorded easement.
takeaways: Match the address to the current tax lot and trace older lot numbers before searching the zoning index and recorder.
Search predecessor lots as well as current condo unit lots. At 91 Gerry Street, the state easement is indexed to the old parent lot.
Read the air, noise and hazardous-materials entries separately. Record the scope of each notice.
Check the recorded instrument and site management plan before treating a cleanup milestone as clearance for the work you plan.

sections.heading: Start with the tax lot and its earlier numbers

blocks.text: The state calls this site 380 4th Avenue. PLUTO 26v3 gives 376 4 AVENUE, and the city cleanup-site record uses 374 4th Avenue. The PLUTO row and the recorder identify Brooklyn block 980, lot 77, or BBL 3009800077. Use that identifier to reconcile the city and state records.

Search the current and predecessor lots. The Office of Environmental Remediation (OER) warns that the city lookup may miss lots after a split, merger or condo conversion. Use the Digital Tax Map and lot history to check which original land your transaction covers. Section 11-15 describes how environmental conditions apply when affected lots change.

blocks.label: Parcel checks

items.label: Trace a split or merger through dated tax maps
Check parcel fields and API coverage

sections.heading: What the records show at 380 Fourth Avenue

blocks.text: The same lot has a city zoning designation, a state cleanup project and a recorded environmental easement. Keep the source and date for each. They answer different questions about the property.

rows: November 23, 2021
NYC E-601
The city put air, hazardous-materials and noise requirements on lot 77 under the Gowanus rezoning.
June 4, 2024
Environmental easement recorded
CRFN 2024000141888 covers the entire lot. It sets allowable uses and requires compliance with the site management plan.
December 29, 2024
State certificate milestone
DEC’s project data records this date for the Certificate of Completion. The certificate register lists restricted residential as the highest allowable future use.
January 22, 2026
Air and noise dates in the city index
The index shows this lot remediation date for those two categories. The hazardous-materials row lists lot 77 with a blank date.
November 24, 2026 lookup
City cleanup-site record
OER’s separate record says Completed (C) and Site Management. Its program field includes state brownfield cleanup and city E/RD review.

blocks.text: The recorded state easement lists restricted residential, commercial and industrial uses and requires adherence to the site management plan. The plan addresses engineering controls, monitoring and certifications. For a renovation involving excavation or changes to those controls, ask for the plan and latest compliance records before setting the work budget.

blocks.label: Download the parcel, zoning, recorder and cleanup evidence

sections.heading: Find the environmental easement after a lot merger or condo conversion

blocks.text: A mortgage on condo lot 2701 at 91 Gerry Street in Brooklyn was recorded in February 2026. The earlier environmental easement is indexed to lot 40 on the same block. To find it from the unit lot, follow the recorded condominium declaration back to the parent lot and check the easement’s legal description.

rows: November 24, 2021 tax map merger
Brooklyn block 2266, lots 40 and 41 → lot 40
The former 89–91 Gerry Street addresses became one tax lot at 91 Gerry Street. DEC reflected the merger in the cleanup agreement in October 2024.
March 11, 2025 recorded easement
The legal description covers about 5,000 square feet. The recorder indexes the easement against the parent lot.
May 13, 2025 condo declaration
The declaration index connects the old lot to six unit lots. The PLUTO 26v3 snapshot uses billing lot 7517 for 91 Gerry Street.
February 5, 2026 recorded mortgage
An exact match on this unit lot misses the easement. The declaration supplies the link to the parent lot.

blocks.text: The DEC register summarizes the site’s highest future use as “Unrestricted.” The signed May 22, 2025 certificate specifies Conditional Track 1 and gives five years to meet soil vapor intrusion cleanup goals. The certificate cites the recorded easement. That instrument lists restricted residential, commercial and industrial uses and sets conditions for soil disturbance, groundwater use and site management. For an acquisition or refinance, compare the proposed work with the current instrument and plan, and ask for later amendments, releases and monitoring records.

Keep 93 Gerry Street separate. It is lot 39 and DEC site C224326, with its own December 21, 2023 certificate milestone. The neighboring addresses and related project names make an address-only match easy to misread.

blocks.label: Download the Gerry Street lot history and environmental instrument references

sections.heading: Check permits and title before you close

blocks.text: For an E-designation, use Appendix C Table 1 to find the designation number, category and listed date. Open the environmental review and ask OER for the notice that covers your work. Section 11-15 requires an OER notice before covered building permits or certificates of occupancy can issue. Triggers include certain work that disturbs soil for hazardous materials, alters ventilation or exhaust for air quality, or replaces windows or exterior walls for noise.

For a city environmental restrictive declaration, use Appendix C Table 2 to find the recording reference and pull the instrument from the recorder. Also search the title records for state environmental easements, recorded site management declarations, changes and releases. At 380 Fourth Avenue, the state easement is an ACRIS instrument with its own document ID and legal description.

For an acquisition or loan, compare the planned use and construction scope with the recorded instrument. Ask who is responsible for inspections, reporting and maintenance after transfer. Keep any missing notices or amendments open in the credit file. This sample identifies the recorded documents and agency entries. It does not establish the present title position or approval for a new project.

faqs.question: Does an E-designation mean a property is contaminated?
faqs.answer: An E-designation records a city environmental requirement that can concern hazardous materials, air quality or noise. Match the lot and read the category and underlying records to understand what investigation or mitigation was required.

faqs.question: Does a New York brownfield cleanup certificate remove an environmental easement?
faqs.answer: Check the recorded easement and any later release or amendment. At 380 Fourth Avenue the state register lists a 2024 certificate, while the original easement documents allowed uses and site management obligations for the property.

faqs.question: What does a blank lot remediation date mean in Appendix C?
faqs.answer: It means the consulted row shows no date. Check the underlying notice, the original and successor lots, and the scope of the work before drawing a conclusion about the property.

title: How to Find Industrial Land for Sale by Acreage and Zoning
description: Find industrial land in public site inventories. Compare sale status, contiguous acreage and zoning, then replay a 50-acre search of Virginia listings.
coverAlt: In a Virginia sale inventory, 341 records showed at least 50 total acres, 254 also showed at least 50 contiguous acres, and 252 also showed at least 50 acres suitable for construction.
coverCaption: Successive filters applied to the Virginia Economic Development Partnership’s public site layer on November 24, 2026.
intro: Start with a state or local economic development inventory for marketed industrial land. Filter for the largest connected area your project needs, then check the acreage reported suitable for construction and the zoning for your specific use. In Virginia, 341 sale records listed at least 50 total acres. Of those, 252 also met both reported acreage checks. Use the result to decide which sites are worth a survey, a zoning call, and a utility inquiry.
takeaways: Define the space your layout needs in one connected block. Include truck courts, setbacks, stormwater and utility equipment.
Keep the acreage the seller can convey, the reported contiguous area and the area suitable for construction on separate lines.
Before pricing land, confirm the offered parcel IDs, permitted use, site access, utility capacity and the dates the providers can support.

guideActions.label: Find parcels in your search area

sections.heading: Where to find industrial land for sale

blocks.text: Start with the state’s site and building directory, then check the local economic development office and commercial land listings. State directories give you a consistent place to start. Local teams can often identify which pad or parcels are still offered and supply a site plan, study, or survey. Save the listing ID and the date you checked it, so you can request the same property later.

For a larger search area, draw the corridors or service areas that meet your freight and site requirements, then look for parcels inside them. Use parcel records to identify candidate tracts and ask owners or their representatives about interest. Record those leads as owner inquiries until someone authorized confirms that they would sell or lease.

sections.heading: Run a 50-acre industrial land search

blocks.text: Suppose the project needs one continuous 50-acre layout. We queried Virginia’s public Available Sites layer on November 24, 2026. Each row below adds a check to the one above it. Treat the numbers as counts of directory records at the time of the query.

rows: Marked for sale
At least 50 total acres

Also at least 50 acres suitable for construction

blocks.text: The last two acreage checks removed 89 records, about 26% of the results returned by total acreage alone. The remaining 252 are prospects for a closer look. Request the buildable-area map before assuming that the land suitable for construction is one connected block on the tract you can buy.

Carry it into layout review. Confirm the 53-acre construction area within the specific tract on offer.

Carry the acreage forward and check the land use separately. The record lists A-1. Ask the locality where the proposed operation can be permitted.

blocks.text: Send the planner your parcel IDs, site plan and proposed operation, including truck activity, outdoor storage and utility equipment. Ask which zoning and overlays apply to the building pad and access route, and which approvals you need before work can start.

Find recorded access and utility easements for the tract
Check API fields for zoning, terrain and water

sections.heading: What to ask for before making an offer

blocks.text: Ask for a dated exhibit showing the parcels, access routes, easements and land reserved for later phases. Confirm who can sign for the tract and whether any pad has already been sold or reserved. In North Carolina, for example, the Certified Sites guidelines require documented price and availability assurance for at least two years. Ask for the current assurance and which part of the site it covers.

Ask the water, sewer and power providers to confirm the required capacity, connection point and service date. Use the same drawing and schedule for every provider. The footprint that survives those calls is the one to use in a price comparison.

items.label: Use the site due diligence worksheet
Check what the site certification covers
Test a plant layout against the acreage and utilities
Check a siding or transload terminal before shortlisting rail-served land
Check whether an industrial parcel can be used as a truck or trailer yard

faqs.question: Where can I search for industrial land for sale?
faqs.answer: Start with a state economic development site directory, then check the local development agency and broker listings. Confirm the current offering, seller, parcel IDs and dates directly before comparing prices.

faqs.question: How do I find 50 buildable acres?
faqs.answer: Filter for at least 50 total acres, 50 contiguous acres and 50 acres reported suitable for construction where those fields are available. Ask for a survey and a concept plan showing the connected area that fits your layout, including access, setbacks and utilities.

faqs.question: Does industrial zoning let me build a warehouse or factory?
faqs.answer: Ask the local planning authority how its use table classifies your specific operation and whether overlays or conditions apply. Bring your site plan and separate the building, yard, truck route and any outside materials storage.

title: Property Ownership Change Alerts by Address
description: Set up deed recording alerts, track changes across a property portfolio, and see how NYC recorder data separates a deed from same-day financing documents.
coverAlt: Four ACRIS filings recorded October 5 at 600 Third Avenue. The deed lists $245 million and the mortgage and consolidation lists $185 million. The other filings are a mortgage assignment and sundry agreement.
coverCaption: Selected October 5, 2026 records for Manhattan tax lot 1008950045. Source: NYC Department of Finance, ACRIS.
intro: For a single property, look for a recording notice from the local recorder. For a portfolio, match each address to the correct parcel, then watch for new documents and classify them by instrument type. At one Manhattan office tower, four instruments were recorded on the same day. The deed was one of them. The same watchlist logic can keep financing notices and corrections from looking like extra sales.
takeaways: Confirm the recorder’s parcel identifier and the types of records its notification program covers.
Keep the document date, recording date and first date you saw the record in separate fields.
Join a deed to every affected parcel, then use the recorder’s document ID to count the deed once.

guideActions.label: Match a deed to a property

sections.heading: How do I get an alert when a deed is recorded?

blocks.text: Check the county or city recorder’s official alert program. In New York City, eligible registrants include owners, managing agents, attorneys for owners, and lienors. Register separately for each property by address or by borough, block and lot. The city says it usually issues a notice for covered recordings the next day. Read the instrument listed in the notice to see what was filed.

Programs vary. Los Angeles County mails copies of certain recorded documents for homes and offers opt-in email notices. Confirm which properties, people and instruments apply in your jurisdiction. For Staten Island documents, use the Richmond County Clerk to retrieve the instrument.

sections.heading: One office parcel, four instruments on the same day

blocks.text: The ACRIS Legals records link four selected October 5, 2026 recordings to Manhattan tax lot 1008950045 at 600 Third Avenue. The source uses both “3 Avenue” and “Third Avenue” for the same lot. Join on document ID and tax lot so a difference in spelling does not create a second property.

rows: Deed
Track as a recorded conveyance. The index shows a $245 million document amount and five parties coded as grantees.
Mortgage and consolidation
Track as financing. The index shows a $185 million amount under the mortgage and consolidation code.
Mortgage assignment
Track a change in the mortgage holder’s recorded interest. Check the instrument and its references.
Sundry agreement
Route it for review based on its terms and how it relates to the property.

blocks.text: In Brooklyn, deed 2026000283560 links 467 and 441 Prospect Avenue to two distinct tax lots. Its Master record lists Manhattan as the recording borough. For a parcel watch, use the borough from the Legals record. For a portfolio that watches both lots, retain both links to the deed and count the deed once.

blocks.label: Download the five document records, parcel links and replay results

sections.heading: Which date explains when the change happened?

blocks.text: The 600 Third Avenue deed has a September 18 document date and an October 5 recording date, 17 days apart. In the rows we retrieved on November 24, the extract was good through October 31. The public Master table listed a monthly update frequency and a November 10 row update. Measure when your own system first sees each document rather than treating the table update or extract date as an alert timestamp.

items: Document date. Keep the date shown on the instrument. Check the instrument for an effective date when the transaction terms depend on it.
Recording date. Use the recorder’s legal recording date for the recording sequence. Match follow-on documents to the original document ID where the recorder supplies a reference.
First seen. Save your retrieval timestamp and the source batch. Check overlapping windows for late arrivals and store corrections as new versions of the same source record.

blocks.text: When monitoring a watchlist, use the recorder’s document ID within its jurisdiction as the recording key. Keep parcel links and party roles as separate records. Compare the normalized fields you care about across snapshots and keep the original source values available for review. Use the instrument and title records to confirm what changed.

Track permit changes on the same property

sections.heading: Which API should I use to monitor a portfolio?

blocks.text: Use Invariant Earth to match an address to its parcel and get the boundary and assessor record for the watchlist. Use recorder documents or a documented recording feed for new instruments. For ownership snapshots, keep the assessor’s owner name and the deed’s grantee in separate fields.

Require a stable parcel match, an explicit instrument type, separate dates and a link or identifier you can take back to the recorder. For an LLC membership or control change, check the dated entity or deal filings for the specific interest involved.

faqs.question: Can I get a notification when a deed is recorded against my address?
faqs.answer: Check the local recorder’s program and confirm the exact property ID. In New York City, eligible owners, agents and lienors can register separately for each property. The city usually issues covered recording notices the following day.

faqs.question: Which API field tells me when a deed was recorded?
faqs.answer: In NYC ACRIS Master, recorded_datetime is the legal recording date. Save it alongside document_date, good_through_date and your own first-seen timestamp so you can tell between an older document and a newly received row.

faqs.question: How should I monitor a deed that covers several parcels?
faqs.answer: Store one document keyed by recorder and document ID. Link it to every parcel in the legal index, then surface the matching parcel links for each portfolio. Count the instrument once, even when both lots are on your watchlist.

title: How to Find a Certificate of Occupancy by Address in NYC
description: Find a NYC certificate of occupancy in DOB NOW or BIS. Use the building ID, check the floor use and expiration, and replay two Manhattan address lookups.
coverAlt: 270 Park Avenue has legacy building ID 1035421 and newer building ID 1091010 on the same NYC tax lot.
coverCaption: Selected DOB index results for 270 Park Avenue. Both building IDs appear on Manhattan tax lot 1012830021.
intro: Start with the address in the New York City Department of Buildings records. Search BIS for certificate requests filed before March 1, 2021, and DOB NOW for requests filed on or after that date. Open the issued certificate and check that its building, floors and permitted use match the space you are reviewing. At 270 Park Avenue, the same address and tax lot appear under two different building IDs. An address match alone can send you to the wrong certificate history.
takeaways: Record the building identification number (BIN) and the unit or floor. Keep the tax lot as a separate identifier.
Save the actual issued certificate and any attached floor use records. Read the listed expiration and conditions when the certificate is temporary.
For a loan, policy or lease, confirm the authorized use and applicable certificate on the date you are relying on it.

guideActions.label: Match the address to a building

sections.heading: Where to look up a NYC certificate of occupancy

blocks.text: Use the Department of Buildings lookup instructions to reach the city’s two property profiles. The March 2021 cutoff refers to when the certificate request was filed. For an older building, or when you know the address but have no filing date, check both systems.

rows: Before March 1, 2021
Buildings Information System (BIS). Search by address, open the property profile and select View Certificates of Occupancy.
Open the matching certificate PDF and save the pages that cover the space.
March 1, 2021 or later
DOB NOW Public Portal. Search by address or BIN, open the property profile and select Certificate of Occupancy.
Review Certificate of Occupancy Details and Floor Use Records, then use Print to save a copy.

blocks.text: A certificate describes the legal use or permitted type of occupancy recorded by DOB. A fire inspection, a construction permit and a property listing answer different questions. Before a tenant build-out, compare the proposed use with the certificate’s use for the actual floor or space.

items.label: What a certificate of occupancy covers

sections.heading: Why the building ID matters more than the street address

blocks.text: At 270 Park Avenue, both indexes use Manhattan tax lot 1012830021. The latest legacy record in our sample, dated August 20, 2015, is for BIN 1035421. The new-building job in DOB NOW has BIN 1091010. It starts with a July 1, 2025 issuance. Use the address and lot to find candidates, then keep the two building histories separate.

The split can also occur within one building history. At 350 Fifth Avenue, the Empire State Building, BIN 1015862 and alteration job 120581502 appear in both indexes. BIS records a temporary issuance for that job on February 5, 2021. DOB NOW records an initial issuance for the same job on July 13, 2021. Keep both rows when reconstructing the filing history.

blocks.text: The DOB NOW download gives an issuance status, a filing label and a date. Its published columns do not include the expiration date or the floor use records. The September Park Avenue row tells you which record to open. Read the issued certificate to determine the actual scope and validity.

sections.heading: What to check before closing, binding coverage or signing a lease

items: Match the certificate’s building ID and address to the building in the deal file. On a large campus or a shared lot, confirm which structure the address refers to.
Find the floor or area in the issued records. Compare the authorized use and any limits shown with the tenant operation, underwriting submission or renovation plan.

Record the issue date, certificate type and the expiry or conditions printed on the document. For temporary authority, request the latest applicable issuance and check it against the scheduled closing, policy or move-in date.
Save the certificate, floor records, link, and date you reviewed them. Record unresolved building or floor matches and ask the owner or DOB to resolve them.

blocks.text: For a building built before 1938, DOB advises checking whether later alterations changed the use, egress or occupancy. Ask the borough office about a Letter of No Objection when the building is exempt and you need proof of legal use. When minor work only required a Letter of Completion, keep that letter with the permit history and check the applicable occupancy evidence separately.

For a portfolio review, use Invariant Earth to match the submitted address to a mapped building and retain that source and date. Then retrieve the applicable agency record for the building and space. Use the same identity check when linking permits, hazard maps and occupancy documents.

faqs.question: Can I look up a NYC certificate of occupancy online by address?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use BIS for requests filed before March 1, 2021, and DOB NOW for requests filed on or after that date. In DOB NOW, you can also search by building identification number (BIN). Open the certificate and match its floor use records to the space.

faqs.question: Does a building permit show that I can occupy a space?
faqs.answer: Start with the issued certificate and the floor use records that apply to the space and planned use. A construction permit authorizes the listed work. An occupancy certificate records the legally permitted use or type of occupancy.

faqs.question: Where can I check when a temporary certificate of occupancy expires?
faqs.answer: Read the expiration date on the issued certificate. NYC DOB says temporary certificates typically expire 90 days after issuance. A renewal can have a different date than the earlier certificate in your file.

faqs.question: What if I cannot find a certificate for an older NYC building?
faqs.answer: Check both city systems and verify the building identification number. A qualifying pre-1938 building can be exempt. When you need proof of legal use for an exempt building, ask the appropriate DOB borough office about a Letter of No Objection.

title: How Many Data Centers Are in Loudoun County, Virginia?
description: Loudoun counted 245 data center buildings built or under construction on September 1, 2026. Compare the district and pipeline totals with the county map.
coverAlt: Loudoun County reports 245 data center buildings built or under construction, 114 approved or in administrative review, and 54 in legislative review as of September 1, 2026.
coverCaption: Countywide estimates from Loudoun County’s September 1, 2026 district table. The middle group combines three development stages.
intro: Loudoun County counted 245 data center buildings built or under construction as of September 1, 2026, covering about 58.3 million square feet. That count includes buildings with issued permits that are still under construction. The county reported another 114 buildings in its approved or administrative group and 54 in legislative review. For a particular address, use the county map to find the parent project and then check the building or site-plan record.
takeaways: The county’s built or under-construction count rose from 233 in March to 245 in September 2026.
Sterling and Broad Run together accounted for 173 of the 245 buildings in the September category.
The countywide table and the dashboard’s building point layer return different totals. Cite the one that answers your question.

blocks.text: The middle group combines 47 buildings with approved or conditionally approved site plans and no building permit, 62 buildings with site plans under administrative review, and five buildings on projects that received legislative approval but had yet to apply for a site plan. The county uses the site plan when one exists to avoid counting the same buildings again under legislative approval.

The county’s March 1 fact sheet counted 233 buildings in the built or under-construction group. The September table counted 245, a net increase of 12 in that category. To identify which projects moved forward, check individual permits and approvals. The two snapshots do not identify 12 completed facilities.

sections.heading: Where are the data center buildings?

blocks.text: Sterling had the largest September count in the built or under-construction group, with 105 buildings. Broad Run followed with 68. Together they accounted for about 71% of that countywide total. Use the election district labels for this comparison. The county also groups facilities by parcel, parent project and campus in the map.

sections.heading: Why does the map return a different count?

blocks.text: We queried the point layer named in the official dashboard and grouped it by the county’s built-status field. On November 24 the query returned 199 points labeled built and 50 labeled under construction. That is 249 point records, four more than the published countywide count. The point layer returned about 54.8 million square feet across the 247 records with an area value, compared with about 58.3 million in the county’s published table.

Five points share one building permit number, and two have no permit number. A permit number can link multiple points, so counting unique permit numbers gives a different answer again. The published district table does not include a row-by-row key that proves how to match these points to its 245 buildings. Cite the dated county table for a countywide count and use the GIS layer to locate specific records.

The county’s guide describes the dashboard as a March and September snapshot. Its built and under-construction labels come from permit milestones. For example, the guide classifies an issued building permit without a final occupancy permit as under construction. To establish when a tenant moved in or a facility took load, look for evidence of that event separately.

sections.heading: How to check a proposed or existing data center near an address

items: Open the county dashboard, search for the address, and switch on the parent project and building layers. The project boundary can include more than one parcel and building.
Open the project or building popup. Copy the project number, parcel ID and permit number where available. Keep the identifier for the specific building you are checking.
Use LandMARC to find the active site plan, building permit, and any final permit or occupancy record. For a proposal in legislative review, check the agenda and the recorded vote.

faqs.answer: The county’s September 1, 2026 district table reports 245 data center buildings built or under construction, covering about 58.3 million square feet. The number combines two permit-based stages.

faqs.question: How many data centers are operating in Loudoun County?
faqs.answer: The county’s published 245 combines built buildings with buildings under construction. Its map uses permit milestones for the built label. Use operator or facility records to establish operational status for a specific building.

faqs.question: How many data centers are planned in Loudoun County?
faqs.answer: The September 1 table reports 114 prospective buildings in the approved or administrative group and 54 in legislative review. Those figures count buildings in plans and applications, which can change during review.

faqs.question: Where can I look up a data center near my address in Loudoun?
faqs.answer: Search the county’s data center dashboard by address. Open the parent project or building popup for the parcel, project, and permit numbers, then use LandMARC for the latest applicable records.

title: Truck Routing APIs and NYC Truck Route Restrictions
description: Compare truck routing APIs and verify posted bridge and tunnel restrictions. Replay how two public NYC GIS feeds handle the October 2026 truck route changes.
coverAlt: Two routes changed October 4, 2026. NYC removed a Greenpoint Avenue block from the local network and added a section of 44th Drive.
coverCaption: Selected New York City truck route changes. The street centerlines illustrate only the compared stretches.
intro: Start with the truck and its trip. Measure the loaded height, width and length, record axle count and weights, and use the actual loading gate. A truck routing API can check a candidate route against its map. In New York City, compare the route with current City rules and the facility operator’s restrictions. We found two corridors where the adopted October 4, 2026 rule and the public GIS records still disagreed when queried on November 24.
takeaways: Keep the effective date of the rule and the source feed’s update date as separate fields.
Match by segment ID and the two cross streets. A rule change may cover only part of a named road.
Check the vehicle class and posted conditions for each crossing, even when the height fits the published limit.

sections.heading: Which truck routing API or data source should you use?

columns: What to check in a trial
rows: HERE Routing API v8
Calculate routes with truck mode and explicit height, dimensions, and weight values.
Confirm vehicle parameters are populated and check the restriction coverage and notices.
Trimble Maps
Use a truck profile with specified vehicle dimensions, weight and axles to calculate a route.
Check which profile values your request overrides and what warnings apply at the destination.
NYC DOT and City Planning
Match a segment to a local or through route and read the enacted change for specified cross streets.
Check the route date, effective rule, and any restriction that applies to the actual truck.
Road, bridge or tunnel operator
Verify crossing-specific access, size restrictions, weight limits, and temporary closures.
Confirm the exact deck, tube, approach, traffic direction, and travel time.

blocks.text: For warehouse and fleet site selection, use Invariant Earth to locate the property and screen nearby transport infrastructure. Test an actual route with a truck router, then verify any constraints against the agency and facility operator. Repeat the check for each entrance and vehicle profile.

sections.heading: Two NYC truck route changes you can replay

blocks.text: The city adopted changes to its truck route network effective October 4, 2026. We matched selected corridors by LION segment ID and checked both NYC DOT’s public truck route features and City Planning’s LION street centerlines. The DOT feature table reported a March 2 update. The LION endpoint reported a November 23 data edit. Both still disagreed with the adopted rule for these two examples.

rows: Greenpoint Avenue, West Street to Franklin Street, Brooklyn
Removed from the designated local network.
DOT still labeled segment 0035007 Local. City Planning’s LION layer returned code 2, meaning Local.
44th Drive, Vernon Boulevard to Thomson Avenue, Queens
Added to the designated local network.
DOT returned zero rows for the ten matched IDs. The ten centerline segments existed in LION with a blank truck-route code.

blocks.text: The 44th Drive counts use unique segment IDs. The LION response repeats two of those IDs across source rows. Keep the original blank values, the dates, and the result from the adopted rule. An update timestamp tells you when a dataset changed. It cannot tell you whether a specific rule change made it into the data.

blocks.label: Download both corridor checks with IDs and source queries

sections.heading: How to check truck clearance and crossing restrictions

blocks.text: At the George Washington Bridge, the Port Authority’s guide lists a 13-foot-6-inch height limit on both levels. Its separate restriction directs trucks to the upper level. At the Holland Tunnel, the operator excludes combination vehicles and vehicles with four or more axles. A vehicle can fit the published dimensions and still be excluded by a class rule.

Record traffic direction, turn restrictions, posted height, gross and axle limits, and any construction or time-of-day rules. Verify approach roads and the exact deck or tube with the operator. The Federal Highway Administration directs users to other sources for route clearance instead of relying on National Bridge Inventory values.

New York City requires through routes when the trip has neither an origin nor a destination in the borough. For a delivery on a street outside the designated network, the City explains how to use the closest appropriate network intersection and the direct local access path. Review the adopted rule and current signs for the intended trip.

sections.heading: How to test a truck routing feed before rollout

items: Save the vehicle profile and a specific entrance coordinate. Keep the route output and the notices returned with it.
Test one newly added street stretch and one removed stretch. Record the affected segment IDs and the date the rule took effect.
Test a crossing where the access rule depends on a bridge level or vehicle class. Confirm the route output names the correct level or flags the limitation.
Recheck the operator’s notices for a departure. When the feed and road authority disagree, record the conflict and have dispatch verify the proposed path before sending the vehicle.

faqs.question: Where can I find the current NYC truck route map?
faqs.answer: Start with NYC DOT’s truck routing page and the change map effective October 4, 2026. Check the adopted rule for exact cross streets, route type and vehicle applicability. Keep the publication dates when comparing older maps or downloaded GIS layers.

faqs.question: Can a truck routing API account for low bridges and weight limits?
faqs.answer: Truck routing tools such as HERE and Trimble Maps have vehicle-aware options. Supply the truck’s dimensions, axle count and weights, check which restrictions the service covers, and verify the specific crossing and approach with the operator.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a local and a through truck route in NYC?
faqs.answer: The city requires through truck routes for trips with neither an origin nor a destination in the borough. Local truck routes serve trips with a borough stop such as a delivery or pickup. Check the adopted rule for the exact streets and permitted local access.

faqs.question: Can a truck use the lower level of the George Washington Bridge?
faqs.answer: The Port Authority directs trucks to the upper level. Check its current size, weight and approach restrictions for the specific vehicle and trip.

title: Commercial Property Replacement Cost by Address
description: Look up commercial building replacement cost by address. Compare modeled values with city records, and see what a documented Florida rebuild tells an underwriter.
coverAlt: Comparison of four amounts for 32 Old Slip. The federal model totals $331.97 million full reconstruction and $276.05 million depreciated. The city reports $283.52 million in tax market value and $127.58 million actual assessed value.
coverCaption: 32 Old Slip, Manhattan. Invariant summed seven 2026 National Structure Inventory records within one NYC footprint and matched the lot to its FY2027 final tax roll. The federal model uses August 2025 prices.
intro: Start with the building you intend to insure, then check which kind of value the source returns. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers publishes two modeled costs for structures in its 2026 National Structure Inventory. A city assessment measures the property for taxation. A carrier uses its accepted reconstruction valuation and policy terms to determine coverage. At 32 Old Slip in Manhattan, those public sources put four different figures beside the same street address.
takeaways: Use the 2026 National Structure Inventory for an initial comparison of full and depreciated reconstruction costs. Both estimates use approximately August 2025 prices.

Match the federal points to the intended building. At 32 Old Slip, seven occupancy records share one location and footprint ID. Keeping only the largest row would omit about $28.8 million from the published model’s full replacement total.

Check the estimator’s floor area, occupancy, construction and valuation date before relying on it. For underwriting, resolve discrepancies against the insured schedule, building records and the carrier’s accepted estimate.
Use an actual rebuild to check which costs the estimate covers. Verify insurance limits and valuation terms in the policy documents.

sections.heading: Which value are you looking for?

rows: Full modeled replacement cost
Estimated cost to reconstruct a comparable new structure. The NSI model excludes land.
Use fullrep in the 2026 NSI for an initial comparison.
Depreciated modeled replacement cost
The NSI structure estimate after its depreciation adjustment.
Use val_struct for that model’s depreciated value.
Tax market value and actual assessment
The local authority’s property valuation and the amount assigned under its assessment rules. In NYC, Class 4 market value is based on income potential and expenses.
Use the final assessment roll and preserve the tax year and lot ID.
Insurance replacement cost
An estimate to replace covered property with property of comparable kind and quality. Coverage depends on the policy’s scope and limits.
Confirm the building and scope with the insurer’s accepted estimator or valuation.

blocks.text: Start with the valuation date and what the number includes. A policy’s treatment of actual cash value follows its terms and applicable rules. Keep that policy measure separate from the depreciated figure in the federal model.

sections.heading: What the records show for 32 Old Slip

blocks.text: NYC Geosearch identifies the address as building 1000867 on tax lot 1000350001. The final tax roll calls the lot 77 Front Street. The city’s footprint query returns one polygon for the building ID. Both the city’s address point and the seven selected federal records fall inside it. Eight other federal records in the surrounding query fall outside the footprint.

rows: NSI full model, sum of fullrep

blocks.text: The largest NSI row, professional and technical services, accounts for $303.17 million of the full modeled total. Six other rows at the same point account for the remaining $28.81 million. The Corps uses shared footprint IDs for stacked occupancy records. Preserve the rows during review and use the footprint ID to count the modeled building once.

The seven inventory rows total 1,256,816 square feet. PLUTO 26v3 reports 973,587 square feet of building area on this one-building tax lot. That is a 29% difference relative to PLUTO. The public records do not establish which area definition applies to a given policy. Ask for the insured floor area, occupancy split and recent renovations before estimating reconstruction cost.

sections.heading: Can a construction contract establish replacement cost for insurance?

blocks.text: A rebuild contract establishes the price for a defined scope at a given date. For insurance, use that scope to check the carrier’s reconstruction estimate. At 5171 Sanibel Captiva Road in Florida, the district rebuilt Fire Station 172 after Hurricane Ian. Its signed resolutions and audited financial statements give underwriters several different records to reconcile at one address.

rows: Contract authorization, March 13, 2024
$7,439,017.49 for the construction contract, with up to $500,000 separately authorized for contingencies.
Keep the authorization and contingency ceiling separate. Request the executed scope and change orders.
Construction spending at September 30, 2025
$8,249,324 spent on construction. The audit separately estimated total construction costs at approximately $8.5 million.
Record the spending cutoff and keep the estimate marked as provisional. Request a cost breakdown before comparing the amounts.
Flood insurance authorization, December 10, 2025
The board authorized the chief to obtain flood insurance. The resolution records a quoted annual premium of $11,500.
Log the quote and authorization as separate records. Verify the issued policy, building limit, deductible and dates.
Permanent certificate of occupancy, February 13, 2026
The district reported substantial completion in November 2025 and receipt of the permanent certificate in February 2026.
Use both milestones to date the building record and ask for the final closeout costs separately.

blocks.text: To use this kind of evidence in a renewal, match the building on the statement of values to the project address and scope. Ask which costs belong to the insured building and which cover site work, contents, temporary operations or design. Then use the insurer’s accepted estimate and check the issued policy’s limits and treatment of debris removal and code upgrades. The records cited here leave final audited project cost and bound flood terms unconfirmed.
