faqs.question: Can I look up commercial building replacement cost by address?
faqs.answer: Use an address match to locate the intended footprint, then query the 2026 NSI for a public screening estimate. For an underwriting valuation, verify the building attributes and use the estimator or appraisal process accepted by the carrier.

faqs.question: What is the difference between fullrep and val_struct in the 2026 NSI?
faqs.answer: Fullrep is the modeled cost to build a comparable new structure. Val_struct is the modeled structural value after depreciation. The published values use approximately August 2025 prices.

faqs.question: How do I handle multiple NSI rows at the same building?
faqs.answer: Check the shared footprint identifier and occupancy codes. The Corps sometimes models several uses as separate records at one footprint. Count the footprint once for building counts and preserve the individual occupancy records when reviewing the model’s total.

faqs.question: Can tax assessed value be used as building replacement cost?
faqs.answer: Use the assessment for the tax decision it describes. For reconstruction, verify the insured building and get a current estimate using the applicable construction costs and coverage scope. For example, NYC’s Class 4 assessment applies a tax ratio to a market value based on income potential and expenses.

faqs.question: Can a construction contract or permit value establish a building insurance limit?
faqs.answer: Use its dated scope to check a reconstruction estimate. The contract or permit covers the work described in the record. Confirm the carrier’s valuation and the issued policy’s building limit, endorsements and deductible separately.

title: How to Map Flood Exposure Across a Property Portfolio
description: Download an Excel workbook to group commercial building and contents values by FEMA flood zone. Use the county example to review incomplete matches and reconcile totals.
coverAlt: Aerial map of downtown Centerville with the two matched building outlines and the Census street-range points plotted separately.
coverCaption: The street-range points miss the two building outlines. USDA NAIP 2023 imagery served by the Federal Geospatial Platform. Building outlines from FEMA and Oak Ridge National Laboratory.
intro: To screen a property portfolio for flood exposure, match each statement-of-values row to its building, intersect the building outline with the effective flood map, and sum values by zone and coverage type. Keep unmatched values in the same report. The Excel workbook below includes a blank input sheet and the Appanoose County example. Of the 22 coverage lines in the example, $8,445,100 matched to buildings in unshaded Zone X and $1,604,700 still needed a building match.
takeaways: Match the insured building before assigning a flood zone. One street address can cover a campus with several individually scheduled structures.
Sum building and contents values separately. Carry unresolved values in the denominator so the report shows how much of the schedule was classified.
Keep the schedule term, building imagery date, FEMA panel effective date and date of retrieval. Each describes a different part of the evidence.

guideActions.label: Check FEMA exposure for a property

sections.heading: How do you calculate flood exposure from a statement of values?

blocks.text: A statement of values, or SOV, records amounts submitted for the locations and property interests in a placement. Start with the version in effect for the review. Save the original location and building IDs, the coverage subject, the basis of valuation and currency. An insurer may also track business interruption separately. Decide which of those values your concentration report includes before you make comparisons.

columns: What to keep in the exposure file
rows: Reconcile the schedule
Retain one source row per building and coverage subject. Keep the row key and schedule term. Identify subtotals, repeated policy limits and overlapping placements before adding values.
Match the structure
Verify the address, locality and footprint using an authoritative record. For same-address campuses, request a site plan or a schedule that identifies the individual structures.
Intersect the effective map
Record all zones that intersect the footprint, including the Zone X subtype. Save the panel, applicable map revisions and date checked.
Group the values
Sum the declared amounts by coverage type and zone-review status. Put mixed-zone buildings in a separate review group where a single classification would hide a boundary crossing.

sections.heading: Download the property portfolio flood workbook

blocks.text: Paste up to 200 coverage lines into Your portfolio. Use one schedule period and USD values. Enter the building ID, coverage type, valuation basis, and the FEMA panel and effective date where you have a verified footprint. The workbook flags duplicate row IDs, incomplete inputs and buildings that still need a match. Enter a zone label to see the mapped values for that zone.

blocks.label: Download the property portfolio flood exposure workbook

blocks.text: On the County example tab, four coverage lines from two buildings map to unshaded Zone X. Another 18 lines stay in the review totals. The four mapped lines account for 84.0% of the $10,049,800 entered value. The workbook retains separate totals for building and contents values and shows the share mapped across the whole sample. Correct duplicate rows and input errors before sharing totals.

blocks.text: The January 18, 2021 county board packet lists submitted values for the 2021 policy term. We selected 22 building and contents lines across five address groups. The November 25, 2026 lookup matched the Courthouse and the Human Services address to two USA Structures outlines in unshaded Zone X. Both footprints are covered by panel 19007C0251C, effective February 16, 2018. The outlines come from September 2025 imagery.

That is $1,604,700, or about 16% of the $10,049,800 sample. The totals include the valuation bases printed on the schedule. The example uses selected printed rows. The 2021 packet also carries a handwritten fuel-tank entry for $124,155 at the road yard, outside the printed table. Keep that line in the schedule review with its source page and ask for the final version before including it in a carrier exposure report.

sections.heading: Why can the address point give the wrong answer?

blocks.text: The Census range match lies about 50 metres from the courthouse outline and 23 metres from the Human Services outline. The points and footprints return the same zone in downtown Centerville. At the road yard and park, a Zone X result at a range point still leaves the individual buildings unresolved.

A shared address can also produce misleading joins even when the point looks precise. An Ecopia case study describes how an insurer moved from manual address review to building matches for accumulation work. In your trial, send a shared-address campus and an unmatched address. Ask for the matched building ID, the original geometry, the evidence date and the full dollar amount the provider could not assign.

Use Invariant Earth to look up candidate building and parcel records, then compare them with your schedule. The FEMA workflow returns the point result and parcel overlap. When the decision applies to a specific structure, check its footprint against the flood layer and preserve the result separately.

sections.heading: What should you send to underwriting or reinsurance?

blocks.text: Send the building-level ledger and a summary with the mapped and unresolved dollar values. Include the map vintage, the grouping rule, and the reason each unresolved building needs review. Keep declared exposure values separate from deductibles, limits, sublimits and modeled losses. A zone screen can show where values concentrate. Pricing or catastrophe modeling uses additional information about flood depth, vulnerability and the terms of the insurance.

faqs.question: Can I sum property values by FEMA flood zone using ZIP codes?
faqs.answer: Use ZIP codes for a regional subtotal. To classify a building by FEMA zone, verify its location and overlay the effective hazard map on the building footprint. Retain unresolved values separately.

faqs.question: How should I report a building that intersects more than one flood zone?
faqs.answer: Record each intersecting zone and flag the building for review. Use an explicit grouping rule for the summary. A percentage of footprint area does not determine which share of the declared value would be lost in a flood.

faqs.question: Is the scheduled value in a flood zone the expected insured loss?
faqs.answer: It is the amount recorded on the schedule for the structure or contents. An insured-loss estimate also needs the event, the property’s vulnerability and the applicable policy terms.

title: How to Check Power Outage History by Address
description: Find past outages for a commercial address, compare utility reliability with and without major events, and download ten years of Southern California Edison data.
coverAlt: Southern California Edison’s average unplanned interruption duration reached 545.01 minutes per customer in 2025 with major event days included and 116.37 minutes with those days excluded.
coverCaption: Southern California Edison’s systemwide unplanned interruptions from 2016 to 2025, with and without major event days. Source is Table 3 of its 2025 Annual Electric Reliability Report.
intro: To check past power outages at a commercial address, identify the serving electric utility and the exact service point. Ask the owner for its outage and equipment logs, then request the history the utility can release for that service point. Pull utility or district reliability data for context. In 2025, Southern California Edison reported 545.01 minutes of unplanned interruptions per customer with major events included and 116.37 minutes with those days excluded. Both are system averages.
takeaways: Use the address to find candidate utilities. Confirm the utility and each service point from the account or service documents.
Keep routine interruptions, major event days, planned work and preventive wildfire shutoffs identifiable in the data.
Use event durations and actual equipment behavior to assess a building’s operating exposure and backup requirements.

sections.heading: Find the utility and service point

blocks.text: Start with the property’s service address and ask for a recent electricity bill or service agreement. Record the utility responsible for the wires and the utility’s service point or premise identifier for each building or meter that serves critical equipment. A campus can contain several separately served buildings. For a vacant parcel, ask the utility which service area and proposed connection would apply.

At a U.S. coordinate, Invariant Earth’s electric_utility_service_territory field can surface a candidate retail provider. Some underlying boundaries follow counties. Where multiple service territories overlap, the API lists the candidates in its field notes. Resolve the serving utility from property or utility records before attaching a reliability series.

blocks.label: Check the site

items.label: Check the electric utility service territory field

sections.heading: Where can you find historical power outages?

rows: Service records and facility logs
An interruption tied to the meter, building or equipment in the record.
Match the account, meter and time zone. Ask the owner to authorize access where the utility requires it.
EIA Form 861 and state reliability reports
Annual frequency and duration for a utility, state or reported district.
Match the year, method, scope and whether major event days are included.
Current utility outage map
An incident the utility is currently reporting and any posted restoration estimate.
Save the observation time. For past interruptions, use the utility’s or facility’s retained records.
CPUC Public Safety Power Shutoff dashboard

Record the event dates and reporting scope. Check separately for unplanned failures and planned maintenance.
DOE Form 417 incident summaries
Reported electric emergency events and other disturbances that meet federal reporting criteria.
Use the listed event scope to investigate regional effects. Confirm the service point separately.

blocks.text: Keep the results from each source separately. In a due diligence file, distinguish a documented period with zero interruptions from a period for which you received no service records.

sections.heading: What changed when SCE included major outage days?

blocks.text: SAIDI measures the total minutes of sustained interruptions per customer on average over a year. SAIFI counts sustained interruptions per customer. California’s reporting treats an interruption lasting more than five minutes as sustained. CAIDI measures the average duration of a sustained interruption. SCE also reports MAIFI, the average count of momentary interruptions.

blocks.text: SCE tallied 21 major event days in 2025. Those days account for 428.64 minutes, about 78.6% of the reported unplanned system total. The 116.37-minute figure helps describe the system outside major event days. For refrigeration, industrial operations, or a data center, review severe events as well, especially the longest interruption the service point actually experienced. SCE publishes district figures separately and notes boundary changes that affect some historical comparisons.

sections.heading: What outage records should you request for a lease or purchase?

blocks.text: Specify the dates and service points you want reviewed. Ask the utility what it can provide and how it defines a sustained event. Request the site operator’s building management, automatic transfer switch, and generator or UPS event logs alongside any utility records. For each event, record when utility service failed, when it returned, and when site equipment recovered. Keep the original timestamps and time zone.

items: Classify utility outages, planned maintenance, wildfire shutoffs, and failures of equipment inside the facility. Confirm differences in timing with the operator.
Track voltage sags and brief interruptions when equipment resets or process losses matter. Ask what the meters or power-quality equipment were configured to record.
For two services, request written utility evidence about their independence and shared dependencies. Compare it with the one-line diagram and the transfer and load-test records.
Before valuing a lease or underwriting a site, review which equipment must stay online, how long it can run on backup, and who owns the remaining actions.

faqs.question: Can I look up every past power outage at an address online?
faqs.answer: The serving utility can tell you what history it will release for a service point. The owner or occupant may have more detail in operating records. Public outage maps and annual reliability reports cover different scopes. California’s public shutoff dashboard has a separate address lookup for preventive wildfire shutoffs.

faqs.question: Can I use SAIDI to size a generator or estimate building downtime?
faqs.answer: Use the system average to compare published reliability. For a building, examine the actual interruption durations, the equipment that needs power, transfer and recovery times, and the backup system’s tested runtime under load.

faqs.question: What is a major event day in a utility reliability report?
faqs.answer: Under the IEEE method, a major event day exceeds a threshold calculated from earlier daily outage data. Check the reporting method before comparing utility figures. SCE reported 21 such days in 2025 and gives a separate annual series with those days excluded.

title: Cold Storage Warehouse Capacity by State
description: Compare USDA cold storage capacity by state, including cooler and freezer space. Download the data and check what warehouse operators can offer for your dates.
coverAlt: Georgia, Washington and Wisconsin each had 240 to 255 million cubic feet of usable refrigerated space in the 2025 USDA survey. Wisconsin reported 90.3 million cubic feet of cooler space and Washington reported 12.8 million.
coverCaption: Usable volume by temperature band on October 1, 2025. Source is the USDA National Agricultural Statistics Service, Capacity of Refrigerated Warehouses, pages 8 and 9.
intro: To compare cold storage markets, start with USDA’s usable cooler and freezer volumes, then narrow the search to the routes and facilities that fit your product. On October 1, 2025, Wisconsin and Washington each had about 240 million cubic feet of usable refrigerated space in USDA’s survey. Wisconsin had about seven times as much usable cooler space. To book space or lease a building, confirm the temperature range, available pallet positions and start date with the operator or landlord.
takeaways: Compare usable volume by temperature band. States with similar refrigerated totals can have very different mixes of cooler and freezer space.
Public storage in the USDA survey means storage offered to others for a fee. Ask operators what they can commit for your product and dates.
Confirm product temperature, throughput, freight access and refrigeration power at the specific facility.

sections.heading: How much cooler and freezer space does each state have?

blocks.text: USDA’s latest biennial survey covered October 1, 2025 and was released February 9, 2026. It reported 3.99 billion gross cubic feet of refrigerated storage and 3.25 billion usable cubic feet in the U.S. About 79% of usable volume was freezer space. Use the freezer and cooler tables to compare the capacity that fits your shipment.

blocks.text: These are the five states with the most gross capacity in the survey. Their order changes when you look at cooler space. Wisconsin’s 90.306 million usable cooler cubic feet is 7.08 times Washington’s 12.754 million. Washington reports more usable freezer space than Wisconsin. USDA publishes Washington’s cooler total and withholds the split between public and private or semiprivate operators.

Download the state records, source checksums and comparison calculation

sections.heading: How should you use the USDA cold storage data?

blocks.text: Gross volume covers the refrigerated envelope. Usable volume deducts space for features such as aisles and refrigeration equipment. USDA uses 0°F to distinguish freezer from cooler space. The cooler category extends up to 50°F. Ask a facility for the actual setpoint range, allowable excursion, and how it measures temperature for your product.

The survey focuses on qualifying facilities that normally hold food for at least 30 days. USDA estimates values for some nonrespondents and says its published figures should be treated as minimums. The download retains the figures as published, including rounded totals, zero values and withheld cells. Comparing two survey years shows changes in the published inventory. Use permits, openings and closures to establish why a market changed.

Use USDA’s monthly Cold Storage report to track commodity stocks and its refrigerated truck datasets to compare reported produce flows, lane rates and seasonal truck availability. The stocks and warehouse surveys measure different things. Check the commodity, geography and unit before comparing them. Ask brokers or operators for building vacancy, available positions and written rates.

sections.heading: Where can you find cold storage near the Port of Savannah?

blocks.text: Start with the exact terminal and the dates you need service. The records below show three Savannah-area options and the services their operators list. Use those pages to identify candidates and request a quote for your product, handling requirements and start date.

Ask for the rate sheet and how it charges for storage, receiving, outbound handling and temperature or inspection services. For a lease of dedicated space, verify which racks, refrigeration equipment and docks are included.

sections.heading: What should you verify before leasing or building cold storage?

items: Specify the product, target temperature, pallet type, peak inventory, inbound and outbound volume, and any blast freezing requirement. Ask for usable positions and throughput under that operating plan.

Ask the refrigeration designer for the peak expected electric demand and operating profile. Confirm the tariff, metering point, committed utility service and upgrade dates. Check backup load, runtime and outage logs.
Verify trailer access, dock height, refrigerated staging and truck turning on a site visit. Map the loading gate and the routes you can use with the actual vehicle and trailer.
Obtain the site’s temperature monitoring, sanitation and shipment handling procedures for your product. Confirm who maintains the equipment and who responds to temperature excursions.

faqs.question: Which states have the most cold storage capacity?
faqs.answer: California, Georgia, Washington, Wisconsin and Texas were the five largest states by gross refrigerated warehouse volume in USDA’s October 2025 survey. Compare usable cooler or freezer volume when your search requires a particular temperature band.

faqs.question: What is public cold storage?
faqs.answer: USDA classifies warehouses that store food for others at specified rates as public refrigerated storage. Operators may sell pallet storage and handling services. Ask them for a quote for the required temperature, pallet positions and dates.

faqs.question: Can I use cubic feet to calculate how many pallets I can store?
faqs.answer: Ask for the rack schedule and available positions that fit your pallet size, height and weight. The count also depends on clear height, aisles, clearances and the storage layout. The USDA volume helps you compare markets before you check individual facilities.

title: LightBox Alternatives for Environmental Site Screening
description: Compare LightBox, Invariant Earth, Mireye and ERIS for environmental due diligence. Use an EPA Superfund example to test site geometry and cleanup history.
coverAlt: Map of EPA’s Gowanus Canal Superfund footprint and an enlarged view showing the agency’s published site coordinate 21.7 meters outside the nearest edge.
coverCaption: Invariant mapped the coordinate and footprint from EPA’s NEPAssist Superfund layer. The measured gap is 21.7 meters.
intro: Invariant Earth is a LightBox alternative for teams that want to screen U.S. sites for nearby Superfund and brownfield records alongside parcel, zoning, wetland and utility data. When an environmental professional needs historical records for a Phase I assessment, compare report packages such as LightBox EDR and ERIS. To test any screening API, start with one public case where the original evidence is easy to check. At the Gowanus Canal, EPA’s published coordinate sits 21.7 meters outside the agency’s mapped Superfund footprint, and the cleanup history has several distinct dates.
takeaways: The LightBox EPA Sites API, LightBox EDR packages and ERIS report packages serve different steps in environmental diligence.
Invariant Earth documents nearest-site distance and site counts for Superfund and brownfields. Use them to prioritize parcels for review.
For EPA site NYN000206222, test whether the provider identifies the source geometry, preserves the EPA ID and distinguishes the 2010 listing, 2013 remedy decision and 2025 review.

sections.heading: Which LightBox alternative fits your workflow?

blocks.text: Start with the decision your team needs to make. A site selector can use a screening API to flag a shortlist for follow-up. A lender or acquirer commissioning a Phase I needs a qualified environmental professional, who may order historical sources and regulatory records. Invariant makes Invariant Earth. This comparison uses public product documentation reviewed November 25, 2026. The Gowanus calculation uses EPA data directly.

columns: What to check in a trial
rows: Invariant Earth
Screen a point or parcel alongside physical site data. The public field catalogs list nearest Superfund and brownfield distances and counts within 8 km.
Check coverage and the response’s source and vintage. Use the returned distance as a flag, then open the original EPA footprint and case records.
LightBox EPA Sites API
Retrieve Superfund and brownfield records by EPA ID, address or LightBox property identifiers. The API also documents buffered geometry queries and map tiles.
Use the same EPA ID for the address and geometry queries. Inspect the geometry type and confirm the source and vintage of each return.
Mireye
Screen a point using documented Superfund and brownfield distance and count fields within 8 km.
Check the input coordinate and source. Ask how the response distinguishes an empty search from unavailable coverage.
Transect
Development feasibility reports that bring together buildable area, water features, species constraints and permitting requirements.
Upload the same tract and buffer. Ask which polygons came from a published layer, which reflect proprietary modeling, and which findings need field verification.
LightBox EDR
Order environmental data packages designed for transaction screens and Phase I workflows, depending on the package.
Review the included historical sources and coverage for the subject property with your environmental professional.
ERIS report packages
Order a regulatory database report with historical material such as aerial photographs, fire insurance maps or directories, depending on the package.
Check which sources, years and search areas the package covers. Ask how gaps are documented.

sections.heading: A Superfund point and footprint can disagree

blocks.text: EPA’s NEPAssist Superfund layer returned one polygon for Gowanus Canal, EPA ID NYN000206222, with the registry status Final NPL. The same feature includes latitude and longitude attributes. We converted those attributes into a point and projected both geometries to UTM zone 18N. The shortest distance from the coordinate to the polygon was 21.7 meters. A point can therefore identify a site and still fall outside its mapped footprint.

EPA describes the polygon as its current understanding of the site’s footprint. Coverage can be incomplete, and outlines can change as investigation and cleanup progress. The download lets you replay that geometry calculation. To assess a particular parcel, verify its boundary and intersect it with the appropriate dated layer. Refer the site and supporting documents for environmental review before relying on the result for a transaction.

blocks.label: Download the EPA footprint, site coordinate and dated cleanup records

sections.heading: Which cleanup date belongs in the deal file?

blocks.text: Keep the site ID and the event scope on every record. EPA’s public schedule indexes the 2025 five-year review under its sitewide entry. The report itself describes the work it reviewed under Operable Unit 01, the cleanup component covering work in the canal, two retention tanks and part of an upland former gas plant. Preserve both scope labels when you summarize the case.

sections.heading: How to run an environmental screening API trial

blocks.text: Use a small batch of known addresses or parcel IDs. For each return, save the address or parcel match and the geometry used for the distance calculation. Decide in advance whether your next step needs a count, a named site record with an EPA ID, or a polygon. With Invariant Earth, start by requesting nearest_superfund_distance_m and superfund_sites_within_radius_count, then add the brownfield equivalents. Check the field’s source, vintage and status in the response. For a Gowanus comparison, query the EPA ID separately and compare the site geometry with the download.

Record what you could verify on the decision date and what needs a specialist or newer document. For example, a proximity flag can justify pulling the agency files, while an old cleanup entry may need the current review report. When the deal calls for a Phase I or All Appropriate Inquiries, involve an environmental professional and use the screen to organize the handoff.

faqs.question: What is a LightBox alternative for screening many parcels?
faqs.answer: Evaluate Invariant Earth when your team needs Superfund and brownfield screening fields alongside parcel, zoning or utility evidence. Run the trial on known parcels and check the parcel match, search radius, source date and missing-data behavior before scaling.

faqs.question: Can an environmental screening API replace a Phase I assessment?
faqs.answer: Use an API for screening and evidence collection. A Phase I assessment is performed by an environmental professional and draws on more than registry searches. EPA’s All Appropriate Inquiries guidance includes records review, interviews, visual inspection and a signed report.

faqs.question: Does a nearby Superfund record mean a property is contaminated?
faqs.answer: A nearby record is grounds to review the named site, source geometry and case documents. A registry distance alone cannot establish the condition of a particular property.

faqs.question: Why might two Superfund distances differ for the same address?
faqs.answer: One service may measure to a registry coordinate and another to a mapped footprint. They may also resolve the subject address to different positions. At Gowanus, the EPA layer’s own coordinate is 21.7 meters outside the mapped polygon.

title: Point-in-Time Property Data: How to Rebuild a Property File
description: Reconstruct building, parcel and recording records as of an earlier date. Download a 25 Water Street example with three cutoffs and the original source queries.
coverAlt: Three December 2025 cutoffs for 25 Water Street. Eligible occupancy issuances rise from six to seven, and selected recorder entries increase from eight to twelve.
coverCaption: NYC issued an occupancy renewal on December 3 and recorded four selected financing documents on December 9. Invariant reconstructed the cutoffs from records retrieved November 25, 2026.
intro: To reconstruct a property file as of an earlier date, match the parcel and building, then apply the date that belongs to each source. An occupancy certificate has an issuance date. A mortgage has a document date and a separate recording date. A later parcel edition belongs in a separate observation. At 25 Water Street in Manhattan, those distinctions change what goes into the same property file over nine days.
takeaways: Filter each record by the date that answers your question. Preserve the original event date, the source edition and when your team first captured the record.
At 25 Water Street, the latest eligible occupancy issuance changed on December 3, 2025. The four selected financing records were recorded on December 9.
To reproduce exactly what an analyst or data feed could see at the time, use an archived response or a dated capture log.

sections.heading: Match the building and parcel before comparing dates

blocks.text: NYC identifies 25 Water Street, 115 Broad Street and 4 New York Plaza as addresses for the same building. Use Manhattan borough-block-lot 1000050010 for the recorder and tax lot queries, and building identification number 1000007 with job M08013214 for the Department of Buildings query. Keep the source identifiers together in the file so the certificate series stays tied to the intended building.

Use Invariant Earth to confirm a present-day parcel match and capture the source and edition for future comparisons. For a past decision, look for the source edition or the record dated to that decision. A building job and a tax lot identify different things, so check the building identifier before carrying a certificate over to a whole parcel.

sections.heading: What changed between December 1, 5 and 10?

blocks.text: We retrieved the city records on November 25, 2026. For each 2025 cutoff, we kept DOB issuance rows through that calendar date and selected ACRIS instrument rows through their recording date. The occupancy series contains ten rows and the recorder sample contains 12 instruments chosen from a published mortgage-chain study. The counts below describe those queries.

rows: December 1, 2025
6 issuances. Latest eligible certificate ends in 0000006, September 11.
8 selected instruments. The four November 25 documents were still outside the recorded-date cutoff.
December 5, 2025
7 issuances. The December 3 renewal ends in 0000007 and reports 1,320 dwelling units.
8 selected instruments. The four documents still fall outside this cutoff.
December 10, 2025
7 issuances. The December 3 renewal remains the latest eligible row.
12 selected instruments. All four November 25 documents were recorded December 9.

blocks.text: The rent assignment references the agreement and repeats its $415 million indexed amount. Use the document references to connect them before calculating debt. The index preserves the amount on each document, and the signed instruments and subsequent records are needed to verify current obligations.

blocks.label: Download the three cutoffs, dated source rows and query fingerprints

blocks.text: Try a December 5 diligence cutoff. All 12 selected instruments pass a document-date filter. Only eight pass a recorded-date filter. The other four carry a November 25 document date and a December 9 recording date. Use the recorded date to reconstruct the recording history. Keep the document date for the instrument chronology and the retrieval date for the source audit.

blocks.label: Download the cutoff replay

blocks.text: Save the JSON and Python files in the same folder. The script runs offline and recomputes each cutoff from the dated source rows. It lists the instruments that would appear early under a document-date filter and shows when Invariant retrieved each source.

items.label: What point-in-time property data preserves

sections.heading: How to reconstruct a property record as of a date

blocks.text: Choose a calendar date and state what you want to recover. A permit or certificate review uses issuance evidence. A recorder search compares recording dates. A GIS overlay uses the archived parcel and map editions that applied on the date. Retain the original source records so another reviewer can recheck the cutoff.

Our later MapPLUTO 26v3 lookup returned 1,323 total units and 1,320 residential units. The December 3 DOB issuance reports 1,320 dwelling units. Save the tax lot counts as a separate 2026 observation and keep each measure labeled. The December exercise uses the dated issuance and recording rows.

items: Keep the event date and its field name, such as issued date or recording date.
Save the source edition and query plus the time you fetched the data and the first time your system observed it.
When you replay a past decision, use the captured response or report. If you work from a later extract, label it as a reconstruction and state which visibility and record versions you could verify.

sections.heading: How to test a point-in-time property data API

blocks.text: Ask for the same address and building IDs at all three cutoffs. A reproducible answer gives the cutoff rule, the source identifiers and the archived version or dated record used. Ask separately what the vendor refreshed and what changed at the county or city. Regrid documents ll_last_refresh as a county-wide processing date and ll_updated_at as a timestamp for changes to the row. Those fields are useful for tracking data releases and versioning.

With Invariant Earth, save parcel match type, source URL and dataset vintage with each observation. The API documents fetched_at as the time the source answered, which is retained when the value is served from cache. For an event before your first capture, use the archived public record where available and save its identifier with the result.

faqs.question: What is point-in-time property data?
faqs.answer: It is a view of property evidence tied to a specific date. Specify whether you are reconstructing events effective or recorded by that date, or reproducing the information an analyst could access then. A later extract can support the first question. For the second, retain an archived response or timestamped capture.

faqs.question: Should I use the mortgage date or recording date for a historical recorder search?
faqs.answer: Use the recording date for records recorded by a cutoff and keep the document date alongside it. In the 25 Water Street example, four instruments dated November 25, 2025 were recorded on December 9.

faqs.question: How do I check the parcel boundary from an earlier year?
faqs.answer: Ask for a dated boundary from the local archive and check whether the parcel number, predecessor or successor changed. Join through parcel identifiers and verified map changes before applying a hazard overlay or credit record.
